sources.title: Deccan Chronicle: Parliament clears Tribunals Reforms Bill, 2026

questions.question: Which U.S. legislation provides the legal basis for the 123 Agreement framework?
questions.explanation: Section 123 of the US Atomic Energy Act of 1954 is the basis for '123 Agreements'.

questions.question: Which nuclear activity has been at the centre of controversy surrounding the U.S.–Saudi agreement?
questions.explanation: The controversy is over Saudi uranium enrichment and the absence of a 'gold standard' no-enrichment pledge.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes the IAEA Additional Protocol?
options: It permits countries to export enriched uranium without safeguards
It provides the IAEA with expanded verification and inspection powers
It establishes the international nuclear fuel-price mechanism
It authorises the construction of nuclear reactors in developing countries

questions.question: The 2008 India-specific waiver granted by the Nuclear Suppliers Group primarily enabled India to:
options: Participate in international civil nuclear trade despite being outside the NPT
Obtain recognition as a nuclear-weapon state under the NPT
Exempt civilian facilities from IAEA safeguards
Acquire nuclear weapons technology from participating NSG countries

Integrating GIS-based planning with national digital platforms to map and track assets
Conducting periodic physical surveys of all infrastructure projects by external agencies
Delegating infrastructure planning entirely to specialised private institutions

sources.title: Viksit Bharat – G RAM G Act, 2025

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT one of the four priority thematic areas of the scheme?

Selecting India's official contingent for international multi-sport competitions
Determining the sports and events included in international multi-sport competitions

Restrict agricultural imports exceeding domestic quotas
Regulate foreign subsidies received by exporting companies
questions.explanation: The EU's CBAM puts a price on the carbon embedded in carbon-intensive imports.

questions.question: With reference to the European Union mentioned in the passage, which institution generally negotiates international trade agreements on behalf of the EU?
questions.explanation: The European Commission negotiates trade agreements for the EU.

questions.question: Which of the following countries is not a member of the European Union?
questions.explanation: Norway is in EFTA/EEA but not the EU.

questions.question: As per the passage, which of the following can be most reasonably inferred about the status of the India–EU FTA?
options: It became automatically enforceable when negotiations concluded
It has replaced India's existing agreements with European states
It applies only to trade in agricultural and dairy products
It still requires completion of prescribed institutional procedures
questions.explanation: Concluding negotiations still leaves legal scrubbing, signature and ratification before entry into force.

questions.question: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the European Union (EU) from the European Free Trade Association (EFTA)?
options: Both organisations currently have identical memberships
EFTA forms the monetary-policy arm of the European Union
EU is a political-economic union, while EFTA is a trade grouping
EFTA membership is mandatory before accession to the European Union
questions.explanation: The EU is a political and economic union. EFTA (Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway, Switzerland) is a free-trade grouping.

questions.question: Under the World Trade Organization framework, an FTA that grants preferential tariffs to participating countries constitutes an exception to which general principle?
questions.explanation: FTAs are an exception to WTO Most-Favoured-Nation treatment (GATT Article XXIV).

questions.question: The provisions relating specifically to Administrative Tribunals were introduced into the Constitution of India through which constitutional amendment?
questions.explanation: The 42nd Amendment (1976) inserted Part XIV-A (Arts. 323A, 323B).

questions.question: With reference to Articles 323A and 323B of the Constitution, which of the following is correct?
options: Both provisions deal exclusively with service disputes
Article 323B applies only to Union government employees
Both provisions require tribunals to be constitutional courts
questions.explanation: Art. 323A covers administrative tribunals for service matters. Art. 323B covers tribunals for other matters.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes the composition envisaged for the National Tribunals Commission (NTC) under the 2026 reforms?
questions.explanation: The NTC has a Chairperson and four Members.

questions.question: The tribunal reforms discussed in the passage fall primarily within the administrative domain of which Union Ministry?
questions.explanation: Tribunal reform falls under the Ministry of Law and Justice.

questions.question: Which of the following most accurately distinguishes a tribunal from an ordinary court?
options: A tribunal can never decide disputes involving rights
A tribunal derives authority only from the Constitution
A tribunal generally exercises specialised adjudicatory jurisdiction
A tribunal is always headed by a serving Supreme Court judge
questions.explanation: Tribunals exercise specialised jurisdiction over particular subjects.

questions.question: Consider the following pairs: Tribunal Principal Area 1. NCLT Company law 2. CAT Service matters 3. NGT Environmental disputes 4. SAT Securities regulation Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.explanation: All four pairs are correct: NCLT for company law, CAT for service matters, NGT for environment and SAT for securities.

questions.question: India's emphasis on sovereignty and territorial integrity in regional connectivity discussions is most closely associated with its concerns regarding which initiative?
questions.explanation: India opposes the BRI because CPEC runs through PoK, violating its sovereignty.

questions.question: With reference to the institutional structure of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation, consider the following statements: 1. The Council of Heads of State is the SCO's highest decision-making body. 2. The Secretariat and RATS constitute its two permanent bodies. 3. The Council of National Coordinators coordinates interaction among member states. Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: All three are correct. The Council of Heads of State is supreme, the Secretariat (Beijing) and RATS (Tashkent) are the permanent bodies, and the Council of National Coordinators coordinates.

questions.question: As per the developments surrounding the 26th SCO Summit, which of the following correctly describes the transition in chairmanship?
options: Pakistan transferred the chairmanship to Kyrgyzstan.
Kyrgyzstan transferred the chairmanship to Pakistan.
Kazakhstan transferred the chairmanship to Uzbekistan.
Uzbekistan transferred the chairmanship to India.
questions.explanation: Kyrgyzstan passed the chairmanship to Pakistan.

sources.title: Anadolu: SCO leaders adopt Bishkek Declaration

questions.question: Which of the following best distinguishes an SCO observer state from an SCO dialogue partner?
options: An observer necessarily possesses voting rights, while a dialogue partner does not.
Both categories automatically acquire full membership after a fixed period.
They represent different levels of formal engagement short of full membership.
Dialogue partners participate only in security-related institutions of the SCO.
questions.explanation: Observers and dialogue partners are different levels of formal engagement short of full membership. Neither votes or becomes a member automatically.

questions.question: Consider the following initiatives associated with India at the 26th SCO Summit: 1. Civilisation Dialogue Forum 2. Young Scientist Forum 3. Young Author's Conclave 4. Inclusion of English as an official language of the SCO Which of the above found support in the summit outcomes?
questions.explanation: The Bishkek Declaration reflected all four Indian initiatives: Civilisation Dialogue Forum, Young Scientist Forum, Young Authors' Conclave and English as an SCO official language.

sources.title: IBEF: PM Modi participates in 26th SCO Summit

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT an original founding member of the SCO (2001)?
questions.explanation: The 2001 founders were China, Russia, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan and Uzbekistan. India joined in 2017.

questions.question: The award presently known as the Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna Award was originally named after:
questions.explanation: It was the Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna until it was renamed in 2021.

sources.title: Wikipedia: Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna

questions.question: Consider the following pairs relating to the National Sports Awards 2025: Sportsperson Discipline 1. Vidit Santosh Gujarathi Chess 2. Lalremsiami Hockey 3. Ekta Bhyan Para-athletics 4. Arvind Singh Rowing Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.explanation: All four Arjuna 2025 pairs are correct: Vidit Gujrathi (chess), Lalremsiami (hockey), Ekta Bhyan (para-athletics) and Arvind Singh (rowing).

sources.title: Open: Who's on India's National Sports Awards 2025 list

questions.question: Arrange the following sporting honours in chronological order of their institution, from earliest to latest: 1. Arjuna Award 2. Dronacharya Award 3. Khel Ratna Award
questions.explanation: The Arjuna Award began in 1961, the Dronacharya in 1985 and the Khel Ratna in 1991–92.

questions.question: Which of the following pairs is incorrectly matched?
options: Rashtriya Khel Protsahan Puraskar — Sports promotion
questions.explanation: The Khel Ratna honours outstanding sporting performance. Lifetime coaching contribution is the Dronacharya (Lifetime).

sources.title: Wikipedia: Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna

questions.question: With reference to the Arjuna Award (Lifetime) 2025, which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
questions.explanation: Former footballer and coach I. Arumainayagam received the Arjuna Award (Lifetime) 2025.

sources.title: Adda247: National Sports Awards 2025 winners list

questions.question: The 'Five Finger Policy' of China, which asserts responsibility to "liberate" certain regions, considers Tibet as the palm and which of the following as one of the five fingers?
questions.explanation: Mao-era 'Five Fingers' doctrine called Tibet the palm and Ladakh, Nepal, Sikkim, Bhutan and Arunachal (NEFA) its fingers.

questions.question: Which Chinese traveler visited India during the reign of Harshavardhana and contributed significantly to cultural exchange?
questions.explanation: Xuanzang (Hiuen Tsang) visited India (629–645 CE) during Harshavardhana's reign.

questions.question: The year 2025 marks a significant milestone in India-China diplomatic history. What is the occasion?
questions.explanation: India and China set up diplomatic relations on 1 April 1950, so 2025 marked 75 years.

questions.question: China accounts for approximately what percentage of global rare earth ore processing, making it a critical partner for India's high-tech industries?
questions.explanation: China processes about 90% of the world's rare earths.

questions.question: The 'Quad' is a strategic dialogue as a counter to China's assertiveness. Which four countries comprise the Quad?
questions.explanation: The Quad is India, the US, Japan and Australia.

questions.question: The Economic Survey 2023-2024 recommended attracting Chinese investment primarily to boost which sector in India?
questions.explanation: The Economic Survey 2023-24 argued that Chinese FDI could help India join global supply chains and boost manufacturing and exports.

questions.question: The report recommends adopting the "Miyawaki method" to address environmental issues in Delhi. This method is related to:
questions.explanation: The Miyawaki method grows dense native forests quickly, a form of afforestation and urban forestry.

questions.question: The volatility of ethanol-blended petrol can lead to increased evaporative emissions. These emissions act as precursors for the formation of which ground-level pollutant?
questions.explanation: Evaporative VOC emissions are precursors of ground-level ozone.

questions.question: In the context of crop residue management to prevent stubble burning, the use of machines like the 'Super Seeder' or 'Happy Seeder' to mix straw into the soil is an example of:
questions.explanation: Mixing straw into the field with Happy or Super Seeders is in-situ residue management.

questions.question: According to the report on Air Quality Standards, when were the current National Ambient Air Quality Standards (NAAQS) last revised in India?
questions.explanation: India's National Ambient Air Quality Standards were last revised in November 2009.

questions.question: The "Urban Heat Island Effect" is associated with which atmospheric phenomenon in the context of Delhi's pollution?
questions.explanation: Urban heat island effects combine with temperature inversions that trap pollutants near the ground over Delhi.

questions.question: Geographically, Delhi faces a disadvantage in air pollution dispersion because wind movement is blocked by:
options: The Himalayas to the North and Aravalli Hills to the Southwest
The Vindhyas to the South and Himalayas to the North
The Aravalli Hills to the North and Himalayas to the East
The Satpura Range to the South and Himalayas to the Northeast
questions.explanation: Delhi is landlocked between the Himalayas to the north and the Aravallis to the south-west, so pollutants disperse poorly.

questions.question: The 'Centre for Southeast Asian Studies' proposed by India at the 22nd ASEAN-India Summit is intended to promote:
questions.explanation: India's proposed Centre for Southeast Asian Studies (at Nalanda University) is meant for academic and cultural exchange.

questions.question: Which of the following countries was NOT one of the five founding fathers of ASEAN?
questions.explanation: ASEAN's founders (1967) were Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore and Thailand. Vietnam joined in 1995.

questions.question: The 22nd ASEAN–India Summit marked the adoption of which roadmap to implement the Comprehensive Strategic Partnership (CSP)?
questions.explanation: The 22nd summit adopted the ASEAN–India Plan of Action 2026–2030 to implement the Comprehensive Strategic Partnership.

questions.question: The 22nd ASEAN–India Summit, held in October 2025, took place in which city?
questions.explanation: It was held in Kuala Lumpur in October 2025 (Malaysia's chairship).

questions.question: What is the full form of ASEAN?
options: Asian Economic and Security Alliance Network
questions.explanation: ASEAN stands for Association of Southeast Asian Nations.

questions.question: Which country was officially welcomed as the 11th member of ASEAN during the 22nd ASEAN- India Summit in 2025?
questions.explanation: Timor-Leste was admitted as ASEAN's 11th member in October 2025.

questions.question: The Aravalli Green Wall Project draws direct inspiration from the "Great Green Wall" initiative, which is a flagship program of which continent?
questions.explanation: The Great Green Wall is an African Union initiative across the Sahel.

questions.question: Which Directive Principle of State Policy explicitly links the State’s duty to environmental protection?
questions.explanation: Article 48A directs the State to protect and improve the environment.

questions.question: The Aravalli Green Wall Initiative is planned to span across which of the following States/UTs?
questions.explanation: The Aravalli Green Wall covers Gujarat, Rajasthan, Haryana and Delhi.

questions.question: Which social media campaign was triggered by the Supreme Court's decision on the Aravalli Hills definition in 2025?
questions.explanation: The SC's November 2025 height-based definition set off the #SaveAravalli campaign.

questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding the Aravalli Range. Which of the statements given below is INCORRECT?
options: It is one of the oldest mountain systems in the world, dating back to the Precambrian era.
It acts as a natural barrier preventing the expansion of the Thar Desert into north-western India.
The range spans approximately 800 km from Gujarat to Delhi.
Its highest peak, Guru Shikhar, is located in the state of Haryana.
questions.explanation: Guru Shikhar (Mount Abu) is in Rajasthan, not Haryana. The other statements are correct.

questions.question: Where is the origin of archery widely believed to be, based on the earliest known evidence of the bow and arrow?
questions.explanation: The earliest known bow-and-arrow evidence (about 64,000 years ago) comes from Sibudu Cave, South Africa.

questions.question: In which city is the headquarters of the International Paralympic Committee (IPC) located?
questions.explanation: The International Paralympic Committee is headquartered in Bonn, Germany.

questions.question: Who was the first Indian athlete to win a gold medal at the Paralympic Games?
questions.explanation: Murlikant Petkar won India's first Paralympic gold (50 m freestyle swimming, Heidelberg 1972).

questions.question: The World Archery Para Championships 2025, where Sheetal Devi claimed the world title, was hosted in which city?
questions.explanation: The 2025 World Archery Para Championships were held in Gwangju, South Korea, where Sheetal Devi won the compound women's title.

questions.question: In which category of archery does Sheetal Devi primarily compete at the international level?
questions.explanation: Sheetal Devi competes in compound archery.

questions.question: The SHANTI Bill, 2025 repeals which of the following pairs of existing legislations?
options: The Atomic Energy Act, 1962 and the Environment Protection Act, 1986
The Atomic Energy Act, 1962 and the Civil Liability for Nuclear Damage Act, 2010
The Nuclear Safety Act, 2011, the Atomic Energy Act, 1948 and the Civil Liability for Nuclear Damage Act, 2010
The Civil Liability for Nuclear Damage Act, 2010 and the Electricity Act, 2003
questions.explanation: The SHANTI Act repeals and replaces both the Atomic Energy Act, 1962 and the Civil Liability for Nuclear Damage Act, 2010.

sources.title: Takshashila: SHANTI Act advances reform, streamlines and dilutes liability

questions.question: Which international body is responsible for safeguarding India's civilian nuclear reactors that use imported uranium?
options: The International Panel on Fissile Materials
questions.explanation: Indian reactors running on imported fuel are under IAEA safeguards (India-specific safeguards agreement, 2008–09).

questions.question: The Nuclear Energy Mission announced in the Union Budget 2025-26 has set a target to have at least five indigenously designed SMRs operational by which year?
questions.explanation: The Nuclear Energy Mission in Budget 2025-26 targets at least five indigenous SMRs operational by 2033.

questions.question: How does the SHANTI Act, 2025 differ from the CLNDA, 2010 regarding 'Supplier Liability'?
options: It increases supplier liability to ₹1,500 crore.
It restricts supplier liability to domestic companies only.
It mandates supplier liability only in cases of intentional damage.
questions.explanation: Unlike s.17(b) of the CLNDA, the SHANTI Act drops supplier liability and channels liability to the operator, subject to caps.

questions.question: What is the full form of the ‘SHANTI’ Act, 2025, recently assented to by the President?
options: Sustainable Handling and Advancement of Nuclear Technology for India
Sustainable Harnessing and Advancement of Nuclear Energy for Transforming India
Sustainable Holistic Application of Nuclear Technology for India
Sustainable Harnessing and Acceleration of Nuclear Energy for Tomorrow’s India
questions.explanation: SHANTI stands for Sustainable Harnessing and Advancement of Nuclear Energy for Transforming India.

sources.title: Indian Infrastructure: Central government introduces SHANTI Bill, 2025

questions.question: Which of the following authorities is NOT a member of the Selection Committee constituted to recommend the appointment of the Lokpal Chairperson?
options: The Leader of Opposition in Rajya Sabha
An eminent jurist nominated by the President
questions.explanation: The selection committee is the PM, the Lok Sabha Speaker, the Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha, the CJI (or nominee) and an eminent jurist. The Rajya Sabha LoP is not on it.

questions.question: Regarding the jurisdiction of the Lokpal over the Prime Minister, which of the following subject matters is EXCLUDED from an inquiry into corruption allegations?
questions.explanation: Allegations against the PM about international relations, security, public order, atomic energy and space are outside the Lokpal's inquiry.

questions.question: What is the tenure of office for the Chairperson and Members of the Lokpal?
options: 3 years or until the age of 70 years
5 years or until the age of 65 years
5 years or until the age of 70 years
6 years or until the age of 65 years
questions.explanation: The term is 5 years or until age 70, whichever is earlier.

questions.question: Over which agency does the Lokpal have superintendence in matters referred for preliminary inquiry/investigation?
questions.explanation: The Lokpal superintends the Delhi Special Police Establishment (CBI) for cases it refers.

questions.question: Under the Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013, the Inquiry Wing of the Lokpal is vested with the powers of which court for the purpose of conducting a preliminary inquiry?
options: A Criminal Court under the Code of Criminal Procedure
A Civil Court under the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908
A High Court under Article 226 of the Constitution
A Special Court under the Prevention of Corruption Act
questions.explanation: For preliminary inquiry the Lokpal's Inquiry Wing has the powers of a civil court under the CPC, 1908.

questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding the composition and appointment of the Lokpal: 1. The Lokpal consists of a Chairperson and a maximum of eight members, of whom 50% must be Judicial Members. 2. The Central Vigilance Commission (CVC) is not required to report to the Lokpal regarding complaints referred to it. 3. At least 50% of the members must belong to the SC, ST, OBC, Minorities, or Women categories. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements 1 and 3 are correct: at most 8 members, half of them judicial, and at least half from SC/ST/OBC/minorities/women. Statement 2 is wrong because the CVC must report to the Lokpal on referred complaints.

questions.question: During his visit to Ethiopia in December 2025, the Prime Minister of India was conferred with which highest honour of the country?
options: The Order of the Star of Ethiopia
The Grand Collar of the Order of Solomon
The Great Honor Nishan of Ethiopia
questions.explanation: In December 2025 Modi received the Great Honour Nishan of Ethiopia, the country's highest award.

sources.title: News on AIR: PM Modi conferred Great Honour Nishan of Ethiopia

questions.question: The “Solar Mamas” project primarily focuses on:
questions.explanation: 'Solar Mamas' (Barefoot College, with ITEC support) trains rural women, many from Africa, as solar engineers.

questions.question: In 2024–25, Red Sea insecurity forced India–Africa vessels to abandon the Suez Canal in favor of which route?
questions.explanation: Houthi attacks in the Red Sea forced ships around the Cape of Good Hope.

questions.question: In the decades following decolonisation, India and several African states coordinated their strategic autonomy and anti‑colonial agenda primarily through:
questions.explanation: India and African states coordinated through the Non-Aligned Movement.

questions.question: In which year did the Biological Weapons Convention enter into force?
questions.explanation: The BWC opened for signature in 1972 and entered into force on 26 March 1975.

questions.question: Which major verification mechanism does the BWC lack that the Chemical Weapons Convention possesses?
questions.explanation: The BWC has no compliance verification or on-site inspection regime like the CWC's OPCW.

questions.question: What is meant by "dual-use research" in the biosecurity context?
options: Research conducted by two countries jointly
Research with both civilian and military applications
Research funded by public and private sectors
questions.explanation: Dual-use research is legitimate research that could also be misused for weapons or harm.

questions.question: Which recent global event underscored the need for robust biological threat governance?
questions.explanation: COVID-19 is the recent event most cited as showing the need for stronger biological-threat governance.

questions.question: Recently, the Bank of India (BoI) successfully raised ₹10,000 crore via infrastructure bonds. What is the minimum tenure for infrastructure bonds as per RBI norms?
questions.explanation: RBI norms (2014) require long-term infrastructure bonds to have a minimum tenure of 7 years.

sources.title: RBI circular on long-term bonds for infrastructure (2014)

questions.question: Banks primarily issue infrastructure bonds to solve which specific financial challenge?
questions.explanation: Long-tenure infrastructure bonds help banks fund long-gestation loans without asset-liability mismatch.

sources.title: RBI circular on long-term bonds for infrastructure (2014)

questions.question: Which of the following is a primary risk associated with investing in long-term infrastructure bonds if market interest rates rise?
questions.explanation: When rates rise, existing long-duration bond prices fall, which is interest-rate risk.

questions.question: Which of the following institutions is NOT typically an issuer of Infrastructure Bonds?
questions.explanation: The RBI regulates and manages debt but does not issue infrastructure bonds. Banks, PFC and NHAI do.

questions.question: SEBI has proposed a framework to encourage investments in which specific type of bond dedicated to the "Blue Economy"?
questions.explanation: Blue bonds finance ocean and blue-economy projects, and SEBI has proposed a framework for them.

questions.question: Infrastructure Bonds are often compared to InvITs. What is a key difference regarding returns?
options: InvITs offer fixed interest, while Bonds offer variable returns.
Bonds offer fixed interest, while InvITs offer market-linked returns.
InvITs do not offer any returns until maturity.
questions.explanation: Bonds pay fixed coupons, while InvIT returns depend on project cash flows and market prices.

questions.question: As per the passage, the "winter" hearing before the capital's high court will consider pleas seeking that the Fund be juridically treated as:
options: A body corporate under the Companies Act, 2013
A foreign contribution entity under FEMA controls
A scheduled commercial bank under RBI inspection
"State" under Article 12, unlocking the transparency codes
questions.explanation: The Delhi High Court petitions ask that PM CARES be treated as 'State' under Article 12, which would bring RTI and other transparency obligations.

questions.question: With reference to the PM CARES Fund, which one of the following statements is correct?
options: It is a statutory fund established under the Disaster Management Act, 2005.
It receives annual budgetary allocations from the Consolidated Fund of India.
It is a public charitable trust whose contributions can qualify as CSR expenditure under the Companies Act, 2013.
It is administered directly by the Ministry of Finance as a fund of the Union Government.
questions.explanation: PM CARES is a public charitable trust. Donations to it count as CSR spending (Schedule VII, Companies Act). It is not statutory and gets no budget allocation.

questions.question: Which of the following correctly expands the acronym PM CARES?
options: Prime Minister’s Citizen Assistance and Relief in Emergency Situations
Prime Minister’s Central Assistance for Relief and Emergency Services
Prime Minister’s Citizen Aid and Response for Emergency Services
Prime Minister’s Central Action for Relief in Emergency Situations
questions.explanation: PM CARES stands for Prime Minister's Citizen Assistance and Relief in Emergency Situations.

questions.question: The PM CARES Fund was established in which of the following years?
questions.explanation: The fund was set up on 27 March 2020.

questions.question: Which one of the following correctly describes the composition of the PM CARES Fund's Board of Trustees?
options: Prime Minister as Chairperson and the Ministers of Defence, Home Affairs and Finance as ex-officio Trustees
Prime Minister as Chairperson and the Ministers of Finance, External Affairs and Health as ex-officio Trustees
Prime Minister, Vice-President and the Ministers of Home Affairs and Finance as ex-officio Trustees
Prime Minister as Chairperson, with the Cabinet Secretary and Finance Secretary as ex-officio Trustees
questions.explanation: The PM chairs the trust, with the Defence, Home and Finance Ministers as ex-officio trustees.

questions.question: Who has the authority to formulate rules or criteria for disbursal of funds held under PM CARES?
options: Comptroller and Auditor General of India
questions.explanation: The Board of Trustees sets the criteria for disbursal.

questions.question: The metaphor of "two rivers flowing from one indictment" flags which practical worry?
options: One accused consenting while co-accused refuse, fragmenting the trial
Trials and appeals running in different courts simultaneously
Evidence being copied across two separate judicial benches on trial
Double jeopardy attaching to identically worded charges
questions.explanation: If one accused consents and co-accused do not, a single indictment could split into separate trials.

questions.question: Who drafted the original provision relating to sedition in the proposed Indian Penal Code of 1837?
questions.explanation: Thomas Babington Macaulay included sedition (draft s.113) in his 1837 draft Penal Code.

questions.question: Which of the following was NOT one of the safeguards proposed by the 22nd Law Commission regarding the sedition law?
options: Requiring a tendency to incite violence or cause public disorder
Preliminary inquiry by an Inspector-level police officer
Prior permission from the government before registration of an FIR
Automatic transfer of all sedition cases to the Supreme Court
questions.explanation: The 22nd Law Commission (2023) proposed a 'tendency to incite violence' test, a preliminary inquiry by an Inspector-rank officer and government permission before an FIR. It did not propose moving cases to the Supreme Court.

questions.question: The publication whose writings landed its Poona editor in the sedition dock was:
questions.explanation: Bal Gangadhar Tilak, editor of Kesari (Poona), was tried for sedition in 1897 and 1908.

questions.question: The late-May clarification permitting consensual sedition trials was handed down in the matter titled:
options: Kamran v. State of Madhya Pradesh
S. G. Vombatkere v. Union of India
Romesh Thappar v. State of Madras
Anuradha Bhasin v. Union of India
questions.explanation: The May 2026 clarification (trials can proceed if the accused does not object) came in Kamran v. State of Madhya Pradesh.

sources.title: Drishti IAS: Supreme Court's revival of sedition trials

questions.question: Who was chosen as Iran's new Supreme Leader in March 2026 after the killing of Ali Khamenei?
questions.explanation: The Assembly of Experts chose Mojtaba Khamenei as Supreme Leader on 8 March 2026.

sources.title: Arab News: Iran names Khamenei's son Mojtaba as new supreme leader

questions.question: With reference to the air-defence systems used by Israel, which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
options: Iron Dome — Exo-atmospheric interception of long-range ballistic missiles
David’s Sling — Interception of medium- and long-range missiles
Arrow 3 — Interception primarily of short-range rockets
Patriot — Interception exclusively of cruise missiles
questions.explanation: David's Sling intercepts medium- and long-range threats. Iron Dome handles short-range rockets and Arrow-3 exo-atmospheric ballistic missiles.

questions.question: With reference to the Strait of Hormuz, which one of the following best explains its strategic significance?
options: It links the Persian Gulf with the Gulf of Oman and provides a major route for energy shipments.
It connects the Persian Gulf with the Red Sea and facilitates the movement of energy shipments.
It links the Gulf of Oman with the Arabian Sea and serves mainly as a route for container trade.
It connects the Arabian Sea with the Red Sea and provides an alternative route to the Suez Canal.
questions.explanation: Hormuz links the Persian Gulf with the Gulf of Oman and carries about a fifth of world oil.

questions.question: The Israeli codename for the 28 February 2026 decapitation offensive against Iran was:
questions.explanation: Israel's operation was 'Lion's Roar' ('Roar of the Lion'). The US part was Operation Epic Fury, and Rising Lion was the June 2025 operation.

questions.question: Which international convention recognises the right of transit passage for ships through straits used for international navigation?
options: UN Convention on the Law of the Sea
questions.explanation: UNCLOS (Part III) recognises transit passage through international straits.

questions.question: The term "Axis of Resistance" (Mehvar-e Moqawamat) refers to an informal political and military alliance led by Iran. Which of the following groups or non-state actors are considered part of this network? 1) Hezbollah (Lebanon) 2) Ansar Allah / Houthis (Yemen) 3) Islamic Resistance in Iraq 4) Hamas (Palestine) Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.explanation: The Axis of Resistance includes Hezbollah, the Houthis, Iraqi militias (Islamic Resistance in Iraq) and Hamas.

questions.question: The Indus Waters Treaty was signed in:
questions.explanation: The treaty was signed in Karachi in 1960.

questions.question: Approximately what percentage of the total water volume of the six-river Indus system was allocated to Pakistan under the 1960 agreement?
questions.explanation: The Western Rivers allotted to Pakistan carry about 80% of the system's water.

questions.question: The Kishenganga Hydroelectric Project, which has been a major point of technical disagreement under the treaty, is constructed on a tributary of which Western River?
questions.explanation: The Kishenganga (Neelum) is a tributary of the Jhelum.

questions.question: Which of the following correctly matches the river with its classification under the Indus Waters Treaty?
questions.explanation: The Sutlej is an Eastern River. Ravi and Beas are Eastern, while the Chenab and Jhelum are Western.

questions.question: Under the dispute-resolution framework of the Indus Waters Treaty, which sequence correctly represents the mechanisms according to the nature of the issue?
options: Court of Arbitration → Neutral Expert → Permanent Indus Commission
Permanent Indus Commission → Neutral Expert → Court of Arbitration
Neutral Expert → Permanent Indus Commission → Court of Arbitration
Permanent Indus Commission → Court of Arbitration → Neutral Expert
questions.explanation: The three tiers are: questions go to the Permanent Indus Commission, differences to a Neutral Expert, and disputes to a Court of Arbitration (Art. IX).

questions.question: Pakistan's co-signatory of the 1960 treaty, a military ruler, was:
questions.explanation: Pakistan's signatory was President Ayub Khan.

questions.question: Which country won the ICC Women’s T20 World Cup 2026?
questions.explanation: Australia beat England by 7 wickets at Lord's to win the 2026 Women's T20 World Cup.

sources.title: Al Jazeera: Australia thrash England to win record seventh Women's T20 World Cup

questions.question: The fastest fifty by an Indian in Women's T20 World Cup history (India vs Australia in 2026) was struck by:
questions.explanation: Harmanpreet Kaur's 25–27-ball fifty against Australia at Lord's was the fastest by an Indian at a Women's T20 World Cup.

sources.title: IANS: Harmanpreet's fastest fifty powers India to 170/4 vs Australia

questions.question: Which of the following correctly identifies the four teams that qualified for the semi-finals of the 2026 Women’s T20 World Cup?
options: Australia, India, England and New Zealand
Australia, South Africa, England and West Indies
Australia, India, England and South Africa

The EU participates only in economic sessions and not in political discussions.

An informal forum of advanced economies for consultation and coordination
A specialised agency of the United Nations dealing with global economic affairs
A regional economic organisation established under international law

A uniform, gender-equal order of preference among Class-1 heirs
A separate succession framework for married and unmarried women
A system based exclusively on the personal law applicable to the deceased

questions.question: With reference to the Uniform Civil Code, Assam, Bill, 2026, which one of the following is correct?

It seeks to regulate marriage, adoption, divorce, maintenance and religious endowments through a common framework.
It seeks to regulate divorce, guardianship, maintenance and religious conversion through a common framework.

A relationship within specified degrees of kinship
A relationship in which one party has previously been divorced
A relationship in which the parties have different places of residence

questions.question: The Union Budget 2026–27 was inspired by three “Kartavyas”. Which one of the following correctly represents them?

questions.question: Which of the following sectors is explicitly mentioned as remaining duty-free despite the new tariff regime?

options: Continued purchases of Russian oil and defence equipment
High trade surplus with the United States
Refusal to participate in Indo-Pacific trade frameworks

sources.title: Wikipedia: Tariffs in the second Trump administration

questions.question: A multilateral drill conducted in support of a free and open Indo-Pacific, involving India, the US, Japan and Australia, is known as:

sources.title: Ministry of Commerce export data FY2024-25

questions.question: According to the India Meteorological Department (IMD), a rain event is officially classified as a "Cloudburst" if the rainfall received at a station in one hour exceeds:
questions.explanation: IMD calls it a cloudburst when 10 cm (100 mm) or more of rain falls in an hour over a small area.

questions.question: In meteorology, Doppler Weather Radars are primarily used to measure which specific properties of clouds and precipitation to predict extreme weather?
questions.explanation: Doppler radars measure reflectivity (precipitation intensity) and radial velocity (wind and motion).

questions.question: Chamoli district, frequently in the news for cloudbursts and glacial disasters, is located in which Indian state?
questions.explanation: Chamoli district is in Uttarakhand.

questions.question: Under the Disaster Management Act, 2005, who serves as the ex-officio Chairperson of the National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA)?

questions.question: Which nodal agency under the Ministry of Earth Sciences is responsible for issuing official weather forecasts and warnings, including those for cloudbursts, in India?
questions.explanation: IMD, under the Ministry of Earth Sciences, issues official weather forecasts and warnings.

questions.question: Who currently holds the World Record for the Men's Javelin throw with a distance of 98.48 meters?

questions.explanation: The AFI declared 7 August, the day of Neeraj Chopra's Tokyo gold in 2021, National Javelin Day.

questions.explanation: Abhinav Bindra won India's first individual Olympic gold (10 m air rifle, Beijing 2008).

questions.explanation: Tokyo hosted the 2025 World Athletics Championships in September 2025.

questions.question: The Rapid Action Force (RAF), mentioned in the passage, is a specialized wing of which organization?
questions.explanation: The Rapid Action Force is a specialised riot-control wing of the CRPF.

questions.question: While the current event is widely termed 'Mahakumbh', traditionally/technically the term 'Maha Kumbh' refers to the unique event held after the completion of 12 Purna Kumbh cycles, which is once every:
questions.explanation: A Maha Kumbh comes after 12 Purna Kumbhs (12 × 12 years), so once every 144 years. Prayagraj held one in 2025.

questions.explanation: The four Kumbh venues are Prayagraj, Haridwar, Ujjain and Nashik. Varanasi is not one of them.

sources.title: Wikipedia: 2025 Prayag Maha Kumbh crowd crush

Because Indian exporters face pressure from high US tariffs.

It is a bacterium that mimics viral behaviour.

questions.question: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched regarding the disease and its causative agent?

questions.question: In her opening address for the Union Budget 2026-2027, the Finance Minister invoked the birth anniversary of which spiritual leader?
questions.explanation: The FM opened the 2026-27 Budget 'on the sacred occasion of Magh Purnima and the birth anniversary of Guru Ravidas' (1 February 2026).

questions.question: The budget emphasizes "Action Over Ambivalence" and "Reform Over Rhetoric." What is the third principle mentioned?
questions.explanation: The FM credited the government's choices for favouring 'action over ambivalence, reform over rhetoric, and people over populism'.

sources.title: YourStory: FM Nirmala Sitharaman presents Budget 2026

questions.question: What is the approximate high growth rate mentioned in the budget document?
questions.explanation: The Budget describes India sustaining high growth of around 7% with moderate inflation.

sources.title: News on AIR: Union Budget 2026-27 leads towards vision of developed India

questions.question: How many dedicated Chemical Parks are planned to enhance domestic production?
questions.explanation: The Budget announced support for three dedicated chemical parks on a cluster-based, plug-and-play model.

questions.question: Which sector has the highest expenditure allocation in the budget according to the "Expenditure of Major Items" data?
questions.explanation: Among the options, Defence has the largest allocation in the 'Expenditure of Major Items' table, ahead of transport, rural development and home affairs.

sources.title: Union Budget 2026-27: Budget at a Glance – Expenditure of Major Items

questions.question: Under PESA, what role do Gram Sabhas play regarding land alienation?
questions.explanation: PESA makes the Gram Sabha's consultation or consent necessary before land acquisition and lets it prevent alienation of tribal land, making it a gatekeeper rather than an advisory or revenue body.

questions.question: Which body is recognized as the primary authority under PESA?
questions.explanation: PESA puts the Gram Sabha at the centre of self-governance in Scheduled Areas.

questions.question: Across how many states was PESA enacted to operationalize tribal self-rule?
questions.explanation: PESA covers the ten Fifth Schedule States: Andhra Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Gujarat, Himachal Pradesh, Jharkhand, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Odisha, Rajasthan and Telangana.

questions.question: How did PESA transform forest dwellers economically?
options: From wage earners to economic stakeholders
questions.explanation: Gram Sabhas got ownership of minor forest produce and control over local resources, turning forest dwellers from wage earners into economic stakeholders.

questions.question: What broader international norm could be undermined by a Greenland crisis?
options: The Law of the Sea Convention
questions.explanation: The passage says a crisis would test 'global norms governing nuclear restraint and security guarantees', which points to the NPT regime.

questions.question: Which monitoring function does Greenland currently serve in NATO's defense architecture?
options: Monitoring of Chinese naval movements in the Pacific
Surveillance of the Suez Canal shipping routes
GIUK gap monitoring for North Atlantic access control
questions.explanation: Greenland is central to monitoring the GIUK (Greenland–Iceland–UK) gap, the chokepoint for North Atlantic access.

questions.question: Greenland is constitutionally described as:
questions.explanation: Greenland is a self-governing autonomous territory within the Kingdom of Denmark.

questions.question: The U.S. military presence in Greenland is primarily governed by which agreement?
questions.explanation: The US presence (e.g. Pituffik Space Base) is governed by the 1951 Defense of Greenland Agreement with Denmark.

questions.question: Which institution is responsible for the unified central banking system of the Eurozone?
questions.explanation: The European Central Bank runs monetary policy for the euro area.

questions.question: Which country does NOT share a border with Bulgaria?
questions.explanation: Bulgaria borders Romania, Serbia, North Macedonia, Greece and Türkiye. It does not border Albania.

questions.question: What was Bulgaria's national currency before euro adoption?
questions.explanation: Bulgaria's currency before the euro was the lev.

questions.question: Which treaty established the legal framework for the Eurozone and Economic and Monetary Union?
questions.explanation: The Maastricht Treaty (1992) created Economic and Monetary Union and the basis for the euro.

questions.question: On which date did Bulgaria officially adopt the euro as its legal tender?
questions.explanation: Bulgaria adopted the euro on 1 January 2026, becoming the 21st euro-area member.

questions.question: Which country is a member of NATO but NOT a member of the European Union?
questions.explanation: Türkiye is a NATO member but not in the EU. Greece, Spain and Croatia are in both.

questions.question: What major legal concern has been raised regarding the U.S. withdrawal from the WHO?
options: The notice period was not properly served
The withdrawal was not ratified by the U.S. Supreme Court
The WHO Constitution prohibits any member from withdrawing
questions.explanation: The main legal concern was unpaid US assessed contributions. The 1948 joint resolution on US WHO membership conditions withdrawal on one year's notice and full payment of dues.

sources.title: Wikipedia: United States withdrawal from the World Health Organization

questions.question: Where is the headquarters of the World Health Organization located?
questions.explanation: The WHO is headquartered in Geneva, Switzerland.

questions.question: Which of the following diseases was successfully eradicated through a WHO-led global campaign?
questions.explanation: Smallpox was declared eradicated in 1980 after the WHO-led campaign.

questions.question: 'World Health Day' is celebrated on which date and why?
options: 24 October – to mark the founding of the United Nations
7 April – to mark the establishment of the WHO
12 December – to mark Universal Health Coverage Day
22 March – to mark World Water Day
questions.explanation: World Health Day, 7 April, marks the WHO's founding in 1948.

questions.question: The U.S. withdrawal from the WHO is best described as:
options: A judicial decision by the U.S. Supreme Court
An executive action by the U.S. President
A legislative act passed by the U.S. Congress
A decision taken by the UN General Assembly
questions.explanation: President Trump initiated the withdrawal by executive order on 20 January 2025, and it took effect in January 2026.

sources.title: Wikipedia: United States withdrawal from the World Health Organization

questions.question: ECINet is the Election Commission's digital platform used for what purpose?
questions.explanation: Per the passage, ECINet streamlines verification (backend cross-checking, status updates, document uploads). It is not used for vote counting or exit polls.

questions.question: What does EPIC stand for in the context of voter identification?
questions.explanation: EPIC stands for Electors Photo Identity Card.

questions.question: Which Act specifies the procedures for enrolment and revision of electoral rolls?
questions.explanation: Enrolment and roll revision procedures are in the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960, framed under the RP Act, 1950.

questions.question: Under which Article of the Constitution does the Election Commission of India derive its power to conduct elections and electoral roll revisions?
questions.explanation: Article 324 gives the ECI superintendence, direction and control of electoral rolls and elections.

questions.question: The removal process of the Chief Election Commissioner is similar to that of:
questions.explanation: Under Art. 324(5) the CEC can be removed only in the same manner and on the same grounds as a Supreme Court judge.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a stated objective of the Pax Silica initiative?
options: Build resilient supply chains for semiconductors and AI infrastructure
Reduce coercive dependencies on geopolitical rivals
Establish a single global currency for technology trade
Counter non-market practices including overcapacity and dumping
questions.explanation: Pax Silica is about technology supply chains (resilience, cutting coercive dependencies, countering dumping), not a common currency. The passage says so explicitly.

questions.question: Consider the following pairs of Pax Silica members and their strategic contributions: Member Strategic Contribution 1. South Korea EUV lithography machines 2. Singapore Semiconductor fabrication and logistics 3. United Kingdom AI research and semiconductor design (ARM) 4. Israel Memory chip production Which of the pairs given above is/are correctly matched?
questions.explanation: Singapore (fabrication and logistics) and the UK (ARM chip design and AI research) are correctly matched. EUV machines come from the Netherlands (ASML), and memory chips are South Korea's strength, not Israel's.

questions.question: In 2025, China suspended the supply of which critical input to India, negatively impacting India's automobile and electronics industry?
questions.explanation: China's 2025 export curbs on rare-earth magnets disrupted India's auto and electronics makers.

questions.question: Which of the following correctly represents the upstream-to-downstream sequence in the Pax Silica "Full Stack" approach?
questions.explanation: The 'full stack' runs from critical minerals (upstream) to semiconductors to AI infrastructure (downstream).

questions.question: How many 'Chakras' or key areas of multilateral cooperation structure the deliberations at the AI Impact Summit 2026?
questions.explanation: The Summit had seven Chakras: human capital, inclusion, safe and trusted AI, resilience/innovation, science, democratising AI resources and economic growth.

sources.title: Tribune: 3 Sutras, 7 Chakras anchor India AI Impact Summit 2026

questions.question: The three foundational pillars or 'Sutras' of the AI Impact Summit 2026 are:
questions.explanation: The three Sutras were People, Planet and Progress.

sources.title: Tribune: 3 Sutras, 7 Chakras anchor India AI Impact Summit 2026

questions.question: The India AI Impact Summit 2026, inaugurated by Prime Minister Narendra Modi, was held at which venue in New Delhi?
questions.explanation: It was held at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi (16–21 February 2026).

sources.title: Tribune: India AI Impact Summit 2026 at Bharat Mandapam

questions.question: The AI Impact Summit 2026 is aligned with India's broader vision of:
questions.explanation: The summit was framed within India's Viksit Bharat@2047 vision.

questions.question: The three flagship Global Impact Challenges at the AI Impact Summit 2026 are:
options: AI for India, AI for Women, AI for Youth
AI for ALL, AI by HER, and YUVAi
AI Innovation, AI Research, AI Deployment
AI Global, AI National, AI Local
questions.explanation: The three Global Impact Challenges were AI for ALL, AI by HER and YUVAi (for ages 13–21).

questions.question: Which last name belongs to both the last Shah of Iran and his son currently living in exile?
questions.explanation: Mohammad Reza Shah Pahlavi was the last Shah, and his exiled son is Reza Pahlavi.

questions.question: What was the name of the Shah's modernization and land reform program launched in 1963?
questions.explanation: The Shah's 1963 reform programme was the White Revolution.

questions.question: On which date was Iran declared an Islamic Republic following a national referendum?
questions.explanation: Iran became an Islamic Republic on 1 April 1979 after a referendum.

questions.question: The political system established after the 1979 Islamic Revolution in Iran is based on which doctrine of Ayatollah Khomeini?
questions.explanation: The system rests on Khomeini's doctrine of Velayat-e Faqih, Guardianship of the Islamic Jurist.

sources.title: Wikipedia: Guardianship of the Islamic Jurist

questions.question: What was the primary trigger for the deadly protests that erupted in Iran in late December?
options: Strict enforcement of mandatory hijab laws
Allegations of election fraud by the Guardian Council
Demands for the immediate restoration of the Pahlavi dynasty
questions.explanation: The late-December 2025 protests were triggered by economic distress: soaring inflation and the rial's collapse.

questions.question: With reference to the political dynamics in Iran leading up to the 1979 Revolution, which of the following pairs is/are correctly matched? Event/Entity Description 1. SAVAK The secret police force used by Mohammad Reza Pahlavi to suppress dissent. 2. Black Friday (1978) A massacre of protesters in Tehran’s Jaleh Square that intensified the revolution. 3. Nationalisation of Oil A policy championed by Reza Shah Pahlavi in 1925 to expel British influence. Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.explanation: SAVAK was the Shah's secret police, and Black Friday (8 Sept 1978, Jaleh Square) was a massacre of protesters. Oil was nationalised in 1951 under PM Mossadegh, not by Reza Shah in 1925.

questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding the findings of the Global Risks Report 2026: I.  The report identifies geoeconomic confrontation as the single biggest risk facing India in the immediate term. II.  At the global level, cybersecurity has emerged as the most severe risk, surpassing armed conflict and climate threats. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
options: Both Statement I and Statement II
Neither Statement I nor Statement II
questions.explanation: Both statements are reversed. Geoeconomic confrontation is the top global short-term risk, and cyber insecurity is the top risk for India.

sources.title: The Week (PTI): Geoeconomic conflict top global risk for 2026, cyber insecurity for India

questions.question: Which types of cyberattacks dominate India's threat landscape according to the report?
questions.explanation: Seqrite's India Cyber Threat Report 2026 found Trojans (about 43%) and file infectors (about 34%) dominate detections in India.

questions.question: Which of the following is the first international treaty seeking to address Internet and computer crime by harmonizing national laws and improving investigative techniques?
questions.explanation: The Budapest Convention on Cybercrime (2001) was the first international treaty on internet and computer crime.

questions.question: Consider the following statements about India's cybersecurity institutional framework: 1. CERT-In is the nodal agency for cybersecurity incident response under MeitY. 2. NCIIPC protects Critical Information Infrastructure under NTRO. 3. I4C coordinates cybercrime investigation under Ministry of Home Affairs. 4. Defence Cyber Agency handles military cyber operations under Integrated Defence Staff. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: All four are correct: CERT-In (MeitY), NCIIPC (under NTRO), I4C (MHA) and the Defence Cyber Agency (HQ Integrated Defence Staff).

questions.question: Which of the following statements regarding the World Economic Forum (WEF) is NOT correct?
options: It was founded in 1971 by Klaus Schwab.
It is an international organization for public-private cooperation.
It is headquartered in Geneva, Switzerland.
It releases the World Economic Outlook report.
questions.explanation: The World Economic Outlook is an IMF report. The WEF (founded 1971 by Klaus Schwab, based in Cologny, Geneva) publishes reports such as the Global Risks and Global Gender Gap reports.

questions.question: What is India's global ranking in aluminium production as of 2025?
questions.explanation: India is the world's second-largest aluminium producer, after China.

sources.title: Ministry of Mines: Aluminium sector overview

questions.question: Which of the following best describes the three stages of the mineral value chain covered by India's minerals diplomacy?
questions.explanation: India's minerals diplomacy covers the whole value chain: mining, then refining and processing, then manufacturing.

questions.question: According to the Mines and Minerals (Amendment) Act, 2025, how many strategic and critical minerals are subject to centralised auctioning?
questions.explanation: Part D of the First Schedule (MMDR Act, as amended) lists 24 critical and strategic minerals auctioned by the Centre.

sources.title: MMDR Amendment Act, 2023 – Part D, First Schedule

questions.question: India has set a target to achieve Net Zero emissions by which year?
questions.explanation: At COP26 (Glasgow, 2021) India pledged net zero by 2070.

questions.question: According to the Economic Survey 2025-26, which sector remains the main driver of growth on the supply side?
questions.explanation: The Survey identifies services as the main driver of supply-side growth.

questions.question: The Economic Survey was separated from the Union Budget and presented as an independent document after which year?
questions.explanation: The Economic Survey was separated from the Budget and presented on its own from 1964.

questions.question: The Economic Survey 2025-26 projected India's real GDP growth for FY 2026-27 in the range of:
questions.explanation: The Survey projected FY2026-27 real GDP growth at 6.8–7.2%.

questions.question: According to the Economic Survey 2025-26, improvements in urban consumption were aided by:
questions.explanation: Urban consumption was helped by tax rationalisation (income-tax relief and GST cuts).

questions.question: The GST 2.0 proposal suggests what rate for demerit/sin goods including cess?
questions.explanation: GST 2.0 created a 40% special rate for demerit/sin goods, replacing compensation cess.

questions.question: Which ministry prepares the Economic Survey?
options: Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation
questions.explanation: The Ministry of Finance (Economic Division, DEA, under the CEA) prepares the Economic Survey.

questions.question: What right does India reserve regarding the Shaksgam Valley dispute?
questions.explanation: The MEA says India 'reserves the right to take necessary measures to safeguard its interests' on Shaksgam.

questions.question: Under which Indian State or Union Territory does India claim Shaksgam Valley?
questions.explanation: India claims Shaksgam as part of the UT of Ladakh.

questions.question: What mountain ranges border the Shaksgam Valley?
questions.explanation: The valley lies between the Karakoram and the Kunlun ranges.

questions.question: Which river does the Shaksgam River join in China?
questions.explanation: The Shaksgam River joins the Yarkand River in Xinjiang.

questions.question: Which Chinese counties reportedly administer Shaksgam Valley?
questions.explanation: China administers the tract as part of Taxkorgan and Yecheng (Kargilik) counties in Xinjiang.

questions.question: According to the World Anti-Doping Agency (WADA) report published in December 2025, India topped global doping violations for the:
questions.explanation: WADA's 2024 Testing Figures report (December 2025) ranked India top for the third straight year (260 positives).

sources.title: Guardian Nigeria (AFP): India named worst doping offender for third straight year

questions.question: Which sport recorded the highest number of doping violations in India according to the latest report?
questions.explanation: Athletics had the most Indian positives (76).

sources.title: The Bridge: India tops doping countries for 2024 per WADA report

questions.question: Which prominent Indian athlete faced a four-year ban linked to anabolic agents/SARMs starting from January 2023?
questions.explanation: Sprinter Dutee Chand got a four-year ban from January 2023 after testing positive for SARMs.

questions.question: The 2030 Commonwealth Games, relevant to India's doping concerns, are planned to be held in:
questions.explanation: Ahmedabad hosts the 2030 Commonwealth Games.

questions.question: Arrange the following sports in descending order of doping positives recorded in 2024:
questions.explanation: In 2024 the order was athletics (76), weightlifting (43), wrestling (29), then boxing/powerlifting.

sources.title: Factly: India's doping numbers stay high despite record testing

questions.question: The World Anti-Doping Agency (WADA) was established in which year and initiated by which organization?
options: 1995 by the International Association of Athletics Federations (IAAF)
2001 by the Federation Internationale de Football Association (FIFA)
2003 by the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS)
questions.explanation: WADA was set up in 1999 on the initiative of the IOC, after the 1998 Festina cycling scandal.

questions.question: What operating system capability does DHRUV64 support?
questions.explanation: DHRUV64 (C-DAC VEGA AS2161) has an MMU and virtual memory and can run Linux.

questions.question: Which of the following Indian processors was specifically developed for space applications?
questions.explanation: ISRO-SCL's VIKRAM (Vikram 3201) is a space-grade processor for launch-vehicle avionics.

questions.question: India's indigenous microprocessor development efforts include the "Shakti" processor, developed by:
questions.explanation: The SHAKTI RISC-V processors were developed at IIT Madras.

questions.question: The correct hierarchy of memory from fastest to slowest is:
questions.explanation: From fastest to slowest: registers, cache, RAM, hard disk.

questions.question: The Strait of Hormuz has become a critical flashpoint in the 2026 Iran-Israel-US conflict. Which of the following statements about the Strait of Hormuz is/are correct? 1. It is the only sea passage from the Persian Gulf to the open ocean. 2. It is bordered by Iran to the north and Oman and the UAE to the south. 3. Its width varies between 55 to 95 kilometres. 4. It connects the Persian Gulf directly to the Red Sea.
questions.explanation: Hormuz is the Gulf's only sea outlet, lies between Iran and Oman (Musandam) and the UAE, and is about 55–95 km wide. It leads to the Gulf of Oman and Arabian Sea, not the Red Sea.

questions.question: The Persian Gulf connects to the Shatt al-Arab delta at its northwestern extremity. Which two rivers empty into the Persian Gulf through this delta?
questions.explanation: The Tigris and Euphrates meet as the Shatt al-Arab, which enters the Persian Gulf.

questions.question: Which non-state actor launched rockets from Lebanon in solidarity with Iran in March 2026?
questions.explanation: Hezbollah fired rockets from Lebanon across the Blue Line in support of Iran.

questions.question: Which Supreme Leader of Iran was killed in the US-Israeli strike on 28 February 2026?
questions.explanation: Ayatollah Ali Khamenei was killed in the 28 February 2026 strike.

sources.title: NPR: Iran's supreme leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei has been killed

questions.question: With reference to the Quantum Valley project, which of the following statements is correct?
options: It is being developed in Hyderabad.
It aims to install India’s first 133-qubit quantum computer by 2026
It is solely funded by the private sector
It is an initiative under the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology
questions.explanation: Amaravati Quantum Valley (Andhra Pradesh, not Hyderabad) is to host IBM's Quantum System Two, billed as India's first 133-qubit (Heron) system. It is a public–private project of the AP government with IBM, TCS and L&T.

questions.question: The National Quantum Mission follows an implementation strategy described as the Hub-Spoke- Spike model. How many Thematic Hubs has the mission established?
questions.explanation: The NQM has four Thematic Hubs (computing, communication, sensing & metrology, materials & devices).

questions.question: The Quantum Valley project is described as an example of which innovation model involving alliance?
questions.explanation: Government, academia and industry together make up the Triple Helix model of innovation.

sources.title: Wikipedia: Triple helix model of innovation

questions.question: The MeitY Quantum Computing Applications Lab is a collaboration between India's Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology and which global technology company?
questions.explanation: MeitY set up its Quantum Computing Applications Lab with Amazon Web Services (2021).

sources.title: PIB: MeitY Quantum Computing Applications Lab (2021)

questions.question: Which of the following institutions is the lead institution for the Quantum Computing vertical under the National Quantum Mission?
questions.explanation: IISc Bengaluru leads the NQM quantum-computing hub.

questions.question: The Quantum Valley project involves collaboration between government and industry leaders. Which of the following companies is NOT mentioned as an industry partner?
questions.explanation: Quantum Valley's industry partners are IBM, TCS and L&T. Infosys is not one of them.

questions.question: The 16th Finance Commission recommends that the Union government annually disclose CAG- certified data on net tax proceeds under which constitutional article?
questions.explanation: Article 279 defines 'net proceeds' as certified by the CAG.

questions.question: The 16th Finance Commission has recommended grants totalling ₹9.47 lakh crore over the five- year period. Which of the following categories of grants has been DISCONTINUED compared to the 15th Finance Commission? 1. Revenue deficit grants 2. Sector-specific grants 3. State-specific grants 4. Disaster management grants
questions.explanation: The 16th FC dropped revenue-deficit, sector-specific and State-specific grants, keeping grants for local bodies and disaster management.

questions.question: The 16th Finance Commission has redefined the "Demographic Performance" criterion. Under the 15th FC, it was based on Total Fertility Rate (TFR). What metric does the 16th FC use instead?
options: Life Expectancy at birth as per the 2011 Census
questions.explanation: The 16th FC measures demographic performance by population growth between 1971 and 2011.

questions.question: Which of the following institutions is associated with the Chairman of the 16th Finance Commission?
questions.explanation: Chairman Arvind Panagariya was the first Vice-Chairman of NITI Aayog.

questions.question: The 16th Finance Commission has recommended the fiscal deficit limit for states to be capped at:
questions.explanation: The 16th FC suggests capping States' fiscal deficits at 3% of GSDP.

questions.question: Under which constitutional provision may the State impose reasonable restrictions on the right to form associations in the interest of the sovereignty and integrity of India?
questions.explanation: Article 19(4) allows reasonable restrictions on the right to form associations in the interest of sovereignty and integrity, public order or morality.

questions.question: The 2019 Amendment to the UAPA empowered a specific investigative agency to seize properties without state consent. Which agency is this?
questions.explanation: The 2019 amendment lets the NIA Director-General approve property seizure without State consent.

questions.question: Which amendment to the UAPA first introduced terrorism as a distinct legal category within the Act?
questions.explanation: The 2004 amendment (UPA government) made 'terrorist act' a distinct category after POTA was repealed.

questions.question: The Supreme Court recently denied bail to Umar Khalid and Sharjeel Imam in the 2020 Delhi riots conspiracy case under the UAPA. Which of the following principles did the Court apply to distinguish between the accused who were denied bail and those who were granted bail?
options: The Doctrine of Pith and Substance
questions.explanation: The Court used a proportionality-style distinction between 'architect' roles and facilitators in deciding bail.

questions.question: The Supreme Court distinguished the present case from which judgment while denying bail?
questions.explanation: It distinguished Union of India v. K.A. Najeeb (2021), which allowed bail for prolonged incarceration under UAPA.

sources.title: Union of India v. K.A. Najeeb (2021)

questions.question: Under which section of the UAPA is the definition of a “terrorist act” provided?
questions.explanation: Section 15 of the UAPA defines a 'terrorist act'.

questions.question: Which of the following Indian Ramsar Sites are included in the Montreux Record? 1. Chilika Lake 2. Keoladeo Ghana National Park 3. Loktak Lake 4. Sundarban Wetland
questions.explanation: India's Montreux Record sites are Keoladeo National Park and Loktak Lake. Chilika was removed in 2002.

questions.question: Which of the following is the smallest Ramsar Site in India by area?
questions.explanation: Renuka Lake in Himachal Pradesh (about 0.2 sq km), in the Himalayan foothills, is the smallest Ramsar site the passage refers to.

questions.question: Which of the following wetlands is famous for its unique floating islands known as “phumdis”?
questions.explanation: Loktak Lake in Manipur has floating phumdis, including Keibul Lamjao, the world's only floating national park (home of the sangai deer).

questions.question: World Wetlands Day is observed every year on which date?
questions.explanation: World Wetlands Day, 2 February, marks the adoption of the Ramsar Convention (1971).

questions.question: The Supreme Court directed which institution to admit Harish Rana to its palliative care department and formulate an end-of-life care plan?
options: Post Graduate Institute of Medical Education and Research (PGIMER), Chandigarh
All India Institute of Medical Sciences (AIIMS), Delhi
questions.explanation: On 11 March 2026 the Supreme Court directed AIIMS Delhi to admit Harish Rana to its palliative care centre and withdraw life support under an end-of-life care plan.

sources.title: The Week: SC allows first passive euthanasia (11 Mar 2026)

questions.question: The Draft Guidelines for Withdrawal of Life Support were released by which ministry?
questions.explanation: The Union Health Ministry issued the draft guidelines for withdrawal of life support in terminally ill patients (2024).

sources.title: Scroll: From Aruna Shanbaug to Harish Rana

questions.question: The Supreme Court urged the Union Government to enact which of the following?
options: A law on passive euthanasia and end-of-life care
A law banning all forms of euthanasia
A law on active euthanasia only
questions.explanation: The bench urged Parliament to enact comprehensive legislation on passive euthanasia and end-of-life decisions.

sources.title: The Week: SC calls for legislation

questions.question: Which Article of the Constitution was invoked to recognise the right to die with dignity?
questions.explanation: Common Cause (2018) recognised the right to die with dignity as part of the right to life under Article 21.

sources.title: Wikipedia: Common Cause v. Union of India

questions.question: Harish Rana was suffering from which medical condition for over 13 years?
questions.explanation: Harish Rana had been in a permanent vegetative state for about 13 years after a fall.

sources.title: Business Standard: SC allows passive euthanasia for man in vegetative state for 13 years

questions.question: Which of the following countries was the first in the world to legalize euthanasia?
questions.explanation: The Netherlands was the first country to legalise euthanasia (law in force April 2002). Belgium followed months later.

questions.question: Which of the following is the correct ground for the removal of the Chief Election Commissioner?
options: Difference of opinion with the government
questions.explanation: The CEC can be removed only for proved misbehaviour or incapacity, like a Supreme Court judge (Art. 324(5)).

questions.question: The motion for removal of the CEC can be introduced in:
questions.explanation: As with judges, a removal motion can begin in either House of Parliament (Judges (Inquiry) Act procedure).

questions.question: Under the Constitution, the Chief Election Commissioner can be removed only in the same manner and on the same grounds as which constitutional authority?
options: A judge of the Supreme Court
questions.explanation: Art. 324(5) says the CEC is removed in the same manner and on the same grounds as a Supreme Court judge.

questions.question: The Opposition parties are gathering signatures from Members of Parliament to initiate the formal removal motion. This motion is commonly referred to as:
questions.explanation: This is a removal motion (an address for removal), not a no-confidence, adjournment or privilege motion.

questions.question: Who is the present Chief Election Commissioner of India?
questions.explanation: Gyanesh Kumar has been Chief Election Commissioner since February 2025.

questions.question: The India-AI Impact Summit 2026 was held in which city?
questions.explanation: The India-AI Impact Summit 2026 was held at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi.

sources.title: Tribune: India AI Impact Summit 2026 at Bharat Mandapam

questions.question: Which of the following is not one of the Seven Pillars of the IndiaAI Mission?
questions.explanation: The IndiaAI Mission's seven pillars are Compute, Innovation Centre, Datasets Platform, Application Development, FutureSkills, Startup Financing and Safe & Trusted AI. Defence technology is not one.

questions.question: Adi Vaani platform is primarily associated with the preservation of:
questions.explanation: Adi Vaani (Ministry of Tribal Affairs) is an AI translation platform for tribal and endangered languages such as Santali, Bhili, Mundari and Gondi.

questions.question: BHASHINI stands for which of the following?
options: Bharat Hindi Sangam Interface for National Integration
Bharatiya Heritage and Sanskriti Institute of National Importance
Bhasha Samvad Interface for National Inclusion
questions.explanation: BHASHINI stands for BHASHa INterface for India, MeitY's language-translation mission.

questions.question: Gondi language is spoken by the Gond tribal community primarily found in which Indian state?
questions.explanation: Gondi is spoken mainly in Madhya Pradesh and Chhattisgarh (also Maharashtra, Telangana and Odisha).

questions.question: Who is known as the "Father of Artificial Intelligence"?
questions.explanation: John McCarthy, who coined 'artificial intelligence' (1955–56), is called the Father of AI.

questions.question: Under the DPDPA 2023, which body is envisaged to adjudicate complaints relating to data protection violations?
options: Telecom Disputes Settlement and Appellate Tribunal (TDSAT)
questions.explanation: The DPDP Act, 2023 sets up the Data Protection Board of India to decide complaints and impose penalties.

questions.question: Under the IT Amendment Rules 2026, which category of content requires the fastest removal timeline?
questions.explanation: Under the IT Amendment Rules 2026, non-consensual intimate content, including deepfake sexual imagery, must be dealt with within 2 hours. Other flagged unlawful content gets 3 hours.

sources.title: Outlook: Centre cuts sensitive content takedown window to 2 hours

questions.question: When government uses AI chatbots on social media for citizen services, which principle must be ensured?
questions.explanation: Responsible government AI needs transparency/explainability, human review of critical decisions and non-discrimination. All three apply.

sources.title: IndiaAI: Safe and Trusted AI principles

questions.question: Which of the following are traditionally considered the five core pillars of e-governance?
options: Connectivity, Content, Capacity, Capital, Cyber Laws
questions.explanation: E-governance is usually described as resting on technology, process, people and resources, with leadership as the fifth enabler.

questions.question: Consider the following statements about the Puttaswamy judgment: 1. The judgment was unanimous — all nine judges agreed that privacy is a fundamental right. 2. The Right to Privacy was held to be absolute and cannot be restricted under any circumstances. 3. The judgment directly led to the enactment of the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023. Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Puttaswamy (2017) was a unanimous 9-judge ruling that privacy is a fundamental right. It is not absolute (restrictions must meet legality, necessity and proportionality). It led to the Srikrishna Committee and ultimately the DPDP Act, 2023.

sources.title: Wikipedia: Puttaswamy v. Union of India

questions.question: What is the name of the national digital framework launched under JJM 2.0?
questions.explanation: JJM 2.0 brings in 'Sujalam Bharat', a national digital platform that gives each village a Sujal Gaon ID and maps supply from source to tap.

sources.title: PIB: Cabinet approves extension and restructuring of JJM (Mar 2026)

questions.question: Till which year has the Jal Jeevan Mission been extended by the Union Cabinet?
questions.explanation: In March 2026 the Cabinet extended JJM to December 2028 with an outlay of about ₹8.69 lakh crore.

sources.title: Drishti IAS: Cabinet extends Jal Jeevan Mission till 2028

questions.question: Jal Jeevan Mission falls under which ministry?
questions.explanation: JJM is run by the Ministry of Jal Shakti (Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation).

questions.question: JJM 2.0 targets certification of all Gram Panchayats as:
questions.explanation: All Gram Panchayats are to be certified 'Har Ghar Jal' by December 2028.

sources.title: PMIndia: Cabinet approves extension of JJM up to December 2028

questions.question: Which organization estimated that JJM has prevented 400,000 diarrheal deaths?
questions.explanation: A WHO estimate (2023) says universal tap water under JJM could avert about 4 lakh diarrhoeal deaths.

sources.title: PIB: WHO report on JJM health impact

questions.question: The Goods and Services Tax (GST) was introduced in India through which constitutional amendment, effective from which date?
questions.explanation: GST was introduced by the Constitution (One Hundred and First Amendment) Act, 2016 and rolled out on 1 July 2017.

questions.question: The GST Council, established under Article 279A, is chaired by:
