questions.explanation: Under Art. 279A(2)(a) the Union Finance Minister is the Chairperson of the GST Council.

questions.question: In the GST Council's weighted voting mechanism (used only when consensus is not reached), what is the voting weightage of the Centre versus all States combined?
options: Centre has no vote; only States vote
questions.explanation: Art. 279A(9): the Centre's vote carries one-third weightage and all States together two-thirds; decisions need a three-fourths majority of weighted votes.

questions.question: Which mechanism under GST shifts the liability to pay tax from the supplier to the recipient of goods/services, typically applied to specified categories such as certain imports or services from unregistered persons?
questions.explanation: Under the Reverse Charge Mechanism (s.9(3)/(4) CGST Act) the recipient, not the supplier, pays the tax.

questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding the composition and structure of the GST Council: 1) The Council is a statutory body established under the Central Goods and Services Tax (CGST) Act, 2017. 2) The Vice-Chairperson of the GST Council is appointed directly by the President of India. 3) The Chairperson of the Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs (CBIC) is a permanent invitee to the Council but does not possess any voting rights. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: The Council is a constitutional body under Art. 279A (not statutory), and its Vice-Chairperson is chosen by the State members from among themselves, so 1 and 2 are wrong. The CBIC Chairperson attends as a permanent, non-voting invitee.

questions.question: Under Article 279A, the GST Council is mandated to recommend certain items for exemption from the GST levy. Which of the following items is historically excluded from the GST ambit?
questions.explanation: Art. 279A(5) keeps petroleum crude, high-speed diesel, motor spirit (petrol), natural gas and ATF out of GST until the Council recommends a date.

questions.question: How many times has a National Emergency under Article 352 been proclaimed in independent India till date?
questions.explanation: National Emergency has been proclaimed three times: 1962 (China war), 1971 (Indo-Pak war) and 1975 (internal disturbance).

sources.title: Wikipedia: State of emergency in India

questions.question: According to Article 358, which fundamental right is automatically suspended when a National Emergency is declared on the grounds of war or external aggression?
questions.explanation: Art. 358 automatically suspends Article 19 when an emergency is declared on the ground of war or external aggression.

questions.question: The term "internal disturbance" in Article 352 was replaced with "armed rebellion" by which constitutional amendment, and why?
options: 44th Amendment, 1978; to prevent misuse of emergency powers, post-1975
questions.explanation: The 44th Amendment (1978) replaced 'internal disturbance' with 'armed rebellion' to prevent misuse of Art. 352 after the 1975 Emergency.

questions.question: State Emergency, commonly known as "President's Rule", is imposed under which constitutional article?
questions.explanation: President's Rule in a State is imposed under Article 356.

questions.question: Who holds the constitutional authority to officially declare any of the three types of emergencies in India?
questions.explanation: All three emergencies (Arts. 352, 356, 360) are proclaimed by the President.

questions.question: While a National Emergency requires a special majority, what kind of majority is required by Parliament to approve a State Emergency (President's Rule) or a Financial Emergency?
questions.explanation: Proclamations under Art. 356 and Art. 360 are approved by a simple majority of each House; Art. 352 requires a special majority.

sources.title: Wikipedia: State of emergency in India

questions.question: Which state ranked 1 among "Large States" in the 4th edition of the Export Preparedness Index (EPI)?
questions.explanation: In NITI Aayog's EPI 2024 (4th edition, released 14 Jan 2026) Maharashtra ranked first among large states, followed by Tamil Nadu and Gujarat.

sources.title: Drishti IAS: Maharashtra tops NITI Aayog's EPI (Jan 2026)

questions.question: The EPI ranks states using 4 main pillars. Which pillar has the highest weightage (40%) in deciding a state's final score?
questions.explanation: EPI 2024 weights: Business Ecosystem 40%; Export Infrastructure, Policy & Governance and Export Performance 20% each.

questions.question: The EPI groups states into three performance categories. Which of the following is NOT one of those categories?
questions.explanation: EPI classifies states as Leaders, Challengers and Aspirers. 'Achievers' is not a category.

questions.question: Which Indian organization is responsible for preparing and releasing the Export Preparedness Index (EPI)?
questions.explanation: The Export Preparedness Index is prepared and released by NITI Aayog.

sources.title: Drishti IAS: Maharashtra tops NITI Aayog's EPI

questions.question: The Export Preparedness Index (EPI) 2024 is structured around 4 main pillars. How many sub-pillars and indicators are these further divided into?
questions.explanation: EPI 2024 is built on 4 pillars split into 13 sub-pillars and 70 indicators.

questions.question: Which major Middle Eastern oil producer officially left OPEC and OPEC+ in 2026?
questions.explanation: The UAE announced on 28 April 2026 that it would leave OPEC and OPEC+ with effect from 1 May 2026.

sources.title: WAM: UAE announces decision to exit OPEC & OPEC+

questions.question: The country's exit coincided with major shipping disruptions in which critical maritime route for oil?
questions.explanation: The exit came amid the Iran war and disruption to shipping through the Strait of Hormuz.

sources.title: Al Jazeera: UAE leaves OPEC in blow to oil cartel during war on Iran (28 Apr 2026)

questions.question: Which country is currently the de facto leader of OPEC and holds the largest oil production capacity within the organization?
questions.explanation: Saudi Arabia is OPEC's largest producer and its de facto leader.

questions.question: Where is the permanent headquarters of OPEC located?
questions.explanation: OPEC has been headquartered in Vienna, Austria since 1965.

questions.question: What is the primary difference between OPEC and OPEC+?
options: OPEC includes only Middle Eastern nations; OPEC+ includes all global oil exporters.
OPEC is the original organization; OPEC+ includes OPEC members plus non-OPEC countries.
OPEC is a political alliance; OPEC+ is a military alliance for protecting oil fields.
OPEC+ is a separate organization with its own headquarters in Moscow.
questions.explanation: OPEC+ (formed in 2016) is OPEC's members plus non-OPEC producers such as Russia. It has no separate headquarters.

questions.question: Which of the following countries is currently an official member of OPEC?
questions.explanation: Algeria is an OPEC member. India never was, Russia is only in OPEC+, and the UAE left on 1 May 2026.

questions.question: How is a "Super" El Niño typically differentiated from a standard event?
options: By a longer duration of rainfall.
By a higher intensity of warming.
By a smaller shift in trade winds.
By a faster speed of ocean currents.
questions.explanation: A 'super' El Niño has much stronger warming, usually Niño-3.4 anomalies around +2°C or more.

questions.question: What does the "SOI" (Southern Oscillation Index) measure?
questions.explanation: The SOI measures the difference in sea-level air pressure between Tahiti and Darwin.

questions.question: When the SOI index is strongly negative, it is usually associated with which event?
questions.explanation: A sustained negative SOI (low Tahiti pressure relative to Darwin) goes with El Niño. A positive SOI goes with La Niña.

questions.question: What is the generally observed impact of La Niña on the Indian Monsoon?
options: It tends to weaken the monsoon.
It leads to drier conditions nationwide.
It causes a total failure of the monsoon.
questions.explanation: La Niña years generally bring normal or above-normal Indian monsoon rainfall. El Niño tends to weaken it.

questions.question: Which ocean provides the primary moisture source for the Indian Summer Monsoon?
questions.explanation: The south-west monsoon draws its moisture mainly from the Indian Ocean (Arabian Sea and Bay of Bengal).

questions.question: Which of the following developments is generally regarded as the immediate trigger for the large-scale military conflict that began in February 2022?
options: Ukraine's withdrawal from the Commonwealth of Independent States
Russia's recognition of the self-proclaimed Donetsk and Luhansk People's Republics
Ukraine's formal accession to the North Atlantic Treaty Organization (NATO)
The suspension of the Minsk Agreements by the United Nations
questions.explanation: Russia recognised the 'Donetsk' and 'Luhansk People's Republics' on 21 Feb 2022 and launched the full-scale invasion on 24 Feb 2022. Ukraine has never joined NATO.

questions.question: The passage refers to maritime routes connecting enclosed regional seas with the Black Sea. Which strategic waterway best fits this description?
questions.explanation: The Kerch Strait links the enclosed Sea of Azov with the Black Sea. The Crimean Bridge built across it is the 'infrastructure' the passage mentions.

questions.question: Which of the following international institutions possesses jurisdiction to prosecute individuals for genocide, war crimes and crimes against humanity, but not States?
options: International Tribunal for the Law of the Sea
questions.explanation: The ICC (Rome Statute) tries individuals for genocide, war crimes, crimes against humanity and aggression. The ICJ decides disputes between States.

questions.question: Which one of the following countries shares a land border with both Russia and Ukraine?
questions.explanation: Belarus borders both Russia and Ukraine. Romania, Slovakia and Moldova border Ukraine but not Russia.

questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding the North Atlantic Treaty Organization (NATO): 1) It was established through the Washington Treaty. 2) Article 5 embodies the principle of collective defence. 3) Ukraine is presently a full member of NATO. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: NATO was created by the Washington (North Atlantic) Treaty of 1949, and Article 5 is the collective-defence clause. Ukraine is a partner, not a member.

questions.question: Which of the following best explains why the conflict has acquired significance far beyond Eastern Europe?
options: It has fundamentally altered the membership of the United Nations Security Council.
It has influenced global energy markets, supply chains, and debates on the effectiveness of international institutions.
It has resulted in the dissolution of the European Union's common market.
It has transferred responsibility for European security exclusively to the Organization for Security and Co- operation in Europe.
questions.explanation: The war's global significance comes from its effects on energy markets, supply chains and the credibility of international institutions. The other options are factually false.

questions.question: Which of the following constitutional principles most directly enables courts to invalidate legislative or executive action that is inconsistent with the Constitution?
questions.explanation: Judicial review (Arts. 13, 32, 226) lets courts strike down laws and executive actions that violate the Constitution.

questions.question: Which one of the following statements best captures the distinction highlighted in the passage?
options: Elections determine both governmental authority and constitutional validity.
Electoral success alone is sufficient to validate every governmental decision.
Democratic legitimacy obtained through elections remains subject to constitutional limitations.
Constitutional courts may replace elected governments whenever they disagree with public policy.
questions.explanation: The passage says electoral legitimacy remains subject to constitutional limits. Majority rule is not unlimited.

questions.question: The doctrine that prevents any organ of the State from exercising unlimited power is most closely associated with which constitutional principle?
questions.explanation: Separation of powers spreads power across the legislature, executive and judiciary so no organ holds unlimited power.

questions.question: Which one of the following landmark decisions of the Supreme Court established that certain constitutional features are beyond the amending power of Parliament?
options: A.K. Gopalan v. State of Madras
Maneka Gandhi v. Union of India
Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala
S.R. Bommai v. Union of India
questions.explanation: Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala (1973) laid down the basic structure doctrine, which limits Parliament's amending power.

sources.title: Wikipedia: Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala

questions.question: Consider the following statements: 1) Constitutionalism necessarily requires that governmental authority be exercised within legally enforceable limits. 2) A constitutional democracy may permit judicial review even when legislation has been enacted by an overwhelming legislative majority. 3) The Constitution of India permits Parliament to amend every feature of the Constitution without limitation. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements 1 and 2 describe constitutionalism correctly. Statement 3 is wrong because the basic structure cannot be amended.

sources.title: Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala (1973)

questions.question: The passage refers to archaeological surveys conducted under judicial supervision. Which statutory authority is primarily responsible for the conservation of monuments declared to be of national importance in India?
options: Indian National Trust for Art and Cultural Heritage
questions.explanation: The Archaeological Survey of India conserves monuments of national importance under the AMASR Act, 1958.

questions.question: Which of the following constitutional provisions guarantees every religious denomination the right to manage its own affairs in matters of religion, subject to public order, morality and health?
questions.explanation: Article 26 gives every religious denomination the right to manage its own affairs in matters of religion, subject to public order, morality and health.

questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding the Ancient Monuments and Archaeological Sites and Remains Act, 1958: 1) It provides for the protection of monuments declared to be of national importance. 2) It regulates construction activity within notified prohibited and regulated areas around protected monuments. 3) It authorises civil courts to determine ownership disputes relating to all religious sites. Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: The AMASR Act protects monuments of national importance and regulates construction in prohibited and regulated areas. It does not empower civil courts to decide ownership of all religious sites.

sources.title: Ancient Monuments and Archaeological Sites and Remains Act, 1958

questions.question: Bhojshala is historically associated with which of the following ruling dynasties?
questions.explanation: Bhojshala at Dhar is linked to Raja Bhoja of the Paramara dynasty of Malwa (11th century).

questions.question: Bhojshala is traditionally associated with the worship of which deity?
questions.explanation: Hindus regard Bhojshala as a temple of Goddess Saraswati (Vagdevi).

questions.question: The Places of Worship (Special Provisions) Act fixes the religious character of places of worship as it existed on:
questions.explanation: The Places of Worship (Special Provisions) Act, 1991 freezes the religious character of places of worship as it was on 15 August 1947.

sources.title: Places of Worship (Special Provisions) Act, 1991, Section 4

questions.question: The Unified Payments Interface (UPI) primarily facilitates:
questions.explanation: UPI is a real-time system for instant bank-to-bank fund transfers.

questions.question: Which organisation developed and operates the Unified Payments Interface (UPI)?
options: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology
Securities and Exchange Board of India
questions.explanation: UPI was developed and is operated by the National Payments Corporation of India (launched 2016).

questions.question: Which one of the following best explains the institutional relationship between the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) and the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI)?
options: RBI owns and directly manages NPCI as one of its statutory departments.
NPCI functions as an umbrella organisation for retail payment systems under RBI's regulatory oversight.
NPCI operates exclusively under the Ministry of Finance without RBI supervision.
RBI and NPCI exercise concurrent constitutional powers over digital payment regulation.
questions.explanation: NPCI is an umbrella body for retail payments, set up by RBI and the Indian Banks' Association under the PSS Act, 2007, and operates under RBI's regulatory oversight.

sources.title: Wikipedia: National Payments Corporation of India

questions.question: The legal framework governing payment systems in India is primarily provided under the:
questions.explanation: The Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007 is the main law regulating payment systems in India.

questions.question: Which of the following payment systems is directly operated and regulated by the Reserve Bank of India rather than the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI)?
questions.explanation: RBI itself owns and operates NEFT (and RTGS). UPI, IMPS and RuPay are run by NPCI.

questions.question: Which of the following is generally regarded as the greatest environmental concern associated with rapid expansion ethanol production?
questions.explanation: Feedstocks such as sugarcane and rice need a lot of water, so heavy freshwater use is the main environmental worry about scaling up ethanol.

sources.title: Passage on ethanol blending; NITI Aayog Roadmap for Ethanol Blending 2020-25

questions.question: Which sector is expected to receive direct economic benefit from India's ethanol blending programme?
questions.explanation: Ethanol made from sugarcane, grains and surplus produce gives farmers an extra market, so agriculture benefits directly.

questions.question: Which of the following Constitutional Amendments significantly strengthened the constitutional framework for environmental protection in India?
questions.explanation: The 42nd Amendment (1976) inserted Article 48A (DPSP) and Article 51A(g) (fundamental duty) on protecting the environment.

questions.question: Which of the following policy documents provides the principal policy framework for promoting biofuels in India?
questions.explanation: The National Policy on Biofuels (2018, amended 2022) is the main policy framework for biofuels, including the 20% ethanol target.

questions.question: India's ethanol blending programme is most directly associated with achieving which Sustainable Development Goal (SDG)?
questions.explanation: SDG 7 is affordable and clean energy, the goal ethanol blending serves most directly.

questions.question: Which of the following is generally regarded as the primary environmental advantage of ethanol blending over conventional unblended petrol?
options: Complete elimination of nitrogen oxides (NOx) and fine particulate matter
Reduction in net lifecycle carbon emissions through a closed-loop plant carbon cycle
Direct restoration of stratospheric ozone layers above urban industrial centers
Total replacement of fossil fuel dependencies across heavy commercial transit
questions.explanation: Crops reabsorb the CO2 released when ethanol burns, which cuts net lifecycle emissions. It does not eliminate NOx or particulates.

questions.question: Which gas is primarily removed from the crew cabin by the Air Revitalisation System (ARS) in Gaganyaan mission to prevent suffocation?
questions.explanation: The Air Revitalisation System scrubs exhaled carbon dioxide so it cannot build up to toxic levels in the cabin.

sources.title: IASGyan: How does Gaganyaan's life-support system operate? (May 2026)

questions.question: The Gaganyaan ECLSS operates as an "open-loop" system. What does this design choice specifically imply regarding mission resources?
options: Cabin atmosphere is continuously vented and replenished with fresh gas from exterior storage tanks.
Consumables such as oxygen and water are carried from Earth without onboard recycling.
Biological processes such as onboard algae bioreactors are used to synthesize breathable oxygen.
Waste products are converted back into usable drinking water through an advanced electrochemical loop.
questions.explanation: Open-loop means oxygen, water and other consumables are carried from Earth and waste is stored, with no on-board regeneration. That suits a short mission.

sources.title: IASGyan: How does Gaganyaan's life-support system operate?

questions.question: Under nominal operating conditions, what is the composition of the primary breathing gas mixture inside the Gaganyaan Crew Module?
questions.explanation: The crew module keeps a sea-level-equivalent pressure of about 101.3 kPa with an Earth-like nitrogen–oxygen mix, not pure oxygen (which is a fire hazard).

sources.title: IASGyan: How does Gaganyaan's life-support system operate?

questions.question: Which chemical compound is primarily utilized in the Gaganyaan Air Revitalisation System to scrub exhaled Carbon Dioxide (CO2)?
questions.explanation: Lithium hydroxide canisters absorb CO2 in Gaganyaan's ARS, which the crew replaces roughly every 20–24 hours.

sources.title: IAF GLEX-2025 paper on Gaganyaan ARS

questions.question: Which of the following organisations is primarily responsible for developing the Environmental Control and Life Support System (ECLSS) for India's Gaganyaan mission?
questions.explanation: ISRO (Vikram Sarabhai Space Centre) is developing the ECLSS for Gaganyaan.

questions.question: Which of the following is the primary objective of a spacecraft's life support system?
options: Increasing the payload capacity of the launch vehicle.
Maintaining environmental conditions necessary for human survival.
Enhancing satellite communication with ground stations.
questions.explanation: A life-support system exists to maintain the pressure, air, temperature and humidity humans need to survive.

questions.question: According to the Treaty of Sugauli (1816), which geographical feature was designated as the western boundary between Nepal and British India?
options: The Mechi River originating from the eastern Himalayan range
The Kali (Mahakali) River flowing through the western Himalayan border
The Gandak River defining the southern plains of the Terai region
The Kosi River serving as a natural boundary across eastern Nepal
questions.explanation: The Treaty of Sugauli (1815–16) made the Kali (Mahakali) river Nepal's western boundary with British India. The Mechi is the eastern one.

questions.question: Which specific geographical corridor in India is shielded by the strategic presence and stability of Nepal as a buffer state?
questions.explanation: Nepal lies just west of the narrow Siliguri Corridor ('Chicken's Neck') that links north-east India to the rest of the country.

questions.question: What is the official name of the annual joint military exercise conducted between the Indian Army and the Nepalese Army?
questions.explanation: Surya Kiran is the India–Nepal army exercise. Mitra Shakti is with Sri Lanka, Sampriti with Bangladesh and Yudh Abhyas with the USA.

questions.question: Which Indian state does NOT share a border with Nepal?
questions.explanation: Uttarakhand, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, West Bengal and Sikkim border Nepal. Odisha does not.

questions.question: Which Indian foreign policy initiative emphasizes strengthening relations with neighbouring countries, including Nepal?
questions.explanation: India's Neighbourhood First Policy prioritises relations with immediate neighbours such as Nepal.

questions.question: Who became the Prime Minister of Nepal following the 2026 general election?
questions.explanation: After the Rastriya Swatantra Party's sweeping win in the 5 March 2026 election, Balendra (Balen) Shah was sworn in as Prime Minister on 27 March 2026.

sources.title: SCMP: Balendra Shah sworn in as Nepal's prime minister

questions.question: Under which Constitutional provision does Parliament enact laws relating to the readjustment of constituencies after each Census?
questions.explanation: Article 82 provides for readjustment of Lok Sabha seats and constituencies after each Census, by an authority set up under a law of Parliament.

questions.question: Can the orders issued by the Delimitation Commission be challenged or modified in a court of law?
options: Yes, directly in the Supreme Court
No, its orders have the force of law and cannot be questioned in any court
Yes, but only by a petition from the State Governor
questions.explanation: Delimitation Commission orders have the force of law and cannot be challenged in any court (Art. 329(a); Delimitation Act, 2002).

questions.question: What is the primary factor used to determine how constituency boundaries are redrawn during a delimitation exercise?
options: The total geographical land area of a state
Population data collected during the official Census
The economic revenue generated by a state
The total number of registered voters in a single political party
questions.explanation: Constituency boundaries are redrawn using population figures from the Census.

questions.question: Who appoints the Delimitation Commission in India?
options: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha
questions.explanation: The President appoints the Delimitation Commission, which works with the Election Commission.

questions.question: For how long will the reservation of seats for women remain in force from the date of its implementation, unless extended by Parliament?
questions.explanation: Article 334A keeps women's reservation in force for 15 years from commencement, and Parliament can extend it by law.

questions.question: Which Constitutional Amendment Act passed in 2023 provides 33% reservation for women in the Lok Sabha, State Legislative Assemblies, and the Legislative Assembly of NCT of Delhi?
questions.explanation: The Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam is the Constitution (106th Amendment) Act, 2023.

questions.question: What is the primary rationale behind the launch of the National Critical Minerals Mission by the Government of India?
options: Complete nationalization of all rare earth processing plants under state-owned enterprises.
Securing domestic and international supply chains for green transition technology and defense applications.
Halting the export of iron ore and coal to prioritize domestic heavy industrial production.
Subsidizing foreign mining companies to extract industrial sand along Indian coastal regions.
questions.explanation: The National Critical Mineral Mission (approved January 2025) aims to secure domestic and overseas supply chains of critical minerals for clean energy and defence.

sources.title: PIB: National Critical Mineral Mission approved (Jan 2025)

questions.question: The region known as the "Lithium Triangle," which holds over half of the world's identified lithium brine resources, is located across which three South American nations?
questions.explanation: The Lithium Triangle lies across Argentina, Bolivia and Chile.

questions.question: Rare Earth Elements (REEs) are primarily valued because of their importance in the manufacture of: 1) Permanent magnets 2) Wind turbines 3) Electric vehicle motors 4) Advanced defence equipment Select the correct answer.
questions.explanation: Rare earths go into permanent magnets, which are used in wind turbines, EV motors and defence systems, so all four apply.

questions.question: Which specialized Indian Joint Venture company was formed under the Ministry of Mines to acquire strategic mineral assets like Lithium and Cobalt in foreign countries?
questions.explanation: KABIL (a JV of NALCO, HCL and MECL) acquires strategic minerals such as lithium and cobalt abroad.

questions.question: How many chemical elements are officially classified together as Rare Earth Elements (REEs)?
questions.explanation: There are 17 rare earth elements: the 15 lanthanides plus scandium and yttrium.

questions.question: Which organization developed and operates the Unified Payments Interface (UPI) in India?
questions.explanation: UPI was developed by, and is operated by, NPCI.

questions.question: Which version of UPI is designed as an on-device wallet to process small transactions (below ₹1,000) quickly without needing a UPI PIN?
questions.explanation: UPI LITE is an on-device wallet for small payments (up to ₹1,000 per transaction) that needs no UPI PIN.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of the "UPI One World" initiative?
options: To allow cash withdrawals at local kirana shops
To enable foreign nationals and NRIs arriving in India to make UPI payments
To eliminate transaction limits for corporate businesses
To process offline transactions in deep rural areas
questions.explanation: UPI One World is a prepaid-wallet facility that lets foreign nationals and NRIs visiting India pay via UPI.

questions.question: The dominance of applications such as PhonePe and Google Pay mainly raises concerns regarding:
questions.explanation: PhonePe and Google Pay together handle the bulk of UPI volume, which raises market-concentration concerns (hence NPCI's proposed 30% market cap).

questions.question: The legal framework governing NPCI-operated payment systems is primarily provided under the:
questions.explanation: NPCI's payment systems are authorised and regulated under the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007.

questions.question: The judge strength of the Supreme Court was last increased from 30 to 33, excluding the Chief Justice of India, through:
options: Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Amendment Act, 2008
Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Amendment Act, 2014
Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Amendment Act, 2019
Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Amendment Act, 2022
questions.explanation: The Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Amendment Act, 2019 raised the sanctioned strength from 30 to 33 judges, excluding the CJI.

sources.title: Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Amendment Act, 2019

questions.question: With reference to increasing the sanctioned strength of judges of the Supreme Court, which one of the following correctly describes the majority required in Parliament to amend the relevant law?
options: It requires a simple majority of members present and voting in each House of Parliament, as it involves ordinary legislation.
It requires a special majority of the total membership of each House and two-thirds of members present and voting.
It requires a two-thirds majority of the total membership of Parliament in a joint sitting of both Houses.
It requires a special majority in Parliament followed by ratification by at least half of the State Legislatures.
questions.explanation: Under Art. 124(1) Parliament fixes the number of judges by ordinary law (Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Act, 1956), so a simple majority is enough.

questions.question: Under the Constitution of India, who formally appoints the judges of the Supreme Court?
questions.explanation: Under Art. 124(2) the President appoints Supreme Court judges, in practice on the collegium's recommendation.

questions.question: What is the retirement age of a judge of the Supreme Court of India?
questions.explanation: Supreme Court judges retire at 65 (Art. 124(2)). High Court judges retire at 62.

questions.question: Which one of the following correctly identifies the constitutional provisions relating to three important jurisdictions of the Supreme Court?
options: Article 131 — original jurisdiction; Article 136 — special leave jurisdiction; Article 143 — advisory jurisdiction.
Article 129 — original jurisdiction; Article 131 — advisory jurisdiction; Article 143 — appellate jurisdiction.
Article 130 — original jurisdiction; Article 136 — advisory jurisdiction; Article 143 — contempt jurisdiction.
Article 131 — advisory jurisdiction; Article 136 — original jurisdiction; Article 143 — special leave jurisdiction.
questions.explanation: Art. 131 is original jurisdiction, Art. 136 is special leave to appeal, and Art. 143 is advisory jurisdiction.

questions.question: Which one of the following correctly describes the constitutional procedure for removal of a Supreme Court judge?
options: The President may remove a judge directly after receiving a recommendation from the Chief Justice of India on grounds of proved misbehaviour or incapacity.
Parliament may remove a judge by ordinary majority in both Houses, following which the President issues the formal removal order.
The President removes the judge after an address by both Houses of Parliament supported by the constitutionally prescribed special majority.
The Supreme Court Collegium may recommend removal of a judge, after which Parliament confirms the recommendation through a simple majority.
questions.explanation: Under Art. 124(4) the President removes a judge after an address by each House passed by a special majority (majority of total membership and two-thirds of those present and voting).

questions.question: With reference to India–Canada relations during the 2026 G7 Summit, which one of the following is correct?
options: India and Canada agreed to conclude their Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement by the end of 2026.
India and Canada agreed to establish a bilateral investment treaty before beginning CEPA negotiations.
India and Canada announced a target of completing their free trade agreement negotiations by the end of 2027.
India and Canada decided to replace CEPA negotiations with a limited preferential trade agreement framework.
questions.explanation: When Modi and Carney met at the Évian G7 on 16 June 2026, they reaffirmed the aim of concluding CEPA negotiations in 2026.

questions.question: Approximately what share of the world's population and nominal GDP is accounted for by the G7 economies collectively?
options: About 10% of global population and approximately 43% of global nominal GDP.
About 20% of global population and approximately 43% of global nominal GDP.
About 10% of global population and approximately 30% of global nominal GDP.
About 15% of global population and approximately 50% of global nominal GDP.
questions.explanation: The G7 has about 10% of the world's population but roughly 43–45% of global nominal GDP.

questions.question: Which one of the following correctly describes the institutional nature of the G7?
options: It is an informal grouping without a treaty-based foundation, permanent secretariat or headquarters.
It is a treaty-based organisation with a permanent secretariat and headquarters located in Brussels.
It is a formal grouping with treaty- based foundation, without a permanent secretariat or headquarters.
It is an economic organisation headquartered in Paris with a permanent administrative bureaucracy and headquarters.
questions.explanation: The G7 is an informal forum with no founding treaty, permanent secretariat or headquarters. The presidency rotates every year.

questions.question: The next G7 Summit after the 2026 Évian Summit is scheduled to be hosted by which of the following countries?
questions.explanation: The presidency rotation runs Canada (2025), France (2026, Évian), then the United States (2027).

questions.question: Under the Constitution of India, "education" is a subject in which List?
questions.explanation: Education has been in the Concurrent List (Entry 25, List III) since the 42nd Amendment (1976) moved it from the State List.

sources.title: Constitution of India, Seventh Schedule, List III Entry 25

questions.question: The acronym ULLAS, used in the context of the New India Literacy Programme, stands for:
options: Understanding of Lifelong Learning for All in Society
Universal Learning and Literacy Advancement Scheme
Understanding of Language, Learning and Academic Skills
Universal Literacy and Lifelong Advancement for Society
questions.explanation: ULLAS stands for Understanding of Lifelong Learning for All in Society, the name of the New India Literacy Programme.

questions.question: ULLAS – New India Literacy Programme is classified as:
options: A Centrally Sponsored Scheme implemented through Centre-State cooperation
A Central Sector Scheme implemented entirely through the Union Government
A CSS implemented exclusively through local self-government institutions
A centrally funded programme implemented by the Ministry of Skill Development
questions.explanation: ULLAS (2022–27) is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme implemented jointly by the Centre and the States/UTs.

questions.question: ULLAS – New India Literacy Programme is administered by which of the following?
options: Department of School Education and Literacy under the Ministry of Education
Department of Higher Education under the Ministry of Education
Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship through the National Skill Mission
Ministry of Rural Development through the National Rural Livelihood Mission
questions.explanation: The Department of School Education and Literacy, Ministry of Education administers ULLAS.

questions.question: Which of the following platforms is specifically associated with registration and progress tracking under ULLAS?
options: SWAYAM and e-Shram, along with the National Scholarship Portal
DigiLocker and UMANG, along with the National Career Service portal
Mobile App and Portal, along with the DIKSHA platform
PM GatiShakti and GeM, along with the National Apprenticeship Portal
questions.explanation: Learners and volunteers register and track progress on the ULLAS mobile app and portal, with content on DIKSHA.

questions.question: Which one of the following is the most appropriate objective of the ULLAS scheme?
options: To provide literacy, numeracy and relevant life skills to adults who missed formal schooling.
To provide universal secondary education to children through expansion of government schools.
To provide higher education scholarships to adults who have completed foundational literacy.
To provide exclusively vocational training to unemployed youth in rural and semi-urban areas.
questions.explanation: ULLAS gives adults aged 15+ who missed school foundational literacy, numeracy and critical life skills.

questions.question: Where will the NEXT Commonwealth Games (2030) be held?
questions.explanation: Ahmedabad, India was confirmed as host of the 2030 (centenary) Commonwealth Games.

questions.question: Which of the following was NOT among the 10 sports at Glasgow 2026?
questions.explanation: Glasgow 2026's 10 sports were athletics, swimming, artistic gymnastics, track cycling, netball, weightlifting, boxing, judo, bowls and 3x3 basketball. Hockey was dropped.

questions.question: Which two sports have traditionally been India's biggest medal-winners at the Commonwealth Games?
questions.explanation: Shooting and wrestling have historically brought India its largest Commonwealth Games medal hauls.

sources.title: Wikipedia: India at the Commonwealth Games

questions.question: Where were the FIRST Commonwealth Games held?
questions.explanation: The first Games, the 1930 British Empire Games, were held in Hamilton, Canada.

questions.question: At the Glasgow 2026 Commonwealth Games, India finished at which position in the overall medal table?
questions.explanation: India finished 4th at Glasgow 2026 with 39 medals (13 gold, 17 silver, 9 bronze), behind Australia, England and Canada.

sources.title: Free Press Journal: India jump to 4th, total 39

questions.question: Which Indian athlete became the FIRST to win TWO medals at a single Commonwealth Games edition (at Glasgow 2026)?
questions.explanation: Gulveer Singh won silver in the 10,000 m and bronze in the 5,000 m at Glasgow 2026, the only Indian with two medals at those Games. The question's wording 'first ever' overstates it; read it as within Indian athletics.

sources.title: The Bridge: Seven boxing golds, Gulveer Singh history

questions.question: What was the primary motivation behind chartering the steamship during this historical voyage?
options: To establish a commercial trading route and facilitate labor migration across British dominions
To challenge exclusionary immigration laws requiring continuous travel from one's native country
To transport political dissidents and armed revolutionaries directly to South Asian ports
To provide humanitarian assistance and economic relief to stranded overseas Indian workers
questions.explanation: Baba Gurdit Singh chartered the Komagata Maru (1914) to challenge Canada's 'continuous journey' regulation, which in practice barred Indian immigrants.

questions.question: The Komagata Maru passengers were predominantly immigrants from which region of India?
questions.explanation: Almost all of the 376 passengers were from Punjab, mostly Sikhs.

questions.question: Under what name was the transnational revolutionary movement in North America originally established in 1913?
questions.explanation: The Ghadar Party was founded in 1913 as the Pacific Coast Hindustan Association.

questions.question: The Komagata Maru ship, whose passengers were fired upon at Budge Budge near Kolkata in 1914, had originally sailed from which of the following places?
questions.explanation: The Komagata Maru sailed from Hong Kong (via Shanghai and Yokohama) to Vancouver. On its return, passengers were fired on at Budge Budge.

questions.question: Who was the founding President of the Ghadar Party, originally established as the Pacific Coast Hindustan Association?
questions.explanation: Sohan Singh Bhakna was the founding President, and Lala Har Dayal was the General Secretary and main ideologue. (The Mock 26 key prints option (d), but its own explanation names Sohan Singh Bhakna, which is option (b).)

questions.question: Which slogan prominently appeared on the masthead of the weekly newspaper published by the movement?
questions.explanation: The Ghadar weekly's masthead carried the slogan 'Angrezi Raj ka Dushman' (Enemy of the British Raj). (The Mock 26 key prints (d), but its explanation names this slogan, which is option (b).)

questions.question: The treaty that fixed Nepal's boundary along the course of a river, and is at the centre of the dispute, was ratified in which year?
questions.explanation: The Treaty of Sugauli was signed in December 1815 and ratified in March 1816. It fixed the Kali (Mahakali) as Nepal's western boundary.

questions.question: Lipulekh Pass is situated near the disputed trijunction involving which three countries?
questions.explanation: Lipulekh Pass is near the India–Nepal–China (Tibet) trijunction in the Kalapani area.

questions.question: The river whose course the treaty fixed as the boundary is the:
questions.explanation: The Sugauli Treaty made the Kali (Mahakali) river the boundary. Its source is at the heart of the Kalapani–Lipulekh dispute.

questions.question: Apart from Lipulekh Pass, which route in Sikkim is the other gateway announced for the 2026 Kailash Mansarovar Yatra?
questions.explanation: The Kailash Mansarovar Yatra runs through two routes: Lipulekh Pass (Uttarakhand) and Nathu La (Sikkim).

questions.question: The organisation under which the Kailash Mansarovar Yatra is administered/organised by the Government of India is the:
questions.explanation: The Ministry of External Affairs organises the Kailash Mansarovar Yatra.

questions.question: Which of the following pairs correctly identifies two Indian Ramsar sites currently on the Montreux Record (the register of wetlands facing significant ecological stress)?
options: Keoladeo National Park and Loktak Lake
East Kolkata Wetlands and Kolleru Lake
questions.explanation: India's Montreux Record sites are Keoladeo National Park (Rajasthan) and Loktak Lake (Manipur). Chilika was removed in 2002.

questions.question: The designation of Surha Tal took India’s tally of Ramsar sites to one hundred. Which state has the largest number of Ramsar sites?
questions.explanation: Tamil Nadu has the most Ramsar sites of any Indian state (about 20).

sources.title: Adda247: Ramsar sites in India 2026, state-wise list

questions.question: Surha Tal is best described as which type of wetland?
options: A freshwater lake sustaining a rich bird population
questions.explanation: Surha Tal (Ballia, Uttar Pradesh) is a natural freshwater oxbow lake and bird sanctuary that supports many migratory and resident birds.

sources.title: Drishti IAS: Glaw Lake becomes India's 101st Ramsar site

questions.question: The announcement of India's 100th Ramsar site, made by the Prime Minister on 5 June 2026, coincided with the observance of:
questions.explanation: 5 June is World Environment Day. World Wetlands Day is 2 February.

questions.question: Which wetland became India's 101st Ramsar site (and the first from its state) shortly after the 100th?
questions.explanation: Glaw Lake in Kamlang Tiger Reserve became India's 101st Ramsar site in August 2026, Arunachal Pradesh's first.

sources.title: News on AIR: Glaw Lake designated India's 101st Ramsar site

questions.question: The Ramsar Convention, signed in 1971, takes its name from a city in which country?
questions.explanation: The Ramsar Convention was signed in 1971 at Ramsar, Iran.

questions.question: Which combination correctly represents the ocean-atmosphere conditions generally associated with El Niño?
options: Stronger easterly trade winds and increased upwelling in the eastern Pacific
Weaker easterly trade winds and reduced upwelling in the eastern Pacific
Stronger westerly winds and cooling of the entire Indian Ocean
Weaker trade winds and increased upwelling near the Peruvian coast
questions.explanation: During El Niño the easterly trade winds weaken and upwelling of cold water off South America drops, so the eastern Pacific warms.

questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes a positive Indian Ocean Dipole?
options: Warmer western Indian Ocean and cooler eastern Indian Ocean
Cooler western Indian Ocean and warmer eastern Indian Ocean
Equal cooling of the Arabian Sea and Bay of Bengal
Warming limited to the southern Indian Ocean
questions.explanation: A positive Indian Ocean Dipole means a warmer western Indian Ocean and a cooler eastern Indian Ocean.

questions.question: Under India’s flexible inflation-targeting framework for April 2026–March 2031, which combination is correct?
options: Inflation target of 2%, with a tolerance range of 1–3%
Inflation target of 4%, with a tolerance range of 2–6%
Inflation target of 5%, with a tolerance range of 3–7%
Inflation target of 6%, with a tolerance range of 4–8%
questions.explanation: A gazette notification of 25 March 2026 kept the CPI inflation target at 4% with a 2–6% band for April 2026 to March 2031 (s.45ZA, RBI Act).

sources.title: Business Today: Govt retains inflation target at 4% with 2–6% band

questions.question: Why does stagflation challenge the conventional short-run Phillips Curve?
options: Inflation and unemployment can rise together
Inflation and unemployment always move inversely
Inflation rises only with higher employment
questions.explanation: The short-run Phillips curve predicts an inverse link between inflation and unemployment. Stagflation is both rising together.

questions.question: Consider the following responses by food manufacturers to an El Niño-related increase in raw-material costs: 1. A company reduces the weight of a biscuit packet but retains the same price. 2. A company retains the product’s weight and price but substitutes lower-quality ingredients. Which of the following correctly identifies these practices?
options: Statement 1 is shrinkflation; Statement 2 is skimpflation
Statement 1 is skimpflation; Statement 2 is shrinkflation
questions.explanation: Cutting quantity at the same price is shrinkflation. Cutting quality at the same price is skimpflation.

questions.question: At the 3rd India–Nordic Summit held in 2026, the leaders elevated their bilateral-plurilateral relationship to which strategic framework?
options: Green Technology and Innovation Strategic Partnership
questions.explanation: At the 3rd India–Nordic Summit (Oslo, 19 May 2026) ties were raised to a Green Technology and Innovation Strategic Partnership.

sources.title: Tribune: India, Nordic nations elevate ties to Green Technology and Innovation Strategic Partnership

questions.question: Which of the following correctly matches the India–Nordic Summit with its host city?
questions.explanation: The summits were held in Stockholm (2018), Copenhagen (2022) and Oslo (2026). The 4th will be hosted by Finland.

questions.question: Which set of countries constitutes the Nordic group that participates in the India–Nordic Summit?
options: Denmark, Finland, Norway, Sweden, and Estonia
Denmark, Finland, Iceland, Norway, and Sweden
Sweden, Norway, Finland, Iceland, and Ireland
Denmark, Sweden, Norway, Netherlands, and Finland
questions.explanation: The Nordic countries are Denmark, Finland, Iceland, Norway and Sweden.

questions.question: Which two Nordic countries are members of the European Free Trade Association but not members of the European Union?
questions.explanation: Iceland and Norway are EFTA members outside the EU. Denmark, Finland and Sweden are EU members.

questions.question: Which of the following correctly matches Nordic countries with the capabilities highlighted during the summit?
options: Iceland—advanced manufacturing; Norway—health technology; Finland—Arctic fisheries
questions.explanation: The usual pairings are Iceland with geothermal energy, Norway with the blue/maritime economy and Finland with telecommunications (Nokia, 6G).

questions.question: Nordic companies were invited to establish a presence in GIFT City. In which state is GIFT City located?
questions.explanation: GIFT City (Gujarat International Finance Tec-City) is in Gandhinagar, Gujarat.

questions.question: Which one of the following best describes the institutional emphasis of the VB-G RAM G Act?
options: Greater role for Gram Panchayats in participatory planning and asset creation
Greater role for District Collectors in centrally designed rural employment projects
Greater role for private firms in managing village-level employment programmes
Greater role for State departments in directly allocating employment to rural households
questions.explanation: The VB-G RAM G Act puts Gram Panchayats at the centre, through Viksit Gram Panchayat Plans for participatory planning and asset creation.

sources.title: Viksit Bharat – Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin) Act, 2025

questions.question: Which one of the following correctly identifies the Union Minister who is scheduled to formally launch the VB- G RAM G Mission nationally?
questions.explanation: Union Rural Development Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan announced and led the national launch from Andhra Pradesh on 1 July 2026. Pawan Kalyan is AP's Deputy CM, not a Union Minister.

sources.title: News on AIR: VB-G RAM G to be launched in Andhra Pradesh on July 1

questions.question: Under the VB-G RAM G Act, 2025, what is the Centre–State fund-sharing ratio for States and Union Territories with a legislature, other than the North-Eastern and Himalayan States?
questions.explanation: For most States and UTs with a legislature, costs are shared 60:40 between Centre and State. NE and Himalayan States share 90:10.

sources.title: Viksit Bharat – G RAM G Act, 2025 (fund-sharing)

questions.question: Which one of the following is NOT among the four major thematic areas of works under the Viksit Bharat–G RAM G Act, 2025?
questions.explanation: The four thematic areas are water security, core rural infrastructure, livelihood-related infrastructure and mitigation of extreme weather events. Rural financial inclusion is not one of them.

sources.title: Viksit Bharat – G RAM G Act, 2025 (Schedule of works)

questions.question: The Viksit Gram Panchayat Plans under the VB-G RAM G framework are integrated with:
options: PM Gati Shakti, GIS and digital platforms
PM-KISAN, e-NAM and National Career Service
DigiLocker, UMANG and National Health Digital Mission
questions.explanation: Viksit Gram Panchayat Plans are integrated with PM Gati Shakti and GIS-based digital platforms.

sources.title: Viksit Bharat – G RAM G Act, 2025

questions.question: The VB–G RAM G Act, 2025 shall come into force in which of the following areas?
options: All urban and rural areas of India
Only rural areas of selected States
questions.explanation: The Act, which replaced MGNREGA, came into force across all rural areas of India on 1 July 2026.

sources.title: Swarajya: Centre to launch VB-G RAM G from Andhra Pradesh on 1 July

questions.question: According to the UN Sustainable Development Goals (SDG) Index 2026, what is India's overall rank and score out of 169 countries?
questions.explanation: In the Sustainable Development Report 2026 India ranked 94th with a score of 68.3, its best ever (99th in 2025). Most reports give 167 countries; the question says 169.

sources.title: Drishti IAS: India ranks 94th in UN SDG Index 2026

questions.question: According to the key findings, which Sustainable Development Goal represents India's most critical development challenge, impacted heavily by child stunting and wasting?
questions.explanation: SDG 2 (Zero Hunger) is India's biggest challenge, driven by child stunting, wasting and undernourishment.

sources.title: Down To Earth: India climbs to highest-ever rank but hunger remains a major challenge

questions.question: Which country secured the top position in the global SDG Index 2026?
questions.explanation: Finland tops the 2026 SDG Index, ahead of Sweden and Denmark.

sources.title: Vajiram & Ravi: UN Sustainable Development Report 2026

questions.question: Which of the following best captures India’s position according to the SDG Index 2026?
options: India improved its ranking but remains behind several South Asian countries.
India achieved the highest SDG ranking among all South Asian countries.
India’s ranking declined despite improvements in sustainable development.
India has more than half of its SDG targets on track for 2030.
questions.explanation: India rose to 94th but still trails Bhutan, Maldives, Nepal and Sri Lanka in South Asia. Only about a third of its SDG targets are on track.

sources.title: Drishti IAS: India ranks 94th in UN SDG Index 2026

questions.question: In India, the nodal agency responsible for national-level monitoring and reporting on the MDGs — and later for the SDG National Indicator Framework — has been:
options: The Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation
questions.explanation: MoSPI was the nodal agency for MDG monitoring and maintains the SDG National Indicator Framework. NITI Aayog coordinates SDG implementation.

questions.question: The Millennium Development Goals comprised:
questions.explanation: The MDGs (2000–2015) had 8 goals and 21 targets. The SDGs have 17 goals and 169 targets.

questions.question: Who has been selected as the recipient of the 60th Jnanpith Award?
questions.explanation: Tamil poet-lyricist R. Vairamuthu was named the 60th Jnanpith laureate (for 2025) on 14 March 2026.

sources.title: Tribune: Tamil poet Vairamuthu wins 60th Jnanpith Award

questions.question: Who among the following was the first woman to receive the Jnanpith Award?
questions.explanation: Ashapurna Devi (Bengali) was the first woman to receive the Jnanpith, in 1976.

questions.question: The Jnanpith Award covers which of the following languages?
questions.explanation: The Jnanpith covers the 22 Eighth Schedule languages plus English (English added in 2013).

questions.question: The 60th Jnanpith Award was conferred upon a poet, who is a renowned writer in which language?
questions.explanation: Vairamuthu writes in Tamil. He is the third Tamil Jnanpith winner, after Akilan (1975) and Jayakanthan (2002).

sources.title: Tribune: Tamil poet Vairamuthu wins 60th Jnanpith Award

questions.question: What are the cash prize amount and the statutory trophy presented to the winner of the Jnanpith Award?
options: ₹15 lakh cash prize and a silver miniature of the Lotus Temple
₹11 lakh cash prize and a bronze statuette of Vagdevi Saraswati
₹25 lakh cash prize and a gold medallion of the Sun Temple
₹5 lakh cash prize and a brass emblem of Ashoka Chakra
questions.explanation: The award carries ₹11 lakh, a citation and a bronze statuette of Vagdevi (Saraswati).

questions.question: The Jnanpith Award was instituted in which year, and the first award conferred in which year?
questions.explanation: Bharatiya Jnanpith instituted the award in 1961. The first award went to G. Sankara Kurup in 1965.

questions.question: Ladakh's transition to a Union Territory without a legislature in 2019 took place under which one of the following enactments?
questions.explanation: The Jammu and Kashmir Reorganisation Act, 2019 created the UT of Ladakh (no legislature) from 31 October 2019.

sources.title: Wikipedia: Jammu and Kashmir Reorganisation Act, 2019

questions.question: The Sixth Schedule under Article 244(2) provides Autonomous District Councils for tribal areas of which one of the following groups of states?
options: Nagaland, Tripura, Mizoram and Arunachal Pradesh
questions.explanation: The Sixth Schedule covers tribal areas of Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram.

questions.question: Laws enacted by an Autonomous District Council on subjects such as land, forests and social customs take effect only after receiving the assent of:
options: The Chief Minister of the State
The Speaker of the Legislative Assembly
questions.explanation: Under para 3(3) of the Sixth Schedule, laws made by a District Council take effect only after the Governor's assent.

sources.title: Constitution of India, Sixth Schedule, para 3(3)

questions.question: Which one of the following sets of Union Territories at present has its own elected legislature?
questions.explanation: Only Delhi, Puducherry and Jammu & Kashmir have elected legislatures. Ladakh and Chandigarh do not.

questions.question: The special constitutional provisions relating to the National Capital Territory of Delhi were inserted by which one of the following Constitutional Amendments?
questions.explanation: The 69th Amendment Act, 1991 inserted Articles 239AA and 239AB on the NCT of Delhi.

questions.question: The "Samvidhan Hatya Divas" observed by the Government of India commemorates which one of the following events?
options: The adoption of the Constitution by the Constituent Assembly on 26 November 1949
The proclamation of the national Emergency on the night of 25 June 1975
The imposition of President's Rule in a state under Article 356 in 1977
The enactment of the First Amendment to the Constitution in 1951
questions.explanation: Samvidhan Hatya Diwas (notified in 2024) is observed on 25 June to mark the proclamation of the Emergency in 1975.

sources.title: News on AIR: Samvidhaan Hatya Diwas observed

questions.question: The national Emergency was proclaimed under which one of the following Articles of the Constitution, on which ground?
options: Article 352 — on the ground of "internal disturbance"
Article 356 — on the ground of failure of constitutional machinery
Article 360 — on the ground of a threat to the financial stability of India
Article 365 — on the ground of non-compliance with directions of the Union
questions.explanation: The 1975 Emergency was proclaimed under Article 352 on the ground of 'internal disturbance'.

questions.question: Which one of the following Constitutional Amendments, passed during the Emergency, is popularly called the "Mini-Constitution"?
questions.explanation: The 42nd Amendment Act, 1976 is called the 'Mini-Constitution' because of its sweeping changes.

sources.title: Wikipedia: Forty-second Amendment of the Constitution of India

questions.question: Who was the President of India who signed the proclamation of Emergency on 25 June 1975?
questions.explanation: President Fakhruddin Ali Ahmed signed the proclamation on the night of 25 June 1975.

questions.question: The Preventive Detention law under which thousands of political leaders and activists were detained during the Emergency was:
options: The Terrorist and Disruptive Activities Act, 1987
The Maintenance of Internal Security Act, 1971
questions.explanation: Thousands of opposition leaders were detained under the Maintenance of Internal Security Act (MISA), 1971.

sources.title: Wikipedia: Maintenance of Internal Security Act

questions.question: The national commemoration of the 50th anniversary of the Emergency (2024–2026) has been organised by which one of the following Union Ministries?
questions.explanation: The Ministry of Culture ran the year-long 50th-anniversary commemoration (25 Jun 2025 – 25 Jun 2026). The MHA had notified the Diwas itself.

sources.title: ThePrint: Ministry of Culture plans year-long commemorative events

questions.question: The Makkah Joint Defence Agreement was signed between which one of the following groups of countries?
options: United Arab Emirates, Türkiye and Pakistan
questions.explanation: Saudi Arabia, Türkiye and Pakistan signed the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement in Makkah on 7 August 2026.

sources.title: Arab News: Saudi Arabia, Türkiye and Pakistan sign Makkah Joint Defense Agreement

questions.question: The central principle of the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement, as stated in the pact, is:
options: An arms embargo against any country that attacks one of the members
An armed attack on one member will be treated as an attack on all three
Free trade, energy and investment cooperation among the member states
A joint nuclear deterrent placed under a single unified command
questions.explanation: The pact treats an armed attack on any one signatory as an attack on all three.

sources.title: Arab News: Makkah Joint Defence Agreement treats attack on one as attack on all three

questions.question: Besides the Strait of Hormuz, which one of the following chokepoints is as a risk to Saudi Arabia's energy infrastructure?
questions.explanation: Bab-el-Mandeb at the mouth of the Red Sea, where the Houthis attack shipping, is the other key chokepoint for Saudi energy exports.

questions.question: The Houthi attacks threatening Saudi Arabia are associated with which one of the following countries?
questions.explanation: The Houthis (Ansar Allah) are a Yemeni movement.

questions.question: Which of the following was the primary cause of the 2026 floods in Nepal?
options: Sudden failure of a natural landslide dam formed across the Karnali River in western Nepal
Sudden glacial/ice-related water surge in a Himalayan river system in Nepal border.
Breach of the Koshi Barrage following exceptionally heavy monsoon rainfall in eastern Nepal
Failure of a major hydropower reservoir in the Trishuli basin, releasing a large volume of stored water
questions.explanation: The late-August 2026 Bhote Koshi flood came from an ice-avalanche-triggered collapse of a supraglacial lake in Tibet, which sent a glacial surge down the river into Nepal. It was not a landslide dam, barrage or reservoir failure.

sources.title: PreventionWeb: When a mountain falls – how ice and rock triggered Nepal's catastrophic flood

questions.question: With reference to the international response to the 2026 Nepal floods, which of the following countries provided specialised tunnel-rescue assistance? 1) India 2) China 3) Republic of Korea Select the correct answer using the code below:
questions.explanation: Tunnel-rescue teams from India, China and South Korea worked with Nepali forces at the flooded hydropower tunnels.

sources.title: Water Power Magazine: Tunnel rescue efforts continue at flood-hit Nepal hydropower projects

questions.question: The 2026 Nepal flood disaster was particularly associated with which river system/corridors?
questions.explanation: The flood ran down the Bhote Koshi (Rasuwa) into the Trishuli corridor.

sources.title: Kathmandu Post: Bhote Koshi flood was one of region's largest disasters

questions.question: The August 2026 floods in Nepal significantly affected the country's hydropower sector. Which one of the following correctly describes their impact?
options: They damaged only hydropower projects that were still under construction, without affecting operational plants.
They affected both operational hydropower stations and hydropower projects under construction.
They mainly affected thermal power plants, while hydropower infrastructure remained largely unaffected.
They caused temporary disruptions only to electricity transmission, without damaging hydropower generation facilities.
questions.explanation: About 12 operating plants (around 431 MW) and 15 projects under construction (around 470 MW) were damaged.

sources.title: Columbia CGEP: Nepal floods test resilience of its hydropower-dependent economy

questions.question: India–Nepal border traverses five Indian States. Which of the following is NOT one of them?
questions.explanation: Nepal borders Uttarakhand, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, West Bengal and Sikkim. Assam is not one of them.

questions.question: Which Nepalese district, bordering Tibet, was the entry point and the worst-hit area of the flood?
questions.explanation: Rasuwa district (Rasuwagadhi border point with Tibet) was the entry point and worst-hit area.

sources.title: Onlinekhabar: Rasuwa flood – rescue progress in each tunnel

questions.question: With reference to the Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Amendment Act, 2026, which one of the following correctly describes a change introduced by the amendment?
options: It brought mineral-bearing lands under Central Government control and regulation.
It brought mineral-bearing forests under Central Government control and regulation.
It brought mineral-producing industries under Central Government control and regulation.
It brought mineral-exporting ports under Central Government control and regulation.
questions.explanation: The 2026 Amendment extended the Union's declaration (s.2) from regulating mines to regulating mines and mineral-bearing lands.

sources.title: SCC Online: MMDR Amendment Act 2026 explained

questions.question: What is the treatment of a tax, cess or other levy on mineral rights that had already been deposited with or recovered by a State Government before commencement of the 2026 Amendment Act?
options: It must be refunded to the person who paid it
It remains deposited and is not liable to refund
It must be transferred to the Central Government
It must be credited to the district mineral fund
questions.explanation: Levies already deposited with or recovered by a State before commencement are protected and need not be refunded.

questions.question: The Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Amendment Act, 2026 inserted which new provision to regulate State levies on mineral rights and mineral-bearing lands?
questions.explanation: The amendment inserted Section 9D into the MMDR Act to restrict State levies on mineral rights and mineral-bearing lands.

sources.title: SCC Online: MMDR Amendment Act 2026 explained

questions.question: Under the Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Amendment Act, 2026, State Governments can impose specified taxes, cess or other levies on mineral rights only subject to conditions prescribed by the:
questions.explanation: An amended Section 13 lets the Central Government prescribe the conditions and restrictions on State levies.

sources.title: SCC Online: MMDR Amendment Act 2026 explained

questions.question: The 26th SCO Summit of Heads of State in 2026 was hosted by which country?
questions.explanation: Kyrgyzstan hosted the 26th SCO Heads of State Council in Bishkek on 1 September 2026.

sources.title: Anadolu: SCO leaders adopt Bishkek Declaration

questions.question: The SCO currently has two observer states (other earlier observers having become full members). They are:
questions.explanation: Afghanistan and Mongolia are the SCO's two observer states. Iran (2023) and Belarus (2024) have become full members.

questions.question: Prime Minister Narendra Modi highlighted which three pillars for India's approach to the SCO agenda?
questions.explanation: Modi framed India's SCO approach around Security, Connectivity and Opportunity.

sources.title: narendramodi.in: PM Modi addresses the SCO Summit in Bishkek

questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the SCO's position reaffirmed at the 2026 summit?
options: It functions as a collective defence alliance
It operates as a military bloc against NATO
It does not constitute a military alliance
questions.explanation: The SCO has consistently said it is not a military alliance or bloc aimed at any third party.

sources.title: Anadolu: SCO leaders adopt Bishkek Declaration

questions.question: Which SCO initiative did India offer to host during the 2026 summit?
questions.explanation: Modi announced that India would host the first session of the SCO Civilisation Dialogue Forum.

sources.title: Tribune: PM Modi at 26th SCO summit in Bishkek

questions.question: Which country took over the SCO's rotating chairmanship for 2026–27 at the summit, and will host the next (27th) Heads-of-State meeting in 2027?
questions.explanation: Pakistan took over the 2026–27 chairmanship from Kyrgyzstan and will host the 2027 summit.

sources.title: Anadolu: SCO leaders adopt Bishkek Declaration

questions.question: With reference to the Cauvery Water Management Authority (CWMA), which one of the following statements is incorrect?
options: It was constituted under the Cauvery Water Management Scheme, 2018.
It implements the Cauvery Tribunal Award as modified by the Supreme Court.
Its headquarters are located in New Delhi under the Ministry of Jal Shakti.
It is a statutory authority created directly by an Act of Parliament.
questions.explanation: The CWMA was set up under the Cauvery Water Management Scheme, 2018, framed under s.6A of the Inter-State River Water Disputes Act. Parliament did not create it directly by statute. It is based in New Delhi under the Ministry of Jal Shakti.

sources.title: The Week: Centre forms Cauvery Water Management Authority (2018)

questions.question: With reference to the composition of the Cauvery Water Management Authority (CWMA), which of the following statements is correct?
options: Its Chairman is appointed by the States for a fixed term of three years.
Its Chairman is nominated by the Supreme Court for a fixed term of five years.
Its Chairman is appointed by the Centre for five years or until 65 years of age.
Its Chairman is elected by the Authority for five years or until 60 years of age.
questions.explanation: The Central Government appoints the Chairman for five years or until age 65, whichever is earlier.

questions.question: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
options: Article 262 — Adjudication of inter-State river water disputes
Article 263 — Establishment of water dispute tribunals
Article 280 — Settlement of inter-State river disputes
Article 356 — Regulation of inter-State river waters
questions.explanation: Article 262 deals with adjudication of inter-State river water disputes. Art. 263 is the Inter-State Council and Art. 280 the Finance Commission.

questions.question: Which of the following correctly identifies the change made by the Supreme Court in 2018 to the CWDT's allocation?
options: Karnataka's share was reduced while Tamil Nadu's share was increased.
Karnataka's share was increased while Tamil Nadu's share was reduced.
Kerala's share was increased while Puducherry's share was reduced.
Puducherry's share was increased while Kerala's share was reduced.
questions.explanation: In February 2018 the Supreme Court raised Karnataka's allocation by 14.75 TMC and cut Tamil Nadu's correspondingly.

questions.question: Karnataka's proposed "balancing reservoir" across the Cauvery — for Bengaluru's drinking water and power, and strongly opposed by Tamil Nadu — is the:
questions.explanation: Mekedatu is Karnataka's proposed balancing reservoir and drinking-water project, which Tamil Nadu opposes.

questions.question: Which one of the following correctly describes Vikram-1?
options: India's first privately developed orbital launch vehicle
India's first privately developed reusable launch vehicle
India's first privately developed crewed launch vehicle
India's first privately developed heavy-lift launch vehicle
questions.explanation: Skyroot's Vikram-1 is India's first privately developed orbital launch vehicle.

sources.title: SCMP: India launches first private orbital rocket

questions.question: The maiden orbital flight of Vikram-1, launched in July 2026, was designated as:
questions.explanation: The maiden orbital flight on 18 July 2026 was named Mission Aagaman ('arrival').

sources.title: Deccan Chronicle: Vikram-1 launches from Sriharikota

questions.question: Vikram-1's maiden orbital mission was launched from which Indian spaceport?
questions.explanation: It lifted off from the Satish Dhawan Space Centre, Sriharikota. Kulasekarapattinam is still under construction.

sources.title: Deccan Chronicle: Vikram-1 launches from Sriharikota

questions.question: Which of the following was among the payloads carried by Vikram-1 on its maiden orbital mission?
questions.explanation: The payloads included Skyroot's SCOPE, Grahaa Space's SOLARAS, Cosmoserve's robotic arm and a DCubed payload.

sources.title: Deccan Chronicle: Vikram-1 places payloads into orbit

questions.question: Which one of the following correctly describes the technological features of Vikram-1, developed by Skyroot Aerospace?
options: All-carbon composite structure, solid-fuel boosters and a 3D-printed liquid engine
Aluminium composite structure, liquid-fuel boosters and a cryogenic upper engine
Steel-based structure, solid-fuel boosters and a conventional liquid engine
All-carbon composite structure, cryogenic boosters and a conventional solid engine
questions.explanation: Vikram-1 has an all-carbon-composite body, three solid-fuel stages and a 3D-printed liquid upper-stage engine (Raman).

sources.title: The South First: Skyroot's Vikram-1 succeeds on maiden flight

questions.question: The volcano described in the passage, which erupted in September 2026, is:
questions.explanation: An island volcano in the strait between Java and Sumatra is Anak Krakatau ('child of Krakatoa').

questions.question: The volcano is situated in which of the following straits?
questions.explanation: Anak Krakatau lies in the Sunda Strait between Java and Sumatra.

questions.question: The "horseshoe of subduction zones" mentioned in the passage encircles which ocean?
questions.explanation: The Ring of Fire is the horseshoe of subduction zones around the Pacific Ocean.

questions.question: Why does volcanic ash pose a particular danger to aircraft?
options: It reduces oxygen levels inside the passenger cabin
It can melt inside jet engines and cause them to fail
It increases air density, making take-off impossible
It interferes with satellite navigation signals
questions.explanation: Volcanic ash is abrasive glassy silicate that melts in hot jet engines, re-solidifies on turbine parts and can cause flame-out.

sources.title: Wikipedia: Volcanic ash and aviation safety

questions.question: Which of the following is the largest active volcano in the world?
questions.explanation: Mauna Loa in Hawaii is the world's largest active volcano.

questions.question: The "international financial institution" that brokered the treaty, as mentioned in the passage, is:
questions.explanation: The World Bank (IBRD) brokered the Indus Waters Treaty (1960) and is also a signatory.

questions.question: Match the following hydroelectric and navigation projects with the rivers on which they stand: Project River A. Tulbul 1. Bhagirathi B. Chamera 2. Jhelum (at Wular Lake) C. Tehri 3. Ravi
questions.explanation: Tulbul is on the Jhelum at Wular Lake, Chamera on the Ravi and Tehri on the Bhagirathi.

questions.question: While testing India's "abeyance" against the law of treaties, the tribunal examined the doctrine of "fundamental change of circumstances". This doctrine is classically known as:
questions.explanation: Fundamental change of circumstances is rebus sic stantibus (Art. 62, Vienna Convention on the Law of Treaties).

questions.question: The Indus Waters Treaty was signed by which pair of leaders?
options: Lal Bahadur Shastri and Ayub Khan
questions.explanation: Jawaharlal Nehru and Ayub Khan signed it in Karachi on 19 September 1960.

questions.question: Which of the following statements regarding the Permanent Court of Arbitration is INCORRECT?
options: It predates the United Nations, having been established by the 1899 Hague Convention
It is housed in the Peace Palace at The Hague, which it shares with the International Court of Justice
It is a principal judicial organ of the United Nations with binding enforcement powers
India has accepted PCA-administered arbitration in other disputes despite rejecting this tribunal
questions.explanation: The PCA is an independent intergovernmental body, not a UN organ. The ICJ is the UN's principal judicial organ. The PCA (1899) predates the UN and shares the Peace Palace with the ICJ.

questions.question: The CETA was signed by Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal and which UK counterpart?
questions.explanation: Piyush Goyal and UK Business & Trade Secretary Jonathan Reynolds signed the CETA on 24 July 2025 at Chequers.

sources.title: Wikipedia: India–United Kingdom Free Trade Agreement

questions.question: Under the India–UK CETA, the United Kingdom has granted zero-duty access covering approximately:
options: 90% of India's tariff lines, covering 95% of trade value
95% of India's tariff lines, covering 97% of trade value
99% of India's tariff lines, covering nearly 100% of trade value
100% of India's tariff lines, covering 100% of trade value
questions.explanation: The UK gives zero-duty access to about 99% of Indian tariff lines, covering nearly 100% of trade value.

sources.title: Business Today: India–UK CETA – zero duty on 99% of exports

questions.question: Who was the Prime Minister of the United Kingdom at the time of the signing of CETA?
questions.explanation: Keir Starmer was UK Prime Minister when the CETA was signed (July 2025).

questions.question: India and the United Kingdom are both full members of which of the following groupings?
questions.explanation: Both are G20 members. India is not in the G7, AUKUS or Five Eyes.

questions.question: India's first hydrogen-powered train was flagged off by the Prime Minister on  2026 from:
questions.explanation: India's first hydrogen train was flagged off from Jind Junction, Haryana, on the Jind–Sonipat section (89 km).

questions.question: In the colour classification of hydrogen, "green hydrogen" refers to hydrogen produced by:
options: Steam reforming of natural gas with carbon capture
Electrolysis of water using renewable electricity
