questions.explanation: Green hydrogen comes from electrolysis of water using renewable electricity.

questions.question: Who is the Union Minister of Railways under whose tenure India's first hydrogen train was launched?
questions.explanation: Ashwini Vaishnaw is Union Railway Minister.

questions.question: The larger scheme under which Indian Railways plans to run hydrogen trains on hill and heritage routes is called:
questions.explanation: Indian Railways' plan for hydrogen trains on heritage and hill routes is called 'Hydrogen for Heritage'.

questions.question: The Governor-General during whose tenure the first railway line was opened, and who is called the "father of Indian Railways" for his 1853 Railway Minute laying down the trunk-route plan, was:
questions.explanation: Lord Dalhousie's 1853 Railway Minute and the first line (Bombay–Thane, 1853) make him the 'father of Indian Railways'.

sources.title: Wikipedia: James Broun-Ramsay, 1st Marquess of Dalhousie

questions.question: The parent Act amended by the 2026 Bill is:
options: The Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act, 2024
The Prevention of Examination Malpractices Act, 2023
The Public Examinations (Prohibition of Cheating and Unfair Means) Act, 2025
questions.explanation: The 2026 Bill amends the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act, 2024.

sources.title: PRS: Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill, 2026

questions.question: The immediate political context of the 2026 amendment, referred to in the passage, involved the resignation of Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan and his replacement by:
questions.explanation: After Dharmendra Pradhan resigned over the NEET-UG 2026 leak (25 July 2026), Pralhad Joshi was given charge of the Education Ministry.

sources.title: Onmanorama: Pralhad Joshi appointed Education Minister

questions.question: For the organised crime of unfair means in public examinations, the amendment provides:
options: Minimum 5 years' imprisonment and minimum fine of ₹1 crore
Minimum 7 years' imprisonment and minimum fine of ₹10 crore
Minimum 10 years' imprisonment and fine up to ₹50 lakh
Life imprisonment and confiscation of property
questions.explanation: The amendment sets a minimum of 7 years' imprisonment and a minimum ₹10 crore fine for organised paper-leak crime (earlier 5–10 years and at least ₹1 crore).

questions.question: The Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill, 2026, being passed in each House of Parliament by which majority
options: Simple majority of members present and voting
Absolute majority of the total membership of the House
questions.explanation: It is an ordinary bill, passed by a simple majority of members present and voting (the Lok Sabha passed it by voice vote).

sources.title: Governance Now: Lok Sabha passes amendment bill

questions.question: The Aravallis are described as a "green barrier" against the eastward spread of which desert, and their highest peak is:
questions.explanation: The Aravallis check the eastward spread of the Thar desert. Their highest peak is Guru Shikhar (1,722 m) on Mount Abu.

questions.question: Under the definition accepted by the Supreme Court in November 2025, a landform qualifies as an Aravalli Hill if it rises at least:
options: 100 metres above the surrounding local terrain
500 metres above the surrounding local terrain
questions.explanation: The November 2025 definition counts as an Aravalli hill any landform at least 100 m above its local relief.

questions.question: The Aravalli range passes through which of the following states/UTs, in order from southwest to northeast?
questions.explanation: From south-west to north-east the Aravallis run through Gujarat, Rajasthan, Haryana and Delhi.

questions.question: On September 2026 order refusing the Aravalli panel's extension was passed by a Bench headed by:
questions.explanation: On 7 September 2026 a bench led by CJI Surya Kant (with Justices Bagchi and Mohana) refused the Aravalli committee's six-month extension.

sources.title: ThePrint: CJI Surya Kant rejects Aravalli panel's plea for extension

questions.question: Which of the following correctly matches all three Ramon Magsaysay Awardees of 2026 with their respective countries?
options: Tommy Koh—Singapore; Runa Khan—Bangladesh; Bo Kyi—Myanmar
Tommy Koh—Malaysia; Runa Khan—Bangladesh; Bo Kyi—Thailand
Tommy Koh—Singapore; Runa Khan—Myanmar; Bo Kyi—Bangladesh
Tommy Koh—Philippines; Runa Khan—Thailand; Bo Kyi—Myanmar
questions.explanation: The 2026 Magsaysay awardees are Tommy Koh (Singapore), Runa Khan (Bangladesh) and Bo Kyi (Myanmar).

sources.title: Tatler Asia: 2026 Ramon Magsaysay Award recipients

questions.question: Tommy Koh’s 2026 Ramon Magsaysay Award citation particularly recognises his role in the negotiations leading to the adoption of which international treaty?
options: Vienna Convention on the Law of Treaties
United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change
United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea
questions.explanation: Tommy Koh presided over the Third UN Conference on the Law of the Sea, which adopted UNCLOS in 1982.

questions.question: Consider the following statements concerning the Ramon Magsaysay Award Foundation: 1. The Foundation was established in 1957 by the trustees of the Rockefeller Brothers Fund. 2. Beginning in 2009, the Award ceased to be conferred in fixed categories, except for Emergent Leadership. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Both are correct. The Foundation was set up in 1957 by the Rockefeller Brothers Fund trustees with the Philippine government, and since 2009 the award has had no fixed categories except Emergent Leadership.

questions.question: The Ramon Magsaysay Award ceremony is traditionally held in Manila. Which major international financial institution is also headquartered in that city?
questions.explanation: The Asian Development Bank is headquartered in Manila (Mandaluyong, Metro Manila).

questions.question: Who was the first Indian recipient of the Ramon Magsaysay Award?
questions.explanation: Vinoba Bhave was the first Indian recipient, in 1958, the award's first year.

questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding the Emergent Leadership component of the Ramon Magsaysay Award: 1. An eligible individual must be 40 years of age or younger. 2. The Emergent Leadership category was inaugurated in 2009. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Emergent Leadership awardees must be 40 or younger. The category began in 2001 (Ford Foundation support), not 2009.

questions.question: India’s chairship of BRICS in 2026 was its:
questions.explanation: India chaired BRICS in 2012, 2016, 2021 and 2026, so 2026 is its fourth chairship.

questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding the early development of BRICS: 1. The first BRIC Summit was held in Yekaterinburg, Russia, in 2009. 2. South Africa participated as a full member in the first BRIC Summit. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: The first BRIC summit was in Yekaterinburg in 2009. South Africa joined in 2010–11 (first summit as member: Sanya 2011).

questions.question: Which declaration was adopted at the 16th BRICS Summit held in Russia in 2024?
questions.explanation: The 16th summit (Kazan, Russia, October 2024) adopted the Kazan Declaration.

questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding the expansion of BRICS: 1. Egypt and Ethiopia became full members of BRICS in 2024. 2. Indonesia became a full member of BRICS at the same time in January 2024. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Egypt and Ethiopia (with Iran and the UAE) joined in January 2024. Indonesia joined in January 2025.

questions.question: Who among the following served as the first president of the New Development Bank?
questions.explanation: K. V. Kamath was the NDB's first president (2015–2020).

questions.question: The Indian Regional Office of the New Development Bank is located in:
questions.explanation: The NDB's India Regional Office is at GIFT City, Gandhinagar, Gujarat.

questions.question: Which of the following correctly states India’s final position and medal tally at the 2026 Commonwealth Games?
options: Fourth — 13 gold, 17 silver and 9 bronze medals
Fourth — 13 gold, 9 silver and 17 bronze medals
Fifth — 13 gold, 17 silver and 9 bronze medals
Third — 17 gold, 13 silver and 9 bronze medals
questions.explanation: India finished 4th at Glasgow 2026 with 13 gold, 17 silver and 9 bronze (39 medals).

sources.title: Free Press Journal: India jump to 4th, total 39

questions.question: Which sport produced seven of India’s total gold medals at the 2026 Commonwealth Games?
questions.explanation: Indian boxers won seven golds at Glasgow 2026.

sources.title: The Bridge: India's seven boxing golds

questions.question: Which of the following Indian gold medallist at Glasgow 2026 had previously won a silver medal at the Tokyo 2020 Olympic Games?
questions.explanation: Mirabai Chanu won weightlifting silver (49 kg) at Tokyo 2020, the only option with a Tokyo medal.

questions.question: At which Olympic Games did Karnam Malleswari become the first Indian woman to win an Olympic medal?
questions.explanation: Karnam Malleswari won weightlifting bronze at Sydney 2000, the first Olympic medal by an Indian woman.

questions.question: Following Glasgow 2026, Amdavad is scheduled to stage the centenary Commonwealth Games in 2030. Which city hosted the inaugural British Empire Games in 1930?
questions.explanation: Hamilton, Canada hosted the first British Empire Games in 1930.

questions.question: Which pair correctly identifies India’s silver and bronze medallists, respectively, in the men’s javelin throw at Glasgow 2026?
options: Yash Vir Singh and Neeraj Chopra
Neeraj Chopra and Yash Vir Singh
questions.explanation: Neeraj Chopra took silver (85.83 m) and Yashvir Singh bronze (85.41 m). Sri Lanka's Rumesh Pathirage won gold.

sources.title: Outlook: Pathirage floors Neeraj Chopra; Yashvir bronze

questions.question: Which Union Ministry administers the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act?
questions.explanation: The Ministry of Home Affairs administers the FCRA.

questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding permission to receive foreign contributions: 1. An FCRA registration certificate is ordinarily valid for five years. 2. Prior permission allows an organisation to receive funds from any foreign donor for any future activity. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: FCRA registration is valid for five years. Prior permission is specific to a donor, amount and purpose, not open-ended.

questions.question: An organisation registered under the FCRA must receive foreign contributions through a designated account opened at which institution?
options: State Bank of India, New Delhi Main Branch
Punjab National Bank, Parliament Street Branch
Bank of Baroda, New Delhi Main Branch
questions.explanation: Since the 2020 amendment, foreign contributions must first be received in an 'FCRA Account' at SBI, New Delhi Main Branch.

questions.question: Under the existing FCRA framework, what percentage of foreign contributions may ordinarily be used for administrative expenses without prior government approval?
questions.explanation: The 2020 amendment capped administrative expenses at 20% of foreign contributions (earlier 50%).

questions.question: What maximum term of imprisonment does the 2026 Amendment Bill propose under its rationalised punishment provision for specified FCRA violations?
questions.explanation: The 2026 Bill cuts the maximum imprisonment for contraventions under s.35 from five years to one year.

sources.title: PRS: Legislative Brief – FCRA Amendment Bill 2026

questions.question: Which Schedule of the Constitution contains the names and territorial descriptions of the States and Union Territories?
questions.explanation: The First Schedule lists the States and UTs and their territories.

questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding a Bill seeking to change the name of a State: 1. Such a Bill may be introduced in Parliament only on the recommendation of the President. 2. Parliament is constitutionally bound to accept the views expressed by the affected State Legislature. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Under Art. 3 such a bill needs the President's recommendation, but the State Legislature's views do not bind Parliament.

questions.question: What majority is ordinarily required in Parliament to pass a law changing the name of a State under Article 3?
options: A two-thirds majority of the total membership
A simple majority of members present and voting
A special majority followed by ratification by half the States
A unanimous vote of the affected State Legislature
questions.explanation: Art. 4(2) says such laws are not Art. 368 amendments, so a simple majority is enough.

questions.question: On which date was the present State of Kerala created under the States Reorganisation Act, 1956?
questions.explanation: Kerala was formed on 1 November 1956 under the States Reorganisation Act.

questions.question: The territorial jurisdiction of the Kerala High Court also extends to which of the following Union Territory?
questions.explanation: The Kerala High Court also has jurisdiction over Lakshadweep.

questions.question: Which section of the Prevention of Insults to National Honour Act was amended to protect “Vande Mataram”?
questions.explanation: The 2026 amendment changes Section 3 of the Prevention of Insults to National Honour Act, 1971 (which deals with preventing the singing of the National Anthem) to cover Vande Mataram as well.

sources.title: Drishti IAS: Prevention of Insults to National Honour (Amendment) Bill, 2026

questions.question: What is the maximum term of imprisonment prescribed for intentionally preventing the singing of the national song?
questions.explanation: The penalty is the same as for the anthem: up to three years' imprisonment, a fine, or both.

sources.title: Drishti IAS: Prevention of Insults to National Honour (Amendment) Bill, 2026

questions.question: In which case did the Supreme Court recognise that respectfully flying the National Flag is protected under Article 19(1)(a)?
options: Union of India v. Naveen Jindal
Bijoe Emmanuel v. State of Kerala
Shreya Singhal v. Union of India
S. R. Bommai v. Union of India
questions.explanation: Union of India v. Naveen Jindal (2004) held that respectfully flying the National Flag is part of free expression under Art. 19(1)(a).

sources.title: Wikipedia: Union of India v. Naveen Jindal

questions.question: “Vande Mataram” appears in Anandamath, which portrays an ascetic resistance movement in Bengal. Which historical uprising forms the principal background of the novel?
questions.explanation: Anandamath is set against the late-18th-century Sannyasi Rebellion in Bengal.

questions.question: The 2026 amendment gives the national song legal protection comparable to India’s national anthem. At which Congress session was “Jana Gana Mana” first publicly sung?
questions.explanation: Jana Gana Mana was first sung publicly at the Calcutta session of the Congress on 27 December 1911.

questions.question: Which constitutional provision requires citizens to respect the Constitution, the National Flag and the National Anthem?
questions.explanation: Article 51A(a) is the fundamental duty to respect the Constitution, the National Flag and the National Anthem.

questions.question: The new Act replaces the principal legislation that previously guaranteed wage employment to rural households. In which year was that predecessor legislation enacted?
questions.explanation: The predecessor law was MGNREGA, enacted in 2005.

questions.question: The rural employment guarantee is supported by a provision for unemployment allowance when work is not provided promptly. Within what period must employment ordinarily be provided after a valid demand is made?
questions.explanation: Work must be provided within 15 days of a valid demand, or an unemployment allowance is due.

sources.title: MGNREGA, 2005, Section 7 (carried into VB-G RAM G framework)

questions.question: Expenditure under the new rural employment framework is shared between the Union and the States. What is the prescribed Centre–State funding ratio for general-category States?
questions.explanation: General-category States share costs with the Centre 60:40. NE and Himalayan States share 90:10.

sources.title: Viksit Bharat – G RAM G Act, 2025 (fund-sharing)

questions.question: The nationwide implementation of the Act was marked by a formal launch at Mukkavaripalli village in Tirupati district. In which State is the village located?
questions.explanation: Mukkavaripalli, where the national launch was held (July 2026), is in Tirupati district, Andhra Pradesh.

sources.title: Deccan Chronicle: Naidu, Chouhan launch VB G-RAM-G scheme in Tirupati

questions.question: The Act assigns an important planning role to Panchayats through the preparation of Viksit Gram Panchayat Plans. Which constitutional amendment gave constitutional status to Panchayati Raj institutions?
questions.explanation: The 73rd Amendment (1992) gave Panchayati Raj institutions constitutional status (Part IX).

questions.question: Social audits form an important accountability mechanism for examining expenditure and works under rural employment programmes. Which village-level institution is principally associated with conducting such audits?
questions.explanation: The Gram Sabha conducts social audits of rural employment works.

questions.question: FATF leadership positions are filled internally rather than through voting in the United Nations or the OECD. Which FATF body appointed India’s representative as Vice-President?
questions.explanation: The FATF Plenary, its decision-making body, appoints the President and Vice-President.

questions.question: During his Vice-Presidential term, Vivek Aggarwal assists FATF President Giles Thomson in steering the organisation. Giles Thomson represents which FATF member country?
questions.explanation: FATF President Giles Thomson (2026–28) is from the United Kingdom (HM Treasury).

questions.question: FATF is an intergovernmental standard-setting body, but it is not a specialised agency of the United Nations. In which city is FATF based?
questions.explanation: The FATF Secretariat is in Paris, at the OECD.

questions.question: FATF members are assessed against a consolidated set of international standards dealing with illicit financial activity. How many Recommendations constitute the principal FATF standards?
questions.explanation: The FATF standards are the 40 Recommendations.

questions.question: FATF publicly identifies jurisdictions having strategic deficiencies in their systems for combating illicit finance. What is the official description commonly associated with the FATF “grey list”?
questions.explanation: The grey list is officially 'Jurisdictions under Increased Monitoring'.

questions.question: FATF standards are implemented in India through several domestic laws dealing with money laundering and confiscation of proceeds. In which year was the Prevention of Money Laundering Act enacted?
questions.explanation: The Prevention of Money Laundering Act was enacted in 2002 and came into force in 2005.

sources.title: Wikipedia: Prevention of Money Laundering Act, 2002

questions.question: The World Bank reviews the income category of each economy at the beginning of its financial year. Which indicator is principally used to determine these classifications?
options: GDP per capita through PPP conversion
GNI per capita through Atlas conversion
NNI per capita through market conversion
questions.explanation: The World Bank classifies economies by GNI per capita in US dollars, converted using the Atlas method.

sources.title: World Bank: Country and Lending Groups

questions.question: India continued in the lower-middle-income group under the World Bank’s classification for FY2027. What is the upper GNI-per-capita limit of this category?
questions.explanation: For FY2027 the lower-middle-income band is $1,176–$4,635 GNI per capita.

sources.title: World Bank: Country and Lending Groups (FY2027)

questions.question: Several major Asian economies fall into different World Bank income groups despite belonging to the same geographical region. Which of the following is classified as an upper-middle-income economy for FY2027?
questions.explanation: China is upper-middle-income. India, Nepal and Pakistan are lower-middle-income.

sources.title: World Bank: Country and Lending Groups

questions.question: Income classification is connected with the lending framework of the institutions constituting the World Bank Group. Which institution primarily lends to middle-income and creditworthy lower-income countries?
questions.explanation: The IBRD lends to middle-income and creditworthy lower-income countries. IDA gives concessional finance to the poorest.

sources.title: Wikipedia: International Bank for Reconstruction and Development

questions.question: The World Bank relies partly on official national accounts when calculating India’s GNI and per-capita income. Which Indian institution prepares the country’s official national-income estimates?
questions.explanation: The National Statistical Office (MoSPI) compiles India's national income estimates.

questions.question: The proposed safeguard for Ladakh would be placed alongside existing special provisions for certain Indian States. Article 371 and its related provisions form part of which Part of the Constitution?
questions.explanation: Articles 369–392 (including Art. 371) make up Part XXI: Temporary, Transitional and Special Provisions.

questions.question: Ladakh is presently administered as a Union Territory through a Lieutenant Governor. Under Article 239, who appoints the administrator of a Union Territory?
questions.explanation: Under Art. 239 the President administers each UT through an administrator he or she appoints.

questions.question: Ladakhi organisations had earlier demanded inclusion under the Sixth Schedule as an alternative constitutional safeguard. The Sixth Schedule is principally connected with which constitutional provision?
questions.explanation: The Sixth Schedule operates through Articles 244(2) and 275(1).

questions.question: The Sixth Schedule operates only in four northeastern States and does not automatically apply to every tribal- majority region. Which of the following States is not covered by the Sixth Schedule?
questions.explanation: The Sixth Schedule covers Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram. Nagaland has Article 371A instead.

questions.question: Although Ladakh does not have its own Legislative Assembly, its residents are represented directly in the Lok Sabha. How many Lok Sabha constituencies are allotted to the Union Territory?
questions.explanation: Ladakh has one Lok Sabha seat.

questions.question: The first meeting of the Strategic Political and Defence Committee created under the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement was held in:
questions.explanation: The first meeting of the Strategic Political and Defence Committee under the Makkah agreement was held in Istanbul on 31 August 2026.

sources.title: Asharq Al-Awsat: Committee holds first meeting in Istanbul

questions.question: Which institutional body was created to coordinate the implementation of the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement?
questions.explanation: The agreement set up a Strategic Political and Defence Committee to coordinate its implementation.

sources.title: Turkish MFA: First meeting of the Strategic Political and Defence Committee

questions.question: Which party to the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement is also a member of NATO?
questions.explanation: Türkiye has been a NATO member since 1952. Pakistan and Saudi Arabia are not members.

questions.question: The first Islamic Summit, which led to the establishment of the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation, was held in 1969 in:
questions.explanation: The first Islamic Summit (Rabat, September 1969) led to the OIC.

questions.question: Which of the following parties to the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement are also members of the D-8 Organization for Economic Cooperation?
questions.explanation: Pakistan and Türkiye are D-8 members. Saudi Arabia is not.

sources.title: Wikipedia: D-8 Organization for Economic Cooperation

questions.question: Pakistan conducted a series of nuclear tests in May 1998 at which location?
questions.explanation: Pakistan carried out its May 1998 nuclear tests (Chagai-I) in the Chagai Hills, Balochistan.

questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding the constitutional strength of the Supreme Court: 1. Article 124 permits Parliament to prescribe a larger number of Supreme Court judges by law. 2. The Constitution permanently fixes the total strength of the Supreme Court at 34 judges. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Art. 124(1) lets Parliament set the number of judges by law. The Constitution does not fix it permanently.

questions.question: Who has the constitutional authority to decide whether a Bill is a Money Bill?
questions.explanation: Under Art. 110(3) the Lok Sabha Speaker's decision on whether a bill is a Money Bill is final.

questions.question: Within how many days must the Rajya Sabha return a Money Bill to the Lok Sabha?
questions.explanation: The Rajya Sabha must return a Money Bill within 14 days (Art. 109).

questions.question: The salaries and allowances of Supreme Court judges are charged upon which of the following funds?
questions.explanation: Supreme Court judges' salaries and allowances are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India (Art. 112(3)(d)).

questions.question: What majority is required in each House of Parliament to pass an address for the removal of a Supreme Court judge?
options: Majority of the total membership and two-thirds of members present and voting
Majority of the total membership and three-fourths of members present and voting
Two-thirds of the total membership and majority of members present and voting
Two-thirds of the total membership and three-fourths of members present and voting
questions.explanation: Art. 124(4) requires a majority of total membership and two-thirds of members present and voting in each House.

questions.question: For appointment as a Supreme Court judge, a person may qualify by having practised as a High Court advocate for at least:
questions.explanation: Under Art. 124(3) the qualification is 10 years as a High Court advocate (or 5 years as a HC judge, or being a distinguished jurist).

questions.question: Which event in the life of Gautama Buddha is principally associated with Sarnath?
options: The Buddha attained enlightenment at this place
The Buddha delivered his first sermon here
The Buddha entered Mahaparinirvana at this place
The Buddha was born to Queen Maya here
questions.explanation: The Buddha gave his first sermon (Dhammachakkappavattana) at Sarnath.

questions.question: On which date was the Lion Capital of Ashoka at Sarnath adopted as the State Emblem of India?
questions.explanation: The Sarnath Lion Capital was adopted as the State Emblem on 26 January 1950.

questions.question: The Convention concerning the Protection of the World Cultural and Natural Heritage was adopted by UNESCO in:
questions.explanation: UNESCO adopted the World Heritage Convention in 1972.

questions.question: By which ancient name is Sarnath frequently identified in early Buddhist texts written in Pali?
questions.explanation: Pali texts call Sarnath Isipatana (the Deer Park, Migadaya).

questions.question: The First Buddhist Council is traditionally believed to have been held at:
questions.explanation: The First Buddhist Council was held at Rajagriha (Rajgir) under Ajatashatru.

questions.question: Who is generally regarded as the founder and first Director-General of the Archaeological Survey of India?
questions.explanation: Alexander Cunningham founded the ASI (1861) and was its first Director-General.

questions.question: Which country assumed the rotating chairship of the SCO following the 2026 Bishkek Summit?
questions.explanation: Pakistan took over the SCO chairship (2026–27) after the Bishkek summit.

sources.title: Anadolu: SCO leaders adopt Bishkek Declaration

questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding the origins of the SCO: 1. The SCO developed from an earlier grouping known as the Shanghai Five. 2. Uzbekistan was an original member of the Shanghai Five formed in 1996. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: The SCO grew out of the Shanghai Five (China, Russia, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, 1996). Uzbekistan joined only in 2001.

questions.question: The Executive Committee of the SCO’s Regional Anti-Terrorist Structure is headquartered in:
questions.explanation: The RATS Executive Committee is in Tashkent.

questions.question: Which body is the highest decision-making institution of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation?
questions.explanation: The Council of Heads of State is the SCO's highest decision-making body.

questions.question: The Charter of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation was signed at:
questions.explanation: The SCO Charter was signed in St Petersburg in June 2002 (in force 2003).

questions.question: Who among the following won the Golden Boot at the FIFA World Cup 2026?
questions.explanation: Kylian Mbappé won the 2026 Golden Boot with 10 goals, becoming the first two-time winner.

sources.title: Gulf News: Kylian Mbappe wins 2026 World Cup Golden Boot

questions.question: In which city is the headquarters of FIFA located?
questions.explanation: FIFA is headquartered in Zürich.

questions.question: Who became the oldest coach to win the men’s FIFA World Cup in 2026?
questions.explanation: Spain's Luis de la Fuente, 65, became the oldest coach to win the World Cup.

questions.question: Which country hosted and won the inaugural men’s FIFA World Cup?
questions.explanation: Uruguay hosted and won the first World Cup in 1930.

questions.question: Zayu, one of the official mascots of the FIFA World Cup 2026, represents which animal?
questions.explanation: Zayu is a jaguar representing Mexico. Maple (moose) represents Canada and Clutch (bald eagle) the USA.

questions.question: The Trust alluded to in the passage will be rechristened as the:
options: National Mineral Regulation and Auction Trust
National Mineral Security and Conservation Trust
National Mineral Exploration and Development Trust
National Mineral Exchange and Exploration Trust
questions.explanation: The National Mineral Exploration Trust's mandate was widened to fund mine development, and it was renamed the National Mineral Exploration and Development Trust.

sources.title: SCC Online: MMDR Amendment Act 2026 explained

questions.question: As per the passage, the Amendment deals with past State levies that were demanded but never recovered by:
options: Declaring such unpaid demands as invalid for all purposes
Recovering them gradually in three equal annual instalments
Converting them into interest-free loans payable by leaseholders
Adjusting them against royalty payable in the future years
questions.explanation: State levies demanded but not deposited or recovered before commencement are deemed invalid. Amounts already collected are protected.

questions.question: Khanij Bidesh India Ltd. (KABIL), tasked with sourcing critical minerals overseas, is a joint venture of:
questions.explanation: KABIL is a joint venture of NALCO, Hindustan Copper (HCL) and Mineral Exploration & Consultancy (MECL).

questions.question: Which one of the following States is India's largest producer of iron ore?
questions.explanation: Odisha is India's largest iron ore producer.

sources.title: Indian Bureau of Mines: Indian Minerals Yearbook

questions.question: The restriction on State levies on mineral rights and mineral-bearing lands has been introduced by inserting which new provision into the parent Act?
questions.explanation: The amendment inserted Section 9D into the MMDR Act.

sources.title: SCC Online: MMDR Amendment Act 2026 explained

questions.question: The famous Jaduguda mine, located in the state of Jharkhand, is well-known for the extraction of which of the following minerals?
questions.explanation: Jaduguda in Jharkhand is India's first uranium mine (UCIL).

questions.question: The name of the maiden orbital mission, "Aagaman", most nearly translates to:
questions.explanation: 'Aagaman' means 'arrival'.

sources.title: Deccan Chronicle: Vikram-1 launches from Sriharikota

questions.question: IN-SPACe, the nodal agency that authorises and supervises private space missions in India, is headquartered at:
questions.explanation: IN-SPACe is headquartered in Ahmedabad (Bopal), Gujarat.

questions.question: Skyroot's "Dhawan-1", tested in 2021, holds the distinction of being India's first privately developed:
questions.explanation: Skyroot's Dhawan-1 (2021) was India's first privately developed, fully cryogenic rocket engine.

questions.question: According to the passage, the seven-judge bench in 2024 essentially held that:
options: Sub-classification of SCs and STs is wholly impermissible
States may reserve an entire sub-quota for one sub-caste
Parliament alone may apportion benefits within the class
States may sub-classify within the quota relying on empirical data
questions.explanation: In State of Punjab v. Davinder Singh (2024) the seven-judge bench allowed States to sub-classify SCs/STs on the basis of quantifiable data.

sources.title: Wikipedia: State of Punjab v. Davinder Singh

questions.question: The opinion that contrasted "a child in an elite metropolitan school and an elite college" with "a child in a remote village school", urging exclusion of the advanced layer, was authored by:
questions.explanation: Justice B.R. Gavai made the elite-school vs village-school comparison while urging a creamy layer for SC/ST.

sources.title: Wikipedia: State of Punjab v. Davinder Singh

questions.question: The Supreme Court’s 2024 judgment relating to Scheduled Castes renewed debate concerning which of the following?
options: Removal of reservation for Scheduled Castes
Application of the creamy layer to all reserved categories
Introduction of economic criteria for Scheduled Tribe status
questions.explanation: The 2024 judgment revived debate on sub-classification within Scheduled Castes.

sources.title: Wikipedia: State of Punjab v. Davinder Singh

questions.question: The 2024 verdict overruled which judgment that had treated the Scheduled Castes as a homogeneous, indivisible class?
options: Janhit Abhiyan v. Union of India
State of Madras v. Champakam Dorairajan
Indra Sawhney v. Union of India
E. V. Chinnaiah v. State of Andhra Pradesh
questions.explanation: It overruled E.V. Chinnaiah v. State of A.P. (2004), which had treated SCs as one homogeneous class.

sources.title: Wikipedia: State of Punjab v. Davinder Singh

questions.question: Which Article of the Constitution empowers the President to specify the list of Scheduled Tribes?
questions.explanation: Art. 342 provides for specifying Scheduled Tribes. Art. 341 covers Scheduled Castes.

questions.question: The 103rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 2019, introduced what percentage of reservation for Economically Weaker Sections?
questions.explanation: The 103rd Amendment (2019) allows up to 10% EWS reservation.

questions.question: With reference to India’s campaign for reform of the United Nations Security Council, consider the following statements: 1. The SHANTI initiative is associated with India’s campaign for a non-permanent seat on the UNSC for 2028– 2029. 2. India’s demand for permanent membership is linked to its objective of having a greater role in decisions concerning international peace and security. 3. The SHANTI initiative was launched as part of the G4 framework. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: SHANTI is India's campaign for a 2028–29 non-permanent UNSC seat, which also ties into its push for a bigger say in peace and security. It is an Indian national campaign, not a G4 initiative.

sources.title: Tribune: India launches campaign for UNSC non-permanent seat – SHANTI vision

questions.question: The acronym "SHANTI", under which India has launched its latest Security Council campaign, expands to:
options: Securing Holistic Advancement through Norms, Trust and Integrity
Stabilising Humanitarian Architecture through Negotiated Treaties Initiatives
Sustaining Harmony Among Nations through Trust and Inclusion
Strengthening Holistic Alliances for New Trust-based Institutions
questions.explanation: SHANTI is expanded as 'Securing Holistic Advancement through Norms, Trust and Integrity' (launched July 2026).

sources.title: C4S: India and permanent UNSC membership

questions.question: Which one of the following countries is NOT a member of the G4 grouping?
questions.explanation: The G4 are India, Brazil, Germany and Japan. Italy leads the rival Uniting for Consensus group.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT one of the six principal organs of the United Nations?
questions.explanation: The Human Rights Council is a subsidiary of the General Assembly, not a principal organ.

questions.question: Which one of the following provisions creates a major procedural hurdle for reforming the composition of the United Nations Security Council?
options: Article 108 requiring a two-thirds General Assembly vote and ratification by all P5 members
Article 99 requiring approval from all elected members of the Security Council
Article 51 requiring unanimous approval of the General Assembly for Charter changes
Article 109 requiring ratification only by the permanent members of the Council
questions.explanation: Article 108 requires a two-thirds General Assembly vote plus ratification by two-thirds of members including all P5, which in effect gives the P5 a veto on reform.

questions.question: India's Permanent Representative who argued the reform case at the 2026 IGN sessions was:
questions.explanation: P. Harish has been India's Permanent Representative to the UN since 2024.

sources.title: Wikipedia: Permanent Representative of India to the United Nations

questions.question: With reference to India's maritime heritage diplomacy, delays in which of the following initiatives specifically limit India’s ability to leverage Indian Ocean heritage?
questions.explanation: Project Mausam (Ministry of Culture) is about Indian Ocean maritime and cultural routes.

questions.question: India advances cultural cooperation through which of the following multilateral platforms?
questions.explanation: India pursues cultural cooperation through BRICS, the G20, the SCO and BIMSTEC. It is not a member of NATO, the G7, OPEC or the OECD.

questions.question: The "dozen sentinel forts" that entered the UNESCO World Heritage List last year, as per the passage, constitute the:
questions.explanation: The twelve forts inscribed in 2025 are the 'Maratha Military Landscapes of India'.

sources.title: Wikipedia: Maratha Military Landscapes of India

questions.question: After the latest additions (Marathi, Bengali, Assamese, Pali and Prakrit), the number of languages enjoying 'Classical' status in India is:
questions.explanation: The earlier 6 (Tamil, Sanskrit, Telugu, Kannada, Malayalam, Odia) plus 5 added in 2024 make 11 classical languages.

questions.question: The existing Ganges Water Sharing Treaty between India and Bangladesh was signed in which year?
questions.explanation: The Ganges Water Sharing Treaty was signed in December 1996 by PMs Deve Gowda and Sheikh Hasina.

questions.question: What was the principal original purpose behind constructing the Farakka Barrage?
options: Diverting water into the Hooghly to aid navigation
questions.explanation: Farakka was built to divert Ganga water into the Bhagirathi–Hooghly to flush silt and keep Kolkata port navigable.

questions.question: The Farakka Barrage Project forms part of the navigation infrastructure associated with which National Waterway?
questions.explanation: Farakka (with its navigation lock) lies on National Waterway 1, the Ganga–Bhagirathi–Hooghly from Haldia to Prayagraj.

questions.question: Farakka Barrage is located in which Indian State?
questions.explanation: Farakka Barrage is in Murshidabad district, West Bengal.

questions.question: The current Ganga Water Sharing Treaty is scheduled to complete its term in which year?
questions.explanation: The 30-year treaty signed in December 1996 expires in 2026.

questions.question: The Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Amendment Bill, 2026 amended which principal legislation?
questions.explanation: The bill amends the Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Act, 1956.

questions.question: Under the 2026 amendment, the number of Supreme Court judges excluding the Chief Justice of India was increased to:
questions.explanation: The strength went from 34 to 38 including the CJI, i.e. 37 judges besides the Chief Justice.

sources.title: LegalEdge Mock 26 key note: proposed 2026 legislation raises strength to 37 (excl. CJI)

questions.question: Which Article of the Constitution permits Parliament to determine by law the number of judges of the Supreme Court?
questions.explanation: Article 124(1) lets Parliament increase the number of judges by law.

questions.question: The Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Amendment Bill, 2026 was introduced in Parliament by which Union Minister?
questions.explanation: Bills on judges' strength are piloted by the Minister of Law and Justice.

questions.question: The 2026 judge-strength legislation was processed in Parliament as which category of Bill?
options: Ordinary Bill requiring a joint sitting
questions.explanation: As in 2019, it was passed as a Money Bill because it deals with expenditure from the Consolidated Fund.

questions.question: Who has the constitutional authority to certify whether a Bill is a Money Bill?
questions.explanation: The Lok Sabha Speaker certifies Money Bills (Art. 110(3)–(4)).

questions.question: Which institution is responsible for maintaining India's primary time scale, UTC(NPLI), and realising Indian Standard Time?
questions.explanation: CSIR-National Physical Laboratory maintains UTC(NPLI) and realises IST.

sources.title: Drishti IAS: Legal Metrology (Indian Standard Time) Rules, 2026

questions.question: Under the Rules, which of the following is NOT expressly listed as an authorised source through which critical- sector systems may synchronise with IST?
questions.explanation: The authorised timing references are CSIR-NPL, the RRSLs, NavIC and NIC services. The IMD is not one of them.

questions.question: The definition of the base unit of time under the 2026 Rules is linked to the transition frequency of which isotope?
questions.explanation: The SI second is defined by the caesium-133 hyperfine transition frequency.

questions.question: Which technology has been deployed at the Regional Reference Standard Laboratory (RRSL), Bengaluru, to achieve sub-nanosecond-level time synchronisation for institutions such as ISRO, SEBI, NSE and BSNL?
questions.explanation: White Rabbit, a PTP-based technology, gives sub-nanosecond time synchronisation.

questions.question: Which of the following States is NOT crossed by the Standard Meridian of India (82°30′ E)?
questions.explanation: 82°30′E passes through UP, MP, Chhattisgarh, Odisha and Andhra Pradesh, but not Jharkhand.

questions.question: The Third India–Australia Annual Summit in 2026 was held in which city?
questions.explanation: The 3rd India–Australia Annual Summit was held in Melbourne in July 2026.

sources.title: Open: India, Australia boost defence, energy, trade at Melbourne summit

questions.question: Australian uranium supplied to India under the newly operationalised civil nuclear arrangement is expressly subject to safeguards administered by which organisation?
questions.explanation: Australian uranium for India is supplied under IAEA safeguards.

sources.title: News on AIR: India and Australia sign deals on uranium supply

questions.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes ECTA from CECA in India–Australia economic relations as of the 2026 summit?
options: CECA is operational, while ECTA remains under negotiation.
ECTA is operational, while negotiations continue toward CECA.
Both agreements remain unsigned and under negotiation.
Both agreements entered into force simultaneously in 2026.
questions.explanation: ECTA has been in force since December 2022, and talks on the broader CECA continue.

sources.title: Wikipedia: India–Australia Economic Cooperation and Trade Agreement

questions.question: Which initiative announced at the summit specifically seeks to deepen information-sharing, capability development and operational coordination at sea?
questions.explanation: The summit launched the India–Australia Maritime Security Collaboration Roadmap.

sources.title: Third India-Australia Annual Summit Joint Statement

questions.question: Australia’s support for India’s human spaceflight programme at the 2026 Annual Summit included cooperation related to which mission?
questions.explanation: Australia supports Gaganyaan, including a temporary tracking terminal on the Cocos (Keeling) Islands.

sources.title: Third India-Australia Annual Summit Joint Statement

questions.question: As per the passage, which of the following best distinguishes governance of the Arctic from that of Antarctica?
options: The Arctic is administered directly by the United Nations
The Arctic lacks a single comprehensive regional treaty regime
The Arctic prohibits sovereign claims by surrounding states
The Arctic is governed exclusively by the Arctic Council
questions.explanation: The Arctic has no comprehensive treaty like the Antarctic Treaty. It is governed by UNCLOS, national laws and soft-law bodies such as the Arctic Council.

questions.question: The Arctic Council was formally established through which of the following?
questions.explanation: The Ottawa Declaration (1996) set up the Arctic Council.

questions.question: India’s principal research station in the Arctic, Himadri, is located in:
questions.explanation: Himadri (2008) is at Ny-Ålesund, Svalbard, Norway.

questions.question: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the Arctic Council from NATO in the Greenland context?
options: Arctic Council handles collective defence; NATO focuses on environmental cooperation
Arctic Council addresses regional cooperation; NATO has a military-security role
Both organisations possess identical mandates in the Arctic
NATO membership is restricted exclusively to the eight Arctic states
questions.explanation: The Arctic Council handles regional cooperation (it explicitly excludes military security), while NATO is a military alliance.

questions.question: Under the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS), a coastal state's continental shelf normally extends at least to:
questions.explanation: Under UNCLOS Art. 76 the continental shelf extends to at least 200 nautical miles (up to 350 nm in some cases).

questions.question: With reference to Greenland's constitutional position, which of the following is most accurate?
options: It is an independent republic associated with Denmark
It is an autonomous territory within the Kingdom of Denmark
It is an overseas territory administered by the European Union
It is a condominium jointly governed by Denmark and the United States
questions.explanation: Greenland is an autonomous territory within the Kingdom of Denmark.

questions.question: What was the principal reason cited by the Kerala Legislative Assembly for changing the State's name from “Kerala” to “Keralam”?
options: Keralam was the name adopted by the States Reorganisation Commission
Keralam is the name of the State in the Malayalam language
Keralam was the name used in the original Constitution of India
Keralam was the official name used during British administration
questions.explanation: The Assembly's resolution said the State is called 'Keralam' in Malayalam.

questions.question: Which Article of the Constitution empowers Parliament to alter the name of an existing State?
questions.explanation: Article 3(e) empowers Parliament to alter the name of any State.

questions.question: Consider the following events relating to the Kerala (Alteration of Name) Bill, 2026: 1. Passed by the Rajya Sabha 2. Introduced in the Lok Sabha 3. Received Presidential assent 4. Passed by the Lok Sabha Which is the correct chronological order?
questions.explanation: The bill was introduced in and passed by the Lok Sabha, then passed by the Rajya Sabha, then received assent.

sources.title: Passage-based (Lok Sabha passed first, Rajya Sabha next day)

questions.question: The Kerala (Alteration of Name) Act, 2026 primarily amended which Schedule of the Constitution to replace “Kerala” with “Keralam” as the name of the State?
questions.explanation: State names are in the First Schedule.

questions.question: Why did the renaming of Kerala as Keralam not require a constitutional amendment under Article 368?
options: Because State names can be altered without making any change to the Constitution
Because Article 4 excludes laws made under Article 3 from the scope of Article 368
Because Article 368 applies only to amendments affecting Fundamental Rights
Because the President may alter the First Schedule without approval of Parliament
questions.explanation: Art. 4(2) says laws under Arts. 2 and 3 are not Art. 368 amendments, even though they change the First and Fourth Schedules.

questions.question: India's Ethanol Blended Petrol Programme is administered primarily under which Union Ministry?
options: Ministry of New and Renewable Energy
Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas
Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare
questions.explanation: The Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas runs the Ethanol Blended Petrol Programme through oil marketing companies.

questions.question: Which category of vehicles is required to fully meet E20 emission standards in India?
questions.explanation: Vehicles built to BS-VI (Phase II, from April 2023) are designed to be E20-compliant.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT used or permitted as a feedstock for ethanol production under India’s ethanol programme?
questions.explanation: Ethanol feedstocks include sugarcane juice and molasses, maize and surplus or damaged grains. Coal is not one of them.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a major objective of India's Ethanol Blended Petrol Programme?
options: Reducing dependence on imported crude oil
Providing additional support to the agricultural sector
Reducing the environmental impact of fossil fuels
Increasing dependence on imported automotive fuels
questions.explanation: The programme aims to cut dependence on imported fuel, not increase it.

questions.question: Which country remained India's largest supplier of crude oil in 2026?
questions.explanation: Kpler data show Russia stayed India's largest crude supplier through 2026, with a record share of over 50% in mid-2026.

sources.title: ThePrint: Russia's share in India's crude imports hits fresh high in July

questions.question: PM JI-VAN Yojana, which complements India’s biofuel and ethanol strategy, primarily supports projects producing:
options: Advanced biofuels from lignocellulosic biomass and other renewable feedstocks
Conventional fuels from domestically extracted crude oil and natural gas
Green hydrogen from renewable electricity and water electrolysis
Biodiesel from vegetable oils, used cooking oil and animal fats
questions.explanation: PM JI-VAN Yojana (2019) funds second-generation (advanced) ethanol from lignocellulosic biomass and other renewable feedstocks.

questions.question: NASA's invitation to ISRO to join its Moon Base Programme was made during which bilateral mechanism?
options: India–U.S. Civil Space Joint Working Group
questions.explanation: NASA invited ISRO to its Moon Base programme at the 9th India–US Civil Space Joint Working Group meeting (5–6 August 2026).

questions.question: The India–U.S. space cooperation meeting in 2026 was held at:
questions.explanation: The meeting was held at ISRO Headquarters, Bengaluru.

sources.title: Space.com: India-US space ties deepen as NASA invites ISRO to join moon base program

questions.question: India's prospective cooperation with NASA's Moon Base Programme builds primarily on its existing partnership under:

sources.title: News on AIR: NASA invites ISRO under Artemis Accords

questions.question: Who is regarded as the founding father of the Indian Space Programme?
questions.explanation: Vikram Sarabhai is regarded as the father of the Indian space programme.

questions.question: Which joint NASA–ISRO mission, successfully launched before the 2026 discussions, was specifically mentioned while the two sides discussed expanding future cooperation?
questions.explanation: NISAR, the joint NASA–ISRO radar satellite, launched in July 2025. The other missions were ISRO-only.

questions.question: Which provision was inserted by the First Constitutional Amendment to enable the State to make special provisions for socially and educationally backward classes and for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes?
questions.explanation: The First Amendment (1951) inserted Article 15(4) after Champakam Dorairajan.

sources.title: Wikipedia: First Amendment of the Constitution of India

questions.question: Which Schedule of the Constitution was added by the First Constitutional Amendment?

sources.title: Wikipedia: First Amendment of the Constitution of India

questions.question: In which case did the Supreme Court uphold the constitutional validity of the First Constitutional Amendment soon after its enactment?
options: Sajjan Singh v. State of Rajasthan
Shankari Prasad v. Union of India
Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala
Minerva Mills v. Union of India
questions.explanation: Shankari Prasad v. Union of India (1951) upheld the First Amendment.

sources.title: Wikipedia: Shankari Prasad v. Union of India

questions.question: The Constitution (First Amendment) Bill, 1951 was introduced by:
questions.explanation: PM Jawaharlal Nehru introduced the First Amendment Bill in the Provisional Parliament in May 1951.

sources.title: Wikipedia: First Amendment of the Constitution of India

questions.question: Which one of the following was among the principal types of legislation initially sought to be protected through Articles 31A and 31B?
questions.explanation: Articles 31A and 31B were meant to protect zamindari abolition and land reform laws.

sources.title: Wikipedia: First Amendment of the Constitution of India

questions.question: The First Amendment added which new ground for restricting speech under Article 19(2)?
questions.explanation: The First Amendment added 'public order', 'friendly relations with foreign States' and 'incitement to an offence' to Art. 19(2).

sources.title: Wikipedia: First Amendment of the Constitution of India

questions.question: The rural employment framework discussed in the passage replaced which of the following legislations?
options: Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act, 2005
questions.explanation: VB-G RAM G replaced MGNREGA, 2005.

sources.title: Swarajya: VB-G RAM G replaces MGNREGA

questions.question: The constitutional directive most directly associated with the State making provision for securing the “right to work” is contained in:
questions.explanation: Article 41 (DPSP) directs the State to secure the right to work.

questions.question: The passage refers to the role of Gram Panchayats in rural employment planning. Which Constitutional Amendment gave constitutional status to Panchayati Raj Institutions?
questions.explanation: The 73rd Amendment (1992) gave constitutional status to Panchayati Raj.

questions.question: Under VB-G RAM G, what is the Centre-State fund-sharing ratio applicable to most States?
questions.explanation: Most States share costs with the Centre 60:40. NE and Himalayan States share 90:10.

sources.title: Viksit Bharat – G RAM G Act, 2025 (fund-sharing)

questions.question: For administrative purposes, VB-G RAM G is structured as which of the following?
questions.explanation: With Centre–State cost-sharing, VB-G RAM G is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme.

sources.title: Viksit Bharat – G RAM G Act, 2025

questions.question: If an eligible worker demands employment under VB-G RAM G, employment must ordinarily be provided within:
questions.explanation: Work must be provided within 15 days of a demand, or an unemployment allowance is due.

questions.question: The institutional origins of the G7 are most closely associated with:
options: Coordinating responses to economic and financial disruptions
Managing collective responses to military confrontations
Promoting regional integration among neighbouring states
Supervising implementation of multilateral legal obligations
questions.explanation: The G7 began (as the G6 at Rambouillet, 1975) to coordinate responses to the oil shock and financial instability of the 1970s.

questions.question: Which of the following countries is not a member of G7?
questions.explanation: The G7 members are the US, UK, France, Germany, Italy, Japan and Canada (with the EU taking part). Australia is not a member.

questions.question: The Indian Ocean Rim Association (IORA), referred to in the passage, has its Secretariat in:
questions.explanation: The IORA Secretariat is in Mauritius (Ebene, near Port Louis).

questions.question: The expression "Global South" generally refers to:
options: Countries located south of the Equator
questions.explanation: 'Global South' means developing and emerging economies. It is a political-economic term, not a strictly geographic one.

questions.question: At the G7 Outreach Session 2026, India argued that the world's most pressing challenge is:
options: A deficit of strategic natural resources
A growing deficit of mutual trust among nations
A major concern in technological innovation
questions.explanation: At the Évian outreach session (16 June 2026) Modi said the world's biggest challenge is not a lack of resources but a growing deficit of trust.

sources.title: The Statesman: Trust deficit, not resource scarcity, biggest challenge – Modi at G7

questions.question: The Indus Waters Treaty was signed in Karachi between India and Pakistan during the tenure of:
options: Lal Bahadur Shastri and Ayub Khan
questions.explanation: Nehru and Ayub Khan signed the Indus Waters Treaty in Karachi on 19 September 1960, with the World Bank as broker.

questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the Permanent Court of Arbitration?
options: A principal judicial organ of the United Nations
A specialised agency of the United Nations
A subsidiary organ of the Security Council
questions.explanation: The PCA (The Hague, 1899) is an independent intergovernmental organisation, not a UN organ.

questions.question: Which among the following pairs is correctly matched?
questions.explanation: The Ratle project is on the Chenab. Kishenganga is on the Kishenganga (Neelum), a Jhelum tributary.

questions.question: The expression "transboundary river" refers to a river that:
options: Flows across the territory of more than one sovereign state
Originates outside a country's territory and create border between two countries
questions.explanation: A transboundary river flows across the territory of more than one sovereign state.

questions.question: Which of the following rivers does NOT originate in India?
questions.explanation: The Sutlej rises near Lake Rakshastal in Tibet. The Ravi, Beas and Chenab rise in Himachal Pradesh.

questions.question: The dispute concerning pondage limits is most closely associated with which aspect of hydroelectric power generation?
questions.explanation: Pondage is the limited storage a run-of-river plant may keep, so the dispute is about reservoir storage regulation under the Treaty.

questions.question: The constitutional amendment that granted statehood to Sikkim was:
questions.explanation: The 36th Amendment Act, 1975 made Sikkim a full State. The 35th (1974) had made it an 'associate state'.

questions.question: Before attaining statehood in 1975, Sikkim was most accurately described as:
questions.explanation: Under the 1950 Indo-Sikkim Treaty Sikkim was an Indian protectorate (briefly an associate state in 1974–75). It was never a UT, a Part B State or a Portuguese colony.

questions.question: Which of the following mountain passes connects Sikkim with the Tibet Autonomous Region of China?
questions.explanation: Nathu La links Sikkim with Tibet. Zoji La is in Ladakh/J&K, Shipki La in HP and Lipulekh in Uttarakhand.

questions.question: Which of the following statements regarding Sikkim is/are correct? 1. It is the only Indian state sharing borders with China, Nepal, and Bhutan. 2. Kanchenjunga National Park is India's first UNESCO Mixed World Heritage Site is situated here. 3. Mount Kanchenjunga, located partly in Sikkim, is the highest mountain peak physically located within Indian territories. Select the correct answer using the code below:
questions.explanation: All three are correct. Sikkim alone borders China, Nepal and Bhutan; Khangchendzonga NP (2016) is India's first mixed World Heritage Site; and Kangchenjunga is the highest peak within India's administered territory.

questions.question: The Calcutta Convention of 1890 is significant because it:
options: Made Sikkim a princely state of British India
questions.explanation: The 1890 Convention of Calcutta (Britain–China) fixed the Sikkim–Tibet boundary and recognised Britain's protectorate over Sikkim.

questions.question: The Kalapani-Limpiyadhura dispute between India and Nepal is associated with differing interpretations of:
questions.explanation: The Kalapani–Limpiyadhura dispute turns on how the Sugauli Treaty (1815–16) defines the source of the Kali river.

questions.question: The Jayanagar–Kurtha railway line connects India with Nepal through which Indian state?
questions.explanation: The Jaynagar–Kurtha line runs from Jaynagar in Bihar to Janakpur/Kurtha in Nepal.

questions.question: Which among the following country or territory does NOT share a border with Nepal?
questions.explanation: Nepal borders only India and China (Tibet). Bhutan is separated from it by Sikkim.

questions.question: Which one of the following organizations is cited as increasingly relevant because it bypasses the limitations of SAARC?
questions.explanation: BIMSTEC and BBIN are seen as sub-regional alternatives that get around SAARC's paralysis.

questions.question: The recently launched UPI–NPI linkage primarily seeks to:
options: Enable seamless cross-border digital payments and remittances between India and Nepal
Establish a common framework for settlement of bilateral trade in local currencies
Create an integrated digital platform for customs, immigration and border management
Facilitate interoperability between the central bank digital currencies (CBDCs) of both countries
questions.explanation: Linking UPI with Nepal's National Payments Interface (NPI) enables cross-border P2P payments and remittances.

questions.question: Which of the following combinations correctly matches the river and associated issue?
questions.explanation: The Pancheshwar Multipurpose Project is on the Mahakali under the 1996 Mahakali Treaty.

questions.question: Which specific government office is responsible for releasing the revised Wholesale Price Index (WPI) series with the base year 2022-23 on June 15, 2026?
options: Department of Economic Affairs (DEA), Ministry of Finance
Tariff Commission, Ministry of Commerce and Industry
questions.explanation: The Office of the Economic Adviser, DPIIT compiles and releases the WPI, including the new 2022–23 series.

questions.question: The Producer Price Index (PPI) differs from the Consumer Price Index (CPI) primarily because it measures:
questions.explanation: A PPI measures prices producers receive. The CPI measures prices consumers pay.

questions.question: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
questions.explanation: The WPI tracks wholesale-stage prices. The other pairs are mismatched.

questions.question: Under the first phase of the Service Producer Price Index (Service PPI), which of the following services are included in the basket? 1. Banking and Insurance 2. Management of Pension Funds 3. Railways and Air (Passenger) 4. Port Trust Charges and Warehousing 5. Telecom and Securities Transaction Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
questions.explanation: The first-phase Service PPI covers banking, securities transactions, insurance, pension fund management, railways, air (passenger) and telecom. Port trust charges and warehousing are not included.

questions.question: Along with the revised WPI series launched on June 15, 2026, the government is releasing new Producer Price Indices (PPI) to track price movements. This strategic transition directly aligns with the institutional recommendations of which global body?
questions.explanation: The move to PPIs follows IMF guidance (the PPI Manual and SDDS standards) on producer-price statistics.

questions.question: Gross Value of Output (GVO), referred to in the revised methodology, is most closely associated with:
questions.explanation: Gross Value of Output is a national income accounting concept (output weights for GVA/PPI).

questions.question: Which one of the following statements regarding Harappan art is incorrect?
options: Bronze sculptures were commonly produced using the lost-wax casting technique.
Most Harappan seals were made of steatite and frequently depicted animal motifs.
Monumental stone temples formed the dominant architectural feature of Harappan cities.
Terracotta figurines were among the most commonly discovered artefacts.
questions.explanation: Harappan cities had no monumental stone temples. Lost-wax bronzes, steatite seals with animal motifs and abundant terracotta figurines are all typical.

questions.question: Consider the following statements: 1) The Dancing Girl is made of bronze. 2) The Priest-King sculpture is made of steatite. 3) Both artefacts were discovered at Mohenjodaro. Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: The bronze Dancing Girl and the steatite Priest-King were both found at Mohenjodaro.

questions.question: In the context of the geographical extent of the Indus Valley Civilisation and debates surrounding ancient river systems, the Ghaggar–Hakra river is often identified by several scholars with the:
questions.explanation: Many scholars identify the Ghaggar–Hakra with the Vedic Saraswati.

questions.question: The criticism against the modified depiction of the Dancing Girl was primarily based on the argument that it:
options: Reduced the artistic value of the sculpture.
Ignored UNESCO guidelines on heritage conservation.
questions.explanation: Critics said the altered image misrepresented the archaeological evidence, a matter of historical accuracy.

questions.question: Match the following Harappan sites with their present locations: Site State/Country A. Rakhigarhi I. Gujarat B. Lothal II. Haryana C. Mohenjodaro III. Uttar Pradesh D. Alamgirpur IV. Pakistan Choose the correct code:
questions.explanation: Rakhigarhi is in Haryana, Lothal in Gujarat, Mohenjodaro in Pakistan (Sindh) and Alamgirpur in Uttar Pradesh.

sources.title: Wikipedia: List of Indus Valley Civilisation sites

questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding the Right to Be Forgotten: 1) It is an absolute constitutional right. 2) It may be restricted where disclosure serves a legitimate public interest. 3) Courts generally balance it with freedom of speech and expression. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: The right to be forgotten is not absolute. It gives way to legitimate public interest and is weighed against free speech.

questions.question: Which one of the following situations is least likely to justify the application of the Right to Be Forgotten?
options: Removal of obsolete personal information causing disproportionate harm.
Restricting access to acquittal records where continued publication unjustifiably affects reputation.
Seeking deletion of information that remains relevant to public interest and accountability.
Removal of unnecessary personal identifiers from publicly accessible records.
questions.explanation: Information still relevant to public interest and accountability is the weakest case for erasure.

questions.question: The constitutional foundation of the Right to be Forgotten in India primarily flows from the Supreme Court's judgment in:
options: Justice K.S. Puttaswamy v. Union of India
Shreya Singhal v. Union of India
Maneka Gandhi v. Union of India
questions.explanation: Puttaswamy (2017), which recognised informational privacy under Art. 21, is the foundation of the right to be forgotten.

sources.title: Wikipedia: Puttaswamy v. Union of India

questions.question: Which of the following statements regarding the Right to Shelter is correct?
options: It is expressly mentioned as a Fundamental Right in Part III of the Constitution.
It has been judicially recognised as part of the Right to Life under Article 21.
It is exclusively derived from the Directive Principles of State Policy.
It is available only to Indian citizens.
questions.explanation: Courts have read the right to shelter into Art. 21 (e.g. Chameli Singh, 1996). It is not expressly listed in Part III.

sources.title: Chameli Singh v. State of U.P. (1996)

questions.question: Which of the following statements regarding the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 is correct?
options: It expressly recognises the Right to be Forgotten as a statutory right.
It does not expressly mention the Right to be Forgotten.
It provides an absolute right to erase all personal data from the internet.
It abolishes the Right to Privacy recognised under Article 21.
questions.explanation: The DPDP Act, 2023 gives a right to correction and erasure (s.12) but does not expressly name a 'right to be forgotten'.

sources.title: Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023, Section 12

questions.question: The recent Delhi High Court decision concerning the Right to be Forgotten primarily underscored the need to strike a balance between:
options: Judicial transparency through the principle of open justice and an individual's right to informational privacy.
Freedom of speech and expression under Article 19(1)(a) and the State's power to impose reasonable restrictions.
The constitutional principle of open courts and the independence of the judiciary from executive interference.
The public's right to access judicial records and the constitutional guarantee of freedom of the press.
questions.explanation: The Delhi High Court weighed open justice and transparency of court records against informational privacy.

questions.question: Which one of the following best explains the immediate oceanic process that characterises the onset of an El Niño event?
options: Weakening of westerly trade winds causing increased upwelling along South America.
Weakening of easterly trade winds allowing warm surface waters to move eastward.
Cooling of sea surface temperatures across the central Pacific Ocean.
Intensification of the Indian Ocean Dipole over the Arabian Sea.
questions.explanation: El Niño begins when the easterly trade winds weaken and warm water moves east.

questions.question: The rich fisheries along the western coast of South America are primarily supported by:
questions.explanation: Upwelling of cold, nutrient-rich water (Humboldt Current) supports the rich Peruvian fisheries.

questions.question: Consider the following statements: 1) El Niño is associated with warmer-than-normal sea surface temperatures in the eastern Pacific. 2) It generally strengthens the Walker Circulation. 3) It may contribute to higher global average temperatures. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: El Niño warms the eastern Pacific and can raise global temperatures, but it weakens the Walker Circulation rather than strengthening it.

questions.question: Which crop is generally considered most vulnerable to a deficient southwest monsoon associated with El Niño?
questions.explanation: Rice, a water-intensive kharif crop, is most exposed to a weak southwest monsoon. Wheat, mustard and barley are rabi crops.

questions.question: Which one of the following climatic indicators would be most appropriate for assessing departures from normal sea surface temperatures in the equatorial Pacific while forecasting ENSO events?
questions.explanation: The Oceanic Niño Index tracks sea-surface temperature anomalies in the Niño 3.4 region. The SOI measures pressure.

questions.question: Match the following Phenomenon Characteristic A. El Niño I. Suppressed coastal upwelling off Peru and Ecuador B. El Niño Modoki II. Maximum warming concentrated over the central Pacific Ocean C. La Niña III. Cooler-than-normal sea surface temperatures in the eastern equatorial Pacific Choose the correct answer:
questions.explanation: El Niño suppresses upwelling off Peru and Ecuador. El Niño Modoki has peak warming in the central Pacific. La Niña brings a cooler eastern Pacific.

questions.question: India and the United States cooperate under the Quad along with which two countries?
questions.explanation: The Quad is India, the US, Japan and Australia.

questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding defence cooperation between India and the United States: 1) India conducts the Yudh Abhyas exercise with the United States Army. 2) Tiger Triumph is a bilateral tri-service exercise. 3) Cope India is a bilateral naval exercise. Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Yudh Abhyas is the army exercise and Tiger Triumph the tri-service exercise. Cope India is an air force exercise, not naval.

questions.question: The 250th anniversary of U.S. Independence commemorates the adoption of:
questions.explanation: The 250th anniversary (4 July 2026) marks the Declaration of Independence of 1776.

sources.title: Wikipedia: United States Declaration of Independence

questions.question: Under the 2026 Interim Trade Framework between India and the United States, tariffs on many Indian goods were reduced to approximately:
questions.explanation: Under the February 2026 interim framework, US reciprocal tariffs on Indian goods fell to 18% and the extra 25% Russian-oil duty was removed.

sources.title: Business Today: Reciprocal tariffs on India to come down to 18%

questions.question: The India–Nordic Summit primarily serves as a platform to strengthen cooperation between India and:
options: The member states of the European Union.
questions.explanation: The India–Nordic Summit brings together India and the five Nordic countries (Denmark, Finland, Iceland, Norway, Sweden).

questions.question: Which one of the following sectors featured prominently in discussions at the India–Nordic Summit 2026?
questions.explanation: Digital public infrastructure, along with AI and digitalisation, was a stated area of cooperation in the 2026 joint statement.

questions.question: Under the proposed India–Nordic defence industrial collaboration, Nordic defence firms have been offered up to what percentage of Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) in India's Defence Industrial Corridors?
questions.explanation: Nordic defence firms were invited into India's defence industrial corridors, where 100% FDI is offered in select sectors.

questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding the India–Nordic Partnership: 1) The first India–Nordic Summit was held in 2018. 2) The Third India–Nordic Summit was held in Oslo. 3) India–Nordic relations were elevated to a Green Technology and Innovation Strategic Partnership. Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: All three are correct: the 1st summit was in Stockholm (2018), the 3rd in Oslo (May 2026), and ties became a Green Technology and Innovation Strategic Partnership.

sources.title: Tribune: India, Nordic nations elevate ties

questions.question: Which of the following is the title of India's Arctic Policy, released in 2022?
options: India and the Arctic: Building a Partnership for Sustainable Development
India's Vision for the Arctic: Climate, Cooperation and Connectivity
Arctic Strategy for a Sustainable Future
India's Polar Policy: Towards Global Climate Cooperation
questions.explanation: India's 2022 Arctic Policy is titled 'India and the Arctic: Building a Partnership for Sustainable Development'.

questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding India's cooperation with Nordic countries: 1) India collaborates with Norway in geothermal energy and fisheries. 2) India partners with Iceland in the blue economy and Arctic cooperation. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Geothermal energy is Iceland's speciality, not Norway's, so 1 is wrong. India works with Iceland on the blue economy and Arctic issues.

questions.question: On which date did Dr. Rajendra Prasad announce that Vande Mataram would be honoured as the National Song?
questions.explanation: On 24 January 1950 Dr Rajendra Prasad told the Constituent Assembly that Vande Mataram would be honoured equally with Jana Gana Mana as the National Song.

questions.question: Where did nearly 40,000 people gather to sing Vande Mataram in protest during the anti-partition movement in 1905?
questions.explanation: On 7 August 1905 a huge Swadeshi meeting at Calcutta Town Hall sang Vande Mataram in protest against the Partition of Bengal.

questions.question: Which Article of the Constitution asks citizens to respect the National Flag and National Anthem?
questions.explanation: Article 51A(a) makes it a fundamental duty to respect the Constitution, the National Flag and the National Anthem.

questions.question: In which novel was the poem "Vande Mataram" first published as part of the narrative?
questions.explanation: Vande Mataram appears in Bankim Chandra's novel Anandamath (1882).

questions.question: Identify the renowned literary figure credited with composing the lyrics of India's National Song, 'Vande Mataram'.
questions.explanation: Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay (Chatterjee) wrote Vande Mataram.

questions.question: In which literary journal was Vande Mataram first published.
questions.explanation: It first appeared in Bankim's journal Bangadarshan, where Anandamath was serialised (1881–82).

questions.question: The establishment of IN-SPACe (Indian National Space Promotion and Authorisation Centre) reflects which policy shift in India's
options: Complete privatisation of ISRO's core functions
A move to permit and regulate private sector participation in space activities
Transfer of space research responsibilities to state governments
Merger of ISRO with the Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO)
questions.explanation: IN-SPACe (2020) is the single-window body that promotes, authorises and regulates private space activity. ISRO was not privatised.
