questions.question: Which semiconductor-related achievement was presented to the Honourable PM during the Semicon India 2025 event?
options: Indigenous 250nm process technology for RF GaN HEMT
questions.explanation: At Semicon India 2025 the PM was presented ISRO-SCL's indigenous 32-bit Vikram 3201 space-grade processor.

questions.question: Which mission made India the fourth nation to demonstrate autonomous docking and undocking in space?
questions.explanation: SpaDeX (Space Docking Experiment, docking in January 2025) made India the fourth country to demonstrate space docking.

questions.question: Into which orbit will the LVM3-M6 mission place the BlueBird Block-2 satellite?
questions.explanation: LVM3-M6 (December 2025) put AST SpaceMobile's BlueBird Block-2 communication satellite into low Earth orbit.

questions.question: Who developed the LVM3 launch vehicle?
questions.explanation: ISRO developed LVM3 (formerly GSLV Mk III).

questions.question: What is the name of India's upcoming manned spaceflight programme? Options:
questions.explanation: Gaganyaan is India's human spaceflight programme. Vostok, Artemis and Shenzhou belong to the USSR, US and China.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a stated demand or position of Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu ?
options: Israel and the US are fully aligned in their objectives to contain Iran
Dismantling Hezbollah remains a key priority for Israel
Israel will withdraw its troops from Lebanon once a ceasefire is confirmed
Israel will not comply with Hezbollah's call to withdraw its troops beyond the border
questions.explanation: Netanyahu's stated positions were alignment with the US, dismantling Hezbollah and refusing to pull troops back. Promising withdrawal from Lebanon after a ceasefire was not one of them.

questions.question: Which country played the role of a key mediator in facilitating fresh US-Iran peace talks?
questions.explanation: Pakistan hosted and mediated the US–Iran talks in Islamabad (April 2026, led by US VP Vance and Iranian Speaker Qalibaf).

sources.title: Gulf News: 3-way talks with the US and Iran begin in Pakistan

questions.question: Which international body called a special session to discuss the status of Iran's nuclear reactors under fire?
questions.explanation: The IAEA Board of Governors (the UN nuclear watchdog) meets on the safety of nuclear facilities under attack.

questions.question: Where was the Supreme Leader's compound that was destroyed in the airstrike?
questions.explanation: The Supreme Leader's office and residence compound is in central Tehran.

sources.title: Wikipedia: Office of the Supreme Leader of Iran

questions.question: In which year did the Islamic Revolution take place in Iran?
questions.explanation: The Islamic Revolution in Iran took place in 1979.

questions.question: When election candidates use social media for campaigning, which regulatory body has jurisdiction?
options: Both ECI and IT Ministry depending on the issue
questions.explanation: The ECI enforces the Model Code (and pre-certification of political ads) on social media, while MeitY handles takedowns under the IT Act. Jurisdiction depends on the issue.

sources.title: ECI: Social media guidelines for MCC

questions.question: Which Constitutional Amendment Bill was introduced to provide the framework for simultaneous elections?
questions.explanation: The Constitution (129th Amendment) Bill, 2024 was introduced in December 2024 for simultaneous elections, along with the UT Laws (Amendment) Bill.

questions.question: What is the primary objective of the "One Nation, One Election" initiative regarding government finances?
options: To increase the budget allocation for political parties
To reduce the massive financial burden on the public exchequer
To eliminate funding for security personnel during elections
To increase the frequency of election expenditures
questions.explanation: A main aim is to cut the heavy recurring cost of frequent elections to the exchequer.

sources.title: High Level Committee (Kovind) Report on Simultaneous Elections, 2024

questions.question: Which constitutional authority is responsible for conducting elections to Local Bodies (Panchayats and Municipalities)?
questions.explanation: State Election Commissions conduct Panchayat and Municipal elections (Arts. 243K, 243ZA).

questions.question: How many states and Union Territories does India have, as of March 2026? Options:
questions.explanation: India has 28 States and 8 Union Territories (since the 2020 merger of Dadra & Nagar Haveli and Daman & Diu).

sources.title: Wikipedia: States and union territories of India

questions.question: Which court will now review the Sattankulam death penalty verdict? Options:
questions.explanation: A Sessions Court death sentence must be confirmed by the High Court, here the Madras High Court (Madurai Bench).

questions.question: Which Constitutional Article provides that no person shall be deprived of his life or personal liberty except according to procedure established by law?
questions.explanation: This is Article 21.

questions.question: What is the status of India regarding the United Nations Convention against Torture (UNCAT)?
questions.explanation: India signed UNCAT in 1997 but has not ratified it.

sources.title: Wikipedia: United Nations Convention against Torture

questions.question: What is the NHRC guideline regarding reporting of custodial death or rape?
questions.explanation: NHRC guidelines require custodial deaths and custodial rapes to be reported to it within 24 hours.

questions.question: Who were the victims in the Sattankulam custodial death case?
questions.explanation: The Sattankulam (2020) victims were father and son P. Jayaraj and J. Bennix.

sources.title: Wikipedia: Death of Jayaraj and Bennix

questions.question: The freeze on the readjustment of parliamentary constituency boundaries in India, which was initially mandated to remain unaltered based on the 1971 Census figures, was established by which of the following Constitutional Amendment Acts?
questions.explanation: The 42nd Amendment (1976) froze seat allocation on the 1971 Census until 2000. The 84th Amendment (2001) extended the freeze to 2026. (Matches official key.)

questions.question: The Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill, 2026, recently failed to pass in the Lok Sabha. Which of the following best explains the primary political objection raised by opponents that led to the defeat of this legislation?
options: Southern states feared losing parliamentary seats because population-based delimitation penalizes effective population control.
Southern states demanded a higher, disproportionate quota for women to offset their smaller total demographic share.
Southern states opposed using the 2011 Census data, insisting on a freeze until the 2021 Census is officially released.
Southern states resisted the immediate 2029 timeline, arguing their state assemblies needed more representation as they perform effectively in population control.
questions.explanation: Southern States objected that population-based delimitation on the 2011 Census would cut their share of seats as a penalty for successful population control. (Matches official key.)

sources.title: LiveLaw: Lok Sabha rejects Constitution (131st) Amendment Bill 2026

questions.question: The collapse of the Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill, 2026, in the Lok Sabha due to the failure to secure a special majority directly necessitated the immediate withdrawal of which of the following sets of dependent statutory legislations?
options: The Delimitation Bill, 2026; the Union Territories Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026; and the Women's Reservation (Implementation) Bill, 2026
The Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill, 2026; the Union Territories Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026; and the Delimitation Bill, 2026
The Nari Shakti Vandan Bill, 2026; the Southern States Protection Bill, 2026; and the Census Linkage Bill, 2026
The Parliamentary Boundaries Bill, 2026; the Representation of the People (Amendment) Bill, 2026; and the Delimitation Bill, 2026
questions.explanation: After the 131st Amendment Bill fell short of the special majority (298–230) on 17 April 2026, the government withdrew the linked Delimitation Bill, 2026 and the Union Territories Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026. (Matches official key.)

questions.question: The Supreme Court of India ruled that while orders of the Delimitation Commission carry the force of law, they can still be subjected to judicial review if they are demonstrated to be clearly arbitrary and in violation of core constitutional values. Under which of the following landmark cases was this legal principle established?
questions.explanation: In Kishorchandra Chhanganlal Rathod v. Union of India (2024) the Supreme Court held that Delimitation Commission orders can be judicially reviewed if manifestly arbitrary or against constitutional values. (Matches official key.)

sources.title: Kishorchandra Chhanganlal Rathod v. Union of India (2024)

questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding the provisions of the Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam (106th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2023): 1. It mandates a 33% reservation for women in the Lok Sabha, State Legislative Assemblies, and the Rajya Sabha. 2. The Act provides a horizontal sub-quota for women belonging to Scheduled Castes (SC) and Scheduled Tribes (ST), but does not carve out a separate reservation for women from Other Backward Classes (OBCs). 3. The reserved seats are subject to rotation after every delimitation cycle and operate under a sunset clause that automatically terminates the reservation after 15 years unless extended by Parliament. Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Statement 1 is wrong because the reservation does not cover the Rajya Sabha. Statement 2 is right: there is an SC/ST sub-quota but no OBC sub-quota. Statement 3 is right: seats rotate after each delimitation and the reservation lapses after 15 years unless extended. (Matches official key.)

questions.question: The term "Yellow Line," which has been prominently featured in international defense and security news, is best described by which of the following statements?
options: A maritime boundary corridor established in the Mediterranean Sea to protect Israel's offshore natural gas rigs.
A strategic military demarcation and fortified buffer zone utilized by the Israel Defense Forces (IDF) within hostile territory.
A cyber-defense perimeter managed by Israel’s Unit 8200 to block incoming malware targeting critical infrastructure.
A specialized humanitarian transit corridor set up by the Israeli government to evacuate foreign nationals during crises.
questions.explanation: The 'Yellow Line' is the IDF's fortified demarcation and buffer line inside Gaza (later copied in southern Lebanon), behind which Israel keeps control. (Matches official key.)

sources.title: Al Jazeera: 'Yellow line', the de facto Israeli buffer zone shaping life in Gaza

questions.question: Under the "Gaza Model" applied to southern Lebanon during the 10-day ceasefire that began on April 16, how far does Israel's forward buffer zone extend?
options: Up to the Blue Line border coordinates monitored by UNIFIL.
Exactly 5 kilometers north of the Metula salient.
Up to the Awali River basin perimeter.
questions.explanation: Under the 'Gaza model' applied in southern Lebanon, Israel's forward buffer zone reached the Litani River. (Matches official key.)

questions.question: According to security analysts and experts cited in the article, what exact percentage of the Gaza Strip has been brought under direct Israeli military control as a result of the Yellow Line enforcement?
questions.explanation: Analysts (e.g. Forensic Architecture) estimated Israeli control at about 58% of Gaza, up from the 53% the ceasefire line originally gave. (Matches official key.)

questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding the various historical and contemporary military/political demarcation boundaries in the Middle East region: 1. The Green Line refers to the armistice lines established in 1949 following the Arab-Israeli War, serving as a political boundary separating Israel from its neighbors prior to the Six-Day War. 2. The Blue Line is a border demarcation published by the United Nations in 2000 to verify the complete withdrawal of Israeli military forces from southern Lebanon. 3. The newly introduced Yellow Line functions similarly to the political nature of the Green Line, prioritizing international administrative treaties over direct, forward military control inside hostile territory. Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: The Green Line is the 1949 armistice line, and the Blue Line is the UN's 2000 withdrawal line in Lebanon. The Yellow Line is a forward military line, not a political armistice boundary, so statement 3 is wrong. (Matches official key.)

questions.question: Under the rules of engagement enforced east of the Yellow Line inside the Gaza theater, how are these containment areas officially designated by the military?
options: Joint Administrative and Civil Cooperation Corridors
Closed military and free-fire zones where civilian access is completely restricted.
Demilitarized Humanitarian Buffers managed by neutral international watchdogs.
Special Economic Development Sectors for fast-tracked reconstruction.
questions.explanation: Areas beyond the line are treated as closed military/free-fire zones where civilians may not enter. (Matches official key.)

questions.question: During Donald Trump’s May 2025 state visit to Beijing, the trade agenda extensively focused on what Washington termed the "Three Bs"—sectors historically leveraged by China to inflict targeted economic and political pain. Which of the following correctly identifies these three sectors?
questions.explanation: The 'three Bs' are beans (soybeans), beef and Boeing, sectors China has used to apply pressure. (Matches official key.)

questions.question: According to the strategic calculation, which external geopolitical catalyst primarily forced Donald Trump to seek China’s diplomatic support and stabilize ties to mitigate rising domestic economic pain?
options: The escalation of cross-strait military maneuvers by Taiwan's ruling party
The sudden collapse of the APEC summit architecture in Busan
The Iran-U.S. war and the subsequent closure of the Strait of Hormuz
A sudden decoupling of global semiconductor supply chains led by Nvidia
questions.explanation: The Iran–US war and the closure of the Strait of Hormuz pushed up US energy costs, leading Trump to seek China's help. (Matches official key.)

questions.question: During the state banquet, President Xi Jinping raised a foundational question regarding whether the United States and China could successfully bypass a historical, structural trap that frequently dictates conflict when a rising power threatens to displace an established hegemon. What is the name of this geopolitical phenomenon?
questions.explanation: The Thucydides Trap is the tendency toward war when a rising power threatens to displace an established one.

questions.question: Though the May 2025 state visit ended without any signed agreements, a temporary economic freeze had already been established prior to the meeting. Where and when was the one-year tariff truce formally announced by both nations?
options: At the G20 Summit in New Delhi (September 2024)
At the APEC Summit in Gyeongju (October 2025)
At the World Economic Forum in Davos (January 2025)
At the East Asia Summit in Jakarta (November 2025)
questions.explanation: Trump and Xi agreed a one-year trade truce on the sidelines of APEC 2025 in South Korea (summit city Gyeongju; leaders met in Busan, October 2025).

questions.question: Which issue did Xi Jinping describe as “the most important issue in China–U.S. relations”?
questions.explanation: Xi called the Taiwan question 'the most important issue in China–US relations'. (Matches official key.)

questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding the strategic and regional implications of a potential U.S.–China "G2" arrangement highlighted as: 1. A solidified "G2" condominium would effectively restrict India's strategic autonomy and maneuvering space in the Indo-Pacific region. 2. The "G2" concept is viewed by Washington as an alternative framework to completely bypass and replace traditional, highly personalized bilateral leadership meetings. 3. The rise of a "G2" paradigm directly shapes global energy security conversations, forcing major importing nations to look for ways to diversify away from vulnerabilities like the Strait of Hormuz. Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements 1 (a G2 squeezes India's strategic space) and 3 (energy-security and Hormuz diversification) are correct. Statement 2 misdescribes the G2 as a replacement for leader-level meetings. (Matches official key.)

questions.question: The Unified Payments Interface (UPI) completed its 10th anniversary in April 2026. Which of the following bodies handles the direct regulatory oversight of this platform, and which entity launched it?
options: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) and NITI Aayog
Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) and State Bank of India (SBI)
National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development (NABARD) and NPCI
Reserve Bank of India (RBI) and National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI)
questions.explanation: NPCI launched UPI (11 April 2016) and the RBI regulates it.

questions.question: When the Unified Payments Interface (UPI) was launched in April 2016, who was the Governor of the Reserve Bank of India?
questions.explanation: Raghuram Rajan was RBI Governor (2013–Sept 2016) when UPI launched in April 2016.

questions.question: What is the primary operational objective of the "BhashaDaan" initiative launched under the broader BHASHINI ecosystem?
options: Distributing monetary subsidies directly to rural bank accounts
Collecting speech, text, and translations from citizens to train AI systems
Providing free internet bandwidth to remote educational institutions
Training bank employees in sign language communication
questions.explanation: BhashaDaan crowdsources speech, text and translations from citizens to train Indian-language AI models.

questions.question: How many banks were live on the UPI network as of March 2026 compared to its launch in April 2016?
options: 21 banks at launch, expanding to 2,264 banks
44 banks at launch, expanding to 500 banks
100 banks at launch, expanding to 700 banks
21 banks at launch, expanding to 703 banks
questions.explanation: UPI went live with 21 banks in April 2016. By March 2026 about 703 banks were live. (Matches official key.)

sources.title: LegalEdge Mock 13 answer key; NPCI UPI ecosystem statistics

questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding the international operational status and cross-border linkages of India's Unified Payments Interface (UPI) as of 2026: 1. In Singapore, the UPI ecosystem has achieved cross-border interoperability through a direct link with the local real-time payment infrastructure known as PayNow. 2. In the European theater, France has operationalized the network, focusing primarily on expanding payment acceptance for Indian tourists. 3. According to the official deployment roadmap, UPI operations are fully active across eight countries/regions, including the UAE, Bhutan, Nepal, Sri Lanka, Mauritius, and Qatar. Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: UPI is linked with Singapore's PayNow, is live in France for Indian tourists, and works in 8 countries/regions including the UAE, Bhutan, Nepal, Sri Lanka, Mauritius and Qatar. All three statements are correct. (Matches official key.)

questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding the impact of El Niño on global weather patterns: 1. It typically leads to a quieter Atlantic hurricane season. 2. It causes a bend in the jet stream, bringing wetter conditions to the southern United States. 3. It is characterized by the strengthening of trade winds along the equator. Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: El Niño suppresses Atlantic hurricanes (more wind shear) and shifts the jet stream to bring wetter weather to the southern US. It weakens trade winds rather than strengthening them.

questions.question: Which of the following atmospheric phenomena acts as 'fuel' for a Super El Niño by racing warm water eastward?
questions.explanation: Westerly wind bursts push warm water east (as Kelvin waves) and drive strong El Niños.

questions.question:
Arrange the following events in the logical sequence of El Niño formation: 1. Weakening of Trade Winds

2. Atmospheric heating and alteration of global jet streams 3. Eastward migration of warm water (Kelvin Wave) 4. Downward shift of the thermocline Select the correct order:
questions.explanation: The sequence is: trade winds weaken, warm water moves east as a Kelvin wave, the eastern thermocline deepens, and atmospheric heating alters the jet streams.

questions.question: The 'Southern Oscillation' part of ENSO refers to:
options: The southward shift of extreme temperature in Asia.
The movement of the tectonic plates in the Pacific.
questions.explanation: The Southern Oscillation is the atmospheric part: the see-saw in surface pressure between the eastern and western tropical Pacific.

questions.question: In the context of the 'Global Conveyor Belt' (Thermohaline Circulation), what are the two primary drivers of deep-ocean currents?
questions.explanation: Thermohaline circulation is driven by density differences, which depend on temperature and salinity.

questions.question: Which of the following is a warm ocean current found in the Atlantic Ocean that influences the climate of Western Europe?
questions.explanation: The Gulf Stream (North Atlantic Drift) is a warm current that moderates Western Europe's climate. The Labrador, Canary and Benguela are cold currents.

questions.question: Consider the following: 1) The Kerala Assembly requested name change across all official languages recognized in the Eighth Schedule. 2) Amendment of the First Schedule automatically requires amendment of the Eighth Schedule. 3) The Bill for renaming requires a special majority to pass. Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: The Kerala Assembly's resolution asked for 'Keralam' in the First Schedule and in all Eighth Schedule languages. Amending the First Schedule does not automatically amend the Eighth Schedule, and an Art. 3/4 law needs only a simple majority (Art. 4(2)).

questions.question: To change the name of "Kerala" to "Keralam," which Schedule of the Constitution must be amended?
questions.explanation: State names are listed in the First Schedule, which Parliament amends under Arts. 3–4.

sources.title: Constitution of India, First Schedule; Article 4

questions.question: What is the legal status of the "views" expressed by the State Legislature regarding the alteration of its name?
options: They are legally binding on Parliament.
They are not binding on Parliament.
The Parliament cannot proceed if the State Assembly rejects the proposal.
The views must be passed by a two-thirds majority in the State Assembly to be valid.
questions.explanation: Under the proviso to Art. 3, the President refers the bill to the State Legislature for its views, but those views do not bind Parliament.

questions.question: The "Keralam" resolution mentions that states were formed on a linguistic basis on 1st November 1956. Which landmark Act facilitated this reorganization?
questions.explanation: Linguistic reorganisation on 1 November 1956 came through both the States Reorganisation Act, 1956 and the Constitution (Seventh Amendment) Act, 1956.

questions.question: If the President refers a Bill for a name change to a State Legislature and the Legislature fails to express its views within the specified time limit, what is the next step?
options: The Bill is considered lapsed and must be reintroduced.
The President must grant a mandatory six-month extension.
The Bill can be introduced in either House of Parliament despite the lack of views.
The Union Cabinet must seek a stay from the Supreme Court.
questions.explanation: If the State does not give its views within the set time, the bill can still be introduced in Parliament.

questions.question: Historians and linguists widely interpret the Ashokan epigraphic designation "Keralaputra" as a direct external reference to which prominent ruling dynasty of ancient South India?
questions.explanation: 'Keralaputra' in Ashoka's Rock Edict II refers to the Chera kingdom.

questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding the National Testing Agency (NTA): 1) It is a statutory body established by an Act of Parliament in 2017. 2) It operates under the aegis of the Ministry of Education. 3) Its Governing Body solely consists of bureaucrats from the Union Government. Which of the above statement(s) is/are correct?
questions.explanation: The NTA is a society registered under the Societies Registration Act (2017), not a statutory body. It works under the Ministry of Education, and its governing body includes academics as well as officials.

questions.question: The National Testing Agency (NTA), which administers major high-stakes national entrance tests like NEET- UG and JEE-Main, operates under which of the following legislative frameworks?
options: An explicit Act of Parliament passed in 2017
As a Constitutional body under Article 315
Registered as a Society under the Societies Registration Act, 1860
As a statutory regulatory body under the University Grants Commission
questions.explanation: The NTA was set up in 2017 as a society under the Societies Registration Act, 1860.

questions.question: The High-Level Committee of Experts constituted in 2024 to suggest holistic reforms for the National Testing Agency is headed by Dr. K. Radhakrishnan. Which position did Dr. Radhakrishnan formerly hold?
options: Chairman of the Union Public Service Commission (UPSC)
Chairman of the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO)
Director of the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI)
questions.explanation: Dr K. Radhakrishnan, who chaired the 2024 NTA reform committee, is a former ISRO Chairman.

questions.question: The Dr. K. Radhakrishnan Committee recommended the creation of a "DIGI-EXAM" model to overhaul candidate identity verification. Which system's model did the committee mirror for this authentication framework?
questions.explanation: The committee proposed 'DIGI-EXAM' identity verification modelled on DigiYatra.

sources.title: Radhakrishnan Committee report on NTA reforms (Oct 2024)

questions.question: Under the Seventh Schedule of the Constitution of India, in which List is "Education" currently placed, to enact laws on it?
questions.explanation: Education is in the Concurrent List (Entry 25, List III) since the 42nd Amendment.

sources.title: Constitution of India, Seventh Schedule List III

questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding India's energy sector vulnerabilities: 1) India imports over 85% of its crude oil, exposing the economy to global pricing shocks. 2) Crude prices breaching $100 per barrel cause imported inflation by driving up local fuel and transport costs. 3) High global crude prices reduce fiscal strains on state-owned oil marketing companies by lowering under- recoveries. Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: India imports about 85–88% of its crude, and prices above $100 feed imported inflation. High crude prices increase OMC under-recoveries rather than reducing them, so 3 is false.

questions.question: Which country is the largest source of India’s gold imports, accounting for nearly 40% of the total incoming supply?
questions.explanation: Switzerland is India's largest gold import source, at roughly 40% of imports.

sources.title: Ministry of Commerce trade data (gold imports by country)

questions.question: When a country faces a high gold import bill that widens its Current Account Deficit (CAD), which policy represents the most sustainable approach to reduce its external sector pressure?
options: Liquidating national gold reserves held with the IMF to finance domestic jewelry consumption.
Mobilizing passive household gold through monetization schemes to meet local demand locally.
Banning the domestic retail trade of jewelry entirely while increasing bullion imports.
Mandating the physical confiscation of private bank lockers to settle trade imbalances.
questions.explanation: Mobilising idle household gold through monetisation schemes meets demand without fresh imports, easing the CAD.

questions.question: Which of the following macroeconomic mechanisms best explains why massive capital withdrawals by Foreign Institutional Investors (FIIs) lead to the immediate depreciation of the Indian Rupee against the US Dollar? Options:
options: FIIs inject a surplus of US Dollars into the domestic banking system, lowering the global exchange value of the Dollar.
FIIs liquidate their Indian assets and sell Rupees to buy US Dollars, creating a Rupee oversupply and a high Dollar demand.
The RBI automatically devalues the Rupee's exchange peg to make asset liquidation cheaper for exiting foreign funds.
Mass capital flight reduces India's aggregate industrial demand, physically lowering its reliance on imported petroleum products.
questions.explanation: Exiting FIIs sell rupee assets and buy dollars, so dollar demand rises and the rupee weakens.

questions.question: According to the core objectives and mechanisms of the Gold Monetisation Scheme (GMS), which of the following is NOT a designated attribute or outcome of the scheme? Options:
options: Allowing resident individuals to deposit their idle household gold with commercial banks.
Enabling banks to channel mobilized gold into the formal economy for productive purposes.
Shifts the capital account balance, forcing an asymmetric appreciation of the real effective exchange rate.
Easing long-term pressure on the national Current Account Deficit (CAD) by reducing fresh import bills.
questions.explanation: The GMS mobilises idle gold, channels it into productive use and cuts imports. Forcing appreciation of the real effective exchange rate is not one of its aims.

questions.question: Which of the following components are officially included in India’s Foreign Exchange Reserves managed by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI)? 1) Foreign Currency Assets (FCA) 2) Gold Reserves 3) Special Drawing Rights (SDRs) 4) Reserve Position with the International Monetary Fund (IMF)
questions.explanation: India's forex reserves are foreign currency assets, gold, SDRs and the reserve tranche position with the IMF.

questions.question: In which district of Madhya Pradesh is the Bhojshala-Kamal Maula Mosque complex located?
questions.explanation: The Bhojshala–Kamal Maula complex is in Dhar, Madhya Pradesh.

questions.question: Consider the following statements: 1) The Places of Worship Act, 1991 freezes the religious character of all places of worship as it existed on August 15, 1947. 2) Section 4(3) of the Act exempts ancient monuments protected under the AMASR Act, 1958. 3) The Bhojshala complex was declared a protected monument after 1991. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: The Act freezes religious character as on 15 August 1947, and s.4(3)(a) exempts AMASR-protected ancient monuments. Bhojshala was protected long before 1991 (an ASI monument since the early 20th century), so 3 is wrong.

questions.question: Consider the following statements: 1) Raja Bhoj ruled during 1010–1055 CE. 2) He established Bhojshala as a centre of Sanskrit learning. 3) The Chandel dynasty was associated with the Bhojshala complex. 4) Goddess Vagdevi is another name for Goddess Saraswati. Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Paramara king Bhoja (c. 1010–1055 CE) founded Bhojshala as a centre of Sanskrit learning, and Vagdevi is Saraswati. The Chandelas were not linked to it.

questions.question: Who is known as the "Father of the Archaeological Survey of India"?
questions.explanation: Alexander Cunningham, first Director-General of the ASI (1861), is called the Father of the ASI.

questions.question: Consider the following statements about Constitutional provisions related to religious and cultural rights: 1)  Article 25 gives every religious denomination the right to manage its own affairs in matters of religion. 2)  Article 26 guarantees all persons the freedom of conscience and the right to freely profess, practice, and propagate religion. 3)  Article 29 provides that any section of citizens having a distinct language, script, or culture shall have the right to conserve the same. 4)  Article 30 confers upon all minorities the right to establish and administer educational institutions of their choice. Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements 1 and 2 swap Articles 25 and 26. Art. 29(1) protects language, script and culture, and Art. 30 gives all minorities (religious or linguistic) the right to run educational institutions.

questions.question: Which of the following international organizations or states are actively collaborating with the Artemis II launch payload framework via secondary CubeSat integration? 1) Germany 2) South Korea 3) Saudi Arabia 4) Argentina Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.explanation: Artemis II carried international CubeSats from Germany (TACHELES), South Korea (K-RadCube), Saudi Arabia and Argentina (ATENEA).

questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding NASA’s Artemis II mission: 1) It is designed as a crewed lunar landing mission targeting the volatile South Pole-Aitken Basin. 2)  The spacecraft utilizes a free-return trajectory, leveraging lunar gravity to slingshot back to Earth without requiring main engine burns for the return turn. 3)  It marks the first operational deployment of the Laser Communications (O2O) system to stream high- bandwidth 4K video from deep space. Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Artemis II is a crewed lunar flyby on a free-return trajectory, not a landing. It also flew the Orion Optical Communications System (O2O) laser link for high-rate video.

questions.question: Which technical term defines an orbital path that uses a celestial body's gravity to naturally "slingshot" a spacecraft back to Earth without requiring primary engine burns?
questions.explanation: A free-return trajectory uses the Moon's gravity to swing the spacecraft back to Earth without a major engine burn.

questions.question: With reference to the crew profile of the Artemis II lunar mission, which of the following pairs is/are correctly matched? 1) Victor Glover: First person of color to navigate beyond low-Earth orbit. 2) Christina Koch: First woman to walk on the lunar surface during this mission. 3) Jeremy Hansen: Canadian Space Agency (CSA) astronaut and the first non-American to leave Earth's orbit. Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.explanation: Glover is the first person of colour, Koch the first woman and Hansen (CSA) the first non-American to travel beyond low Earth orbit. Artemis II does not land, so no one walks on the Moon and pair 2 is wrong.

questions.question: Which of the following biological research experiments onboard the Artemis II mission utilizes advanced "organ-on-a-chip" technology with the crew's own cells to study the real-time cellular effects of deep-space radiation and microgravity?
questions.explanation: AVATAR (A Virtual Astronaut Tissue Analog Response) uses organ-chips made from the crew's own cells to study deep-space effects.

sources.title: NASA: AVATAR experiment on Artemis II

questions.question: Which of the following spacecraft made history as the first to achieve a survivable soft landing on the Moon, proving that the lunar surface was solid enough to support a vehicle rather than being a thick layer of dust? Options:
questions.explanation: The Soviet Luna 9 (February 1966) made the first soft landing on the Moon, showing the surface could support a lander. Surveyor 1 followed in June 1966.

questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding India's Ramsar Sites: 1) Every Ramsar Site in India is notified under the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972. 2) A Ramsar Site may overlap with a National Park or Wildlife Sanctuary. 3) Ramsar designation automatically grants legal protection under international law enforceable against the State. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Not every Ramsar site is notified under the Wildlife (Protection) Act. Ramsar sites can overlap national parks or sanctuaries. Ramsar listing creates treaty obligations but does not by itself give legal protection enforceable against the State.

questions.question: The "Montreux Record" under the Ramsar Convention is associated with:
options: Wetlands facing ecological changes or threats
Wetlands designated as UNESCO World Heritage Sites
Wetlands located in transboundary river basins
questions.explanation: The Montreux Record lists Ramsar sites where ecological change has happened, is happening or is likely.

questions.question: Which one of the following pairs is incorrectly matched?
questions.explanation: Sasthamkotta Lake is in Kerala (Kollam), not Tamil Nadu. The other pairs are correct.

questions.question: Consider the following: 1) Ramsar Convention 2) Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD) 3) Convention on Migratory Species (CMS) Which of the above may have direct relevance to the conservation of migratory birds using Indian wetlands?
questions.explanation: All three apply: Ramsar protects wetland habitat, the CBD covers biodiversity broadly, and the CMS deals with migratory species (including the Central Asian Flyway).

sources.title: Wikipedia: Convention on the Conservation of Migratory Species

questions.question: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
options: The Convention on Wetlands was adopted in 1971 in the Iranian city of Ramsar.
Chilika Lake (Odisha) and Keoladeo National Park (Rajasthan) were the first Indian wetlands to be designated as Ramsar Sites.
Uttar Pradesh has emerged as the state with the highest number of Ramsar Sites in India.
Jai Prakash Narayan Bird Sanctuary was recently designated as India's 100th Ramsar Site is in U.P.
questions.explanation: Tamil Nadu, not Uttar Pradesh, has the most Ramsar sites. The other statements are true: Ramsar 1971; Chilika and Keoladeo first designated in 1981; JP Narayan Bird Sanctuary (Surha Tal, UP) is the 100th site.

sources.title: Onmanorama: JP Narayan Bird Sanctuary becomes 100th Ramsar site (13th in UP)

questions.question: The Supreme Court noted that a mandatory leave decree could trigger covert hiring biases against women. Which constitutional article guarantees equality of opportunity in public employment and prohibits state discrimination based on sex?
questions.explanation: Article 16 guarantees equal opportunity in public employment and bars discrimination on grounds including sex.

questions.question: Which Indian state pioneered this policy over three decades ago by introducing a regular two-day monthly menstrual leave option for female employees in its government departments?
questions.explanation: Bihar has given female government employees two days of menstrual leave a month since 1992.

questions.question: Under the Maternity Benefit Act, 1961, a woman with less than two surviving children is entitled to a maximum of:
questions.explanation: Since the 2017 amendment, a woman with fewer than two surviving children gets up to 26 weeks of paid maternity leave.

questions.question: The type of judicial order used by the SC to monitor compliance is called:
questions.explanation: Under a continuing mandamus the Supreme Court keeps a case open and monitors compliance over time.

sources.title: Vineet Narain v. Union of India (1998)

questions.question: In the context of the PIL discussed in the passage, which constitutional doctrine prevents courts from taking over the core functions of the Legislature or the Executive?
questions.explanation: Separation of powers stops courts from doing the legislature's or executive's core policy work, such as framing leave policy.

questions.question: Which constitutional list under the Seventh Schedule houses the subject of "Labor", allowing both the Parliament and State Legislatures to enact laws regarding industrial disputes and welfare?
questions.explanation: Trade unions, industrial disputes and labour welfare are in the Concurrent List (Entries 22–24, List III).

sources.title: Constitution of India, Seventh Schedule List III

questions.question: Under the updated labor rules, what is the new employee threshold above which a factory must seek prior government approval before ordering layoffs, retrenchments, or closure?
questions.explanation: The Industrial Relations Code, 2020 raised the threshold for prior permission for layoff, retrenchment or closure from 100 to 300 workers.

questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding the Right to Strike in India: 1. The right to strike is a fundamental right under Article 19 of the Constitution. 2. It was first given limited recognition under the Trade Unions Act, 1926. 3. India is a founding member of the International Labour Organization. Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Striking is not a fundamental right (All India Bank Employees' Assn., 1962; T.K. Rangarajan, 2003). The Trade Unions Act, 1926 gave strikes limited recognition through immunities. India is a founding member of the ILO (1919).

sources.title: T.K. Rangarajan v. Govt of Tamil Nadu (2003)

questions.question: According to the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947, a temporary halt to manufacturing forced by an employer due to a labor deadlock or dispute is legally defined as what?
questions.explanation: Under s.2(l) of the ID Act a lockout is an employer closing the workplace or suspending work.

questions.question: With reference to the Code on Social Security, 2020, which of the following statements best describes the legal status accorded to "gig workers" in India?
options: It categorizes them as formal employees under the platforms, guaranteeing them absolute parity with traditional workers regarding all statutory labor rights.
It recognizes them for targeted welfare schemes but denies them formal employee status, thereby restricting their access to core statutory labor rights.
It mandates that all digital aggregators must provide permanent employment contracts and guarantee fixed minimum monthly wages to every registered platform worker.
It deliberately excludes gig and platform workers from the legislative framework entirely to prioritize and accelerate the financial growth of the startup ecosystem.
questions.explanation: The Code on Social Security, 2020 recognises gig and platform workers for welfare schemes but does not treat them as employees with full labour rights.

questions.question: The Central Government of India consolidated 29 central labor laws into four distinct codes to simplify the regulatory framework. Which of the following is NOT one of these four labor codes?
questions.explanation: The four codes cover Wages, Industrial Relations, Social Security, and Occupational Safety, Health & Working Conditions. There is no Vocational Training code.

questions.question: To accurately reflect post-pandemic structural shifts, MoSPI officially updated the base year for India's national accounts from 2011–12 to which newer financial year?
questions.explanation: In February 2026 MoSPI moved the national accounts base year from 2011–12 to 2022–23.

sources.title: ThePrint: New GDP series projects 7.6% growth in FY26

questions.question: Which advanced statistical method is introduced in the new series to calculate real GVA for manufacturing, requiring input costs and final output values to be deflated using separate, specific price indices?
questions.explanation: Double deflation deflates outputs and inputs with separate price indices to get real GVA.

questions.question: The passage mentions that the new series integrates the ASUSE dataset to better capture informal economic activity. What does the acronym ASUSE stand for?
options: Annual Survey of Unincorporated Sector Enterprises
Automated System for Urban Services and Employment
All-India Survey on Utilitarian Service Sector Earnings
Associated Statistical Unit for Small Scale Entrepreneurs
questions.explanation: ASUSE is NSO's Annual Survey of Unincorporated Sector Enterprises.

questions.question: Which specialized office under MoSPI is directly responsible for processing industrial, household, and price data to compile and release the annual and quarterly National Accounts?
questions.explanation: The National Statistical Office (MoSPI) compiles and releases the national accounts.

questions.question: In May 2026, Nepal sent an official diplomatic protest to both New Delhi and Beijing objecting to the route of which annual pilgrimage?
questions.explanation: Nepal protested the Kailash Mansarovar Yatra route through Lipulekh.

questions.question: Which specific high-altitude mountain pass serves as the primary flashpoint for this recent diplomatic dispute?
questions.explanation: Lipulekh Pass, at the India–Nepal–China tri-junction, is the flashpoint.

questions.question: In which Indian state is the base district (Pithoragarh) and the strategic road leading to this disputed pass located?
questions.explanation: Pithoragarh district and the road to Lipulekh are in Uttarakhand.

questions.question: Under international law, when a boundary river gradually and naturally changes its course over decades (as seen in Susta), the legal process altering the land borders is termed what?
questions.explanation: Accretion is a gradual, natural shift of a river's course, which moves the boundary with it. Avulsion is a sudden shift, which leaves the boundary where it was.

questions.question: Which historic 1816 treaty forms the legal baseline for both nations' claims, despite their disagreement over the exact origin of the boundary river?
questions.explanation: The Treaty of Sugauli (1815–16) is the legal basis for both sides' claims about the Kali river boundary.

questions.question: Five Indian states share an international land border with Nepal. Which of the following represents the correct geographical arrangement of these states from East to West?
options: Sikkim, West Bengal, Bihar, Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand
West Bengal, Sikkim, Bihar, Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand
Sikkim, Bihar, West Bengal, Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand
Uttarakhand, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, West Bengal, Sikkim
questions.explanation: From east to west: Sikkim, West Bengal, Bihar, Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand.

questions.question: The provisions of the Panchayats (Extension to Scheduled Areas) Act, 1996 (PESA) extend to areas identified under which constitutional provision?
questions.explanation: PESA covers Fifth Schedule Scheduled Areas. Sixth Schedule areas have Autonomous District Councils instead.

questions.question: Consider the following statements regarding PESA: 1. It was enacted to extend Part IX of the Constitution to Scheduled Areas. 2. It recognizes the Gram Sabha as a significant institution of self-governance. 3. It applies uniformly to all tribal areas in India. Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: PESA extends Part IX to Scheduled Areas and puts the Gram Sabha at its centre. It does not apply to all tribal areas; Sixth Schedule and other areas are outside it.

questions.question: Which of the following states contains areas governed by the Sixth Schedule of the Constitution?
questions.explanation: The Sixth Schedule covers tribal areas in Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram. Of the options, only Meghalaya qualifies.

questions.question: Which constitutional provision provides for the administration of Scheduled Areas and Tribal Areas?
questions.explanation: Article 244 provides for administering Scheduled Areas (Fifth Schedule) and Tribal Areas (Sixth Schedule).

questions.question: Consider the following: 1. Ownership of minor forest produce. 2. Consultation before land acquisition. 3. Management of community resources. Which of the above subjects are associated with powers recognized under PESA?
questions.explanation: PESA gives Gram Sabhas/Panchayats ownership of minor forest produce, consultation before land acquisition and management of community resources.

questions.question: The concerns discussed in the passage are most closely associated with which constitutional principle?
questions.explanation: The passage is about community participation through Gram Sabhas, which is decentralised self-governance.

questions.question: The CHIPS and Science Act, frequently discussed in the context of US–China technological competition, was enacted by:
questions.explanation: The CHIPS and Science Act (2022) is a US law.

questions.question: Which American company received a major boost through China's initial order of 200 aircraft?
questions.explanation: The 200-aircraft Chinese order was for Boeing, the US commercial aircraft maker.

questions.question: Taiwan is officially governed under the Constitution of the:
questions.explanation: Taiwan is governed under the Constitution of the Republic of China (1947).

sources.title: Wikipedia: Constitution of the Republic of China

questions.question: Which of the following ports is frequently viewed as India's strategic gateway to Afghanistan and Central Asia?
questions.explanation: Chabahar in Iran is India's gateway to Afghanistan and Central Asia.

questions.question: India's proposed response of strengthening ties with countries such as France, Germany, Sweden, Japan, and Australia most directly reflects which foreign-policy strategy?
questions.explanation: Diversifying partnerships with several middle powers to manage uncertainty from both the US and China is strategic hedging.

questions.question: Consider the following statements: 1. The First Battle of Panipat was fought in present-day Haryana. 2. The battle marked the end of the Delhi Sultanate under the Lodis. 3. Babur had originally established his rule in Kabul before invading India. Which statements are correct?
questions.explanation: All three are true. Panipat is in Haryana, Ibrahim Lodi's defeat ended the Delhi Sultanate, and Babur ruled Kabul from 1504 before invading India.

questions.question: Which military formation employed by Babur involved dividing the army into mobile flanking units?
questions.explanation: Tulughma split the army into units that wheeled around to attack the enemy's flanks and rear.

questions.question: The concerns discussed in the passage regarding "state formation" are most closely related to which of the following?
options: Creation and consolidation of political authority
questions.explanation: State formation means creating and consolidating political authority.

questions.question: Consider the following statements: 1. The First Battle of Panipat was fought in 1526. 2. The battle immediately brought the entire Indian subcontinent under Mughal control. 3. After Panipat, Babur faced Rana Sanga of Mewar in the Battle of Khanwa (1527) Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Panipat (1526) did not give Babur the whole subcontinent. He went on to fight Rana Sanga at Khanwa (1527).

questions.question: The passage highlights the role of military technology in historical change. Which military innovation is most closely associated with the battle being commemorated?
questions.explanation: Babur's use of gunpowder artillery and matchlocks was decisive at Panipat.

questions.question: The battle discussed in the passage is often compared with Which battle is commonly regarded as another turning point in Indian political history?
questions.explanation: Plassey (1757), which led to British political dominance, is the battle most often paired with Panipat (1526) as a turning point in Indian political history.

questions.question: The concerns regarding transparency and accountability discussed in the passage are most closely associated with which constitutional principle?
questions.explanation: Transparency, reasoned decisions and accountability in AI-assisted governance come from the rule of law.

questions.question: Which company launched the AI model "Gemini," which has been discussed extensively in debates regarding AI competition?
questions.explanation: Google (Google DeepMind) developed Gemini.

questions.question: India's National Data & Analytics Platform (NDAP) is primarily intended to:
options: Integrate datasets from multiple government agencies and improve data accessibility
questions.explanation: NITI Aayog's NDAP brings government datasets from many agencies onto one accessible platform.

questions.question: The issues discussed regarding cross-border coordination on AI are most similar to governance challenges encountered in:
questions.explanation: AI governance, like climate change, is a transboundary problem that needs international coordination.

questions.question: Consider the following statements: 1. BODH is associated with benchmarking AI models in healthcare. 2. BODH operates within the broader digital-health ecosystem created by ABDM. 3. BODH is India's AI regulator. Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: BODH is a platform for benchmarking health-AI models within the Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission ecosystem. It is not India's AI regulator.

sources.title: NHA/ABDM: BODH health AI benchmarking platform

questions.question: Consider the following statements: 1. BHASHINI seeks to address linguistic barriers in digital access. 2. The objective of BHASHINI is consistent with the constitutional value of equality. 3. BHASHINI is primarily a cybersecurity framework. Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: BHASHINI tackles language barriers to digital access, which supports equality. It is a language-technology mission, not a cybersecurity framework.

questions.question: Consider the following: 1. Artificial Intelligence 2. Quantum Computing 3. Advanced Defence Systems The strategic significance of semiconductors arises because they are critical to:
questions.explanation: Semiconductors are critical to AI, quantum computing and defence systems.

questions.question: Which of the following best explains why semiconductors are often described as "strategic technologies"?
options: They are used only for military applications.
They are essential inputs for both civilian and national-security sectors.
They are produced exclusively by governments.
Their use is restricted by international law.
questions.explanation: They are strategic because both civilian and national-security sectors depend on them.

questions.question: The concerns discussed in the passage regarding technological self-reliance are most closely linked to which contemporary policy objective?
questions.explanation: Technological self-reliance in chips serves India's strategic autonomy.

questions.question: Which of the following companies is widely regarded as the world's leading contract semiconductor manufacturer?
questions.explanation: TSMC (Taiwan) is the world's largest contract chipmaker (foundry).

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT one of the five pillars identified in NITI Aayog’s semiconductor roadmap?
questions.explanation: NITI Aayog's semiconductor roadmap pillars cover people/talent, partnerships, policy and investment, infrastructure and R&D. 'Agricultural electronics' is not one of them.

questions.question: Under Article 249 of the Constitution, the Rajya Sabha can empower Parliament to legislate on a matter in the State List if the resolution is passed by:
options: Simple majority of members present and voting
Absolute majority of the total membership
Two-thirds of members present and voting
questions.explanation: Under Art. 249 the Rajya Sabha must pass the resolution by two-thirds of members present and voting.

questions.question: Which Constitutional Amendment lowered the voting age from 21 to 18 years for elections in India?
questions.explanation: The 61st Amendment Act, 1988 (in force 1989) lowered the voting age from 21 to 18.

questions.question: Why does Uttar Pradesh have the highest representation in the Rajya Sabha?
options: Equal representation is provided to all states
Representation is broadly linked to population
questions.explanation: Fourth Schedule seat allocation roughly follows population, so Uttar Pradesh has the most seats (31).

questions.question: Which Article of the Constitution deals with the composition of the Rajya Sabha?
questions.explanation: Article 80 deals with the composition of the Council of States.

questions.question: Which of the following is the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha?
questions.explanation: The Vice-President is ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha (Art. 64).

questions.question: The system of "open ballot" in Rajya Sabha elections was introduced primarily to:
questions.explanation: The 2003 amendment to the RP Act brought in open ballot, where party MLAs show their vote to the party agent, to curb cross-voting.

sources.title: Kuldip Nayar v. Union of India (2006)

questions.question: Myanmar's strategic importance to India arises most directly because it:
options: Serves as India's only land bridge to ASEAN
Hosts India's largest overseas military base
Controls India's maritime access to the Persian Gulf
questions.explanation: Myanmar is the only ASEAN country with a land border with India, making it India's land bridge to ASEAN.

questions.question: The China–Myanmar Economic Corridor (CMEC) forms a part of:
questions.explanation: CMEC is part of China's Belt and Road Initiative.

questions.question: The "Golden Triangle" is notorious primarily for:
questions.explanation: The Golden Triangle (Myanmar–Laos–Thailand) is known for opium and methamphetamine production and trafficking.

questions.question: Which Indian states have been most directly affected by refugee inflows from Myanmar ?
questions.explanation: Mizoram and Manipur have taken in the largest numbers of refugees since the 2021 coup.

questions.question: Which military exercise is conducted jointly by India and Myanmar?
questions.explanation: IMBEX is the India–Myanmar bilateral army exercise. Yudh Abhyas is with the US, Garuda Shakti with Indonesia and SIMBEX with Singapore.

questions.question: The Supreme Court created a new compensation category called:
questions.explanation: In Shishu Pal v. Surjeet (11 June 2026) the Supreme Court created a new head of compensation called 'loss of domestic care'.

sources.title: Verdictum: Shishu Pal v. Surjeet, 2026 INSC 634

questions.question: The minimum notional monthly income fixed by the Supreme Court for homemakers is:
questions.explanation: A homemaker's notional income was set at a minimum of ₹30,000 a month, rising 10% every three years.

sources.title: Business Standard: SC puts economic value on homemakers' work

questions.question: The Supreme Court described homemakers as:
questions.explanation: The Court called homemakers 'nation builders, not dependents'.

questions.question: Which Article of the Constitution guarantees equality before the law?
questions.explanation: Article 14 guarantees equality before the law and equal protection of the laws.

questions.question: Which economic indicator is often criticised for excluding unpaid domestic labour from its calculations?
questions.explanation: GDP leaves out unpaid household and care work.

questions.question: The judgment arose from a compensation dispute under which legislation?
questions.explanation: It was a motor accident compensation claim under the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988.

sources.title: Outlook Money: SC values homemakers' work at Rs 30,000 a month in accident compensation case

questions.question: Dr. Ambedkar served as the Chairman of:
options: Drafting Committee of the Constituent Assembly
questions.explanation: Ambedkar chaired the Drafting Committee of the Constituent Assembly (1947).

questions.question: Ambedkar's famous address, later published as a book, was titled:
questions.explanation: 'Annihilation of Caste' (1936) was Ambedkar's undelivered address, later published.

questions.question: Which of the following organisations was founded by Dr. Ambedkar in 1924?
questions.explanation: Ambedkar founded the Bahishkrit Hitakarini Sabha in 1924. The ILP (1936), SCF (1942) and RPI (1957) came later.

questions.question: The Mahad Satyagraha was primarily associated with access to:
questions.explanation: The Mahad Satyagraha (1927) asserted Dalits' right to draw water from the public Chavdar tank.

questions.question: Which Fundamental Right directly abolishes untouchability?
questions.explanation: Article 17 abolishes untouchability.

questions.question: Under the National Quantum Mission, India recently demonstrated a quantum communication network spanning approximately:
questions.explanation: In April 2026 India validated a 1,000-km terrestrial quantum communication (QKD) network under the NQM, built with QNu Labs.

sources.title: Business Standard: National Quantum Mission achieves 1,000-km milestone

questions.question: The breakthrough discussed in the passage would most likely strengthen India's position in which of the following domains?
questions.explanation: Quantum-secure communication strengthens cyber and strategic security.

questions.question: Which of the following sectors is expected to benefit most directly from quantum communication? 1. Defence 2. Financial Systems 3. Critical Infrastructure
questions.explanation: Defence, financial systems and critical infrastructure all need tamper-proof communication.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT one of the primary verticals of the National Quantum Mission?
questions.explanation: The NQM's verticals (thematic hubs) are computing, communication, sensing & metrology, and materials & devices. Quantum biotechnology is not one of them.

questions.question: Which government department is the nodal agency for implementing the National Quantum Mission?
questions.explanation: The Department of Science and Technology is the nodal department for the NQM.

questions.question: The 'Malabar' naval exercise, mentioned as a key multilateral engagement, involves the navies of India, USA, Japan, and:
questions.explanation: Malabar now involves the Quad navies: India, the US, Japan and Australia (Australia rejoined in 2020).

questions.question: The "2+2 Ministerial Dialogue" between India and the USA involves which set of Ministers?
options: External Affairs Minister and Defence Minister
Home Minister and National Security Advisor
questions.explanation: The India–US 2+2 dialogue brings together the External Affairs and Defence Ministers of India with the US Secretaries of State and Defense.

questions.question: In a significant escalation of geopolitical tensions, the United States recently launched airstrikes targeting infrastructure in which South American oil-producing nation?
questions.explanation: US military strikes in 2025–26 targeted Venezuela, an oil-producing country.

questions.question: Trump’s latest warning of higher tariffs on India is linked primarily to which issue?
options: India’s FDI rules for US companies
questions.explanation: Trump's tariff threats against India were tied mainly to its imports of Russian oil.

sources.title: Wikipedia: Tariffs in the second Trump administration

questions.question: India’s interest in Chabahar Port is primarily to create a transport corridor to Afghanistan and Central Asia, bypassing which country?
questions.explanation: Chabahar gives India access to Afghanistan and Central Asia without going through Pakistan.

questions.question: The passage references India's participation in the 'SCO' as a point of contention. Which of the following countries is NOT a member of the Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO)?
questions.explanation: Japan is not an SCO member. Pakistan, Russia and Iran are.

questions.question: Who characterised India's macroeconomic situation as a "rare Goldilocks phase"?
options: Chief Economic Advisor V. Anantha Nageswaran
questions.explanation: RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra described a 'rare Goldilocks period' of high growth and low inflation when announcing a rate cut.

questions.question: Which tool involves the purchase and sale of government securities to regulate money supply?
questions.explanation: Open Market Operations are RBI purchases and sales of government securities to manage liquidity.

questions.question: Who serves as the ex-officio Chairperson of the Monetary Policy Committee (MPC)?
questions.explanation: The RBI Governor is ex-officio Chairperson of the six-member MPC (s.45ZB, RBI Act).

questions.question: Who is the current Governor of the Reserve Bank of India (RBI), who recently led the MPC in cutting the repo rate to 5.25%?
questions.explanation: Sanjay Malhotra (Governor since December 2024) led the MPC when it cut the repo rate to 5.25%.

questions.question: The term "Goldilocks" in economics, applied by RBI to India, metaphorically means the economy is:
options: Just right, like baby bear's porridge
questions.explanation: A 'Goldilocks' economy is 'just right': neither overheating nor too cold.

questions.question: Under India’s Flexible Inflation Targeting framework, the RBI is statutorily mandated to keep CPI inflation within:
questions.explanation: The target is 4% CPI inflation within a 2–6% band (s.45ZA, RBI Act), retained for 2026–31.

sources.title: Business Today: Govt retains inflation target at 4% with 2–6% band

questions.question: The first African country to host the G20 summit is:
questions.explanation: South Africa hosted the first G20 summit in Africa (Johannesburg, November 2025).

questions.question: The summit theme is best captured by which set of words?
questions.explanation: The theme was 'Solidarity, Equality, Sustainability'.

questions.question: Which African philosophy explicitly guided the G20 Declaration?
questions.explanation: The declaration was framed around the African philosophy of Ubuntu.

questions.question: Which country will host the G20 Summit in 2026, immediately after South Africa?
questions.explanation: The United States holds the 2026 G20 presidency.

questions.question: The summit set specific targets regarding gender equality in the workforce. What is the specific target mentioned for female labour force participation?
options: Reduce the gender gap by 30% by 2030.
questions.explanation: The declaration endorsed the revised Brisbane–eThekwini Goal of cutting the gender gap in labour force participation by 25% by 2030.

sources.title: G20 Research Group: Labour & Employment Ministers' declaration 2025

questions.question: The G20 was originally established in 1999 primarily in response to:
questions.explanation: The G20 was created in 1999 as a finance ministers' forum after the 1997–98 Asian Financial Crisis.

questions.question: Which unexpected incident occurred on November 20, disrupting the proceedings of the COP 30 summit?
options: A massive cyber-attack on the venue's servers.
A fire at the main venue.
A flash flood in the city of Belém.
A walkout by the G7 nations.
questions.explanation: On 20 November 2025 a fire broke out in the Blue Zone of the COP30 venue in Belém, forcing an evacuation.

sources.title: Wikipedia: 2025 United Nations Climate Change Conference

questions.question: Who led the Indian delegation at COP30?
questions.explanation: Union Environment Minister Bhupender Yadav led India's delegation at COP30.

questions.question: In the context of India’s statement at the summit, the demand for "equity and climate justice" most likely refers to which principle of International Environmental Law?
options: The Precautionary Principle, which mandates that lack of scientific certainty should not postpone measures to prevent degradation.
The Polluter Pays Principle, which implies that the private entities causing the fire at the venue must pay for the damages.
Common But Differentiated Responsibilities (CBDR), emphasizing that developed countries have a greater historical obligation to provide finance.
The Doctrine of Public Trust, which asserts that the government holds natural resources in trust for the benefit of the public.
questions.explanation: 'Equity and climate justice' refers to Common But Differentiated Responsibilities: developed countries' historical emissions mean they should provide finance and technology.

questions.question: According to the section on "India’s NDC Commitments," which specific target was highlighted as having been "achieved early"?
questions.explanation: India's target of 50% installed power capacity from non-fossil sources (meant for 2030) was reached in 2025, five years early.

sources.title: PIB: India achieves 50% non-fossil installed capacity (2025)

questions.question: The "Global Mutirão Agreement" was a key outcome of the summit. What does the term "Mutirão" signify in this context?
questions.explanation: 'Mutirão' is a Brazilian Portuguese word for a collective, community effort.

sources.title: Wikipedia: 2025 United Nations Climate Change Conference

questions.question: India has secured the rights to host the Centenary Commonwealth Games in 2030. Which city has been selected as the host?
questions.explanation: Ahmedabad (Amdavad) was approved in November 2025 as host of the 2030 Centenary Commonwealth Games.

questions.question: The 2030 Games are referred to as the "Centenary Commonwealth Games" because they mark 100 years since the first edition. Where was the first Commonwealth Games held in 1930?
questions.explanation: The first Games (British Empire Games) were held in Hamilton, Canada in 1930.

questions.question: Regarding India's history at the Commonwealth Games, which of the following statements is true about the 2010 New Delhi Games?
options: India finished 1st overall in the medal tally.
India finished 2nd overall in the medal tally.
It was India's second-best performance after Birmingham 2022.
questions.explanation: At Delhi 2010 India finished 2nd overall with 101 medals (38 gold), its best ever.

sources.title: Wikipedia: India at the 2010 Commonwealth Games

questions.question: By securing the Centenary Commonwealth Games 2030, India has achieved a rare distinction in Commonwealth sport history. Which of the following statements most accurately reflects this distinction?
options: India becomes the first Asian nation to host the Games twice
India becomes the first former colony to host the Centenary edition
India becomes the only nation after Australia and Canada to host both the Olympics and Commonwealth Games
India becomes the first developing nation to host the Games in consecutive decades
questions.explanation: With Delhi 2010 and Ahmedabad 2030, India becomes the first Asian country to host the Commonwealth Games twice (Malaysia hosted once, in 1998). India has never hosted the Olympics, so (c) is false.

questions.question: The theme of the first-ever G20 Summit held on African soil was:
questions.explanation: South Africa's 2025 presidency, which held the first G20 summit in Africa (Johannesburg, Nov 2025), used the theme 'Solidarity, Equality, Sustainability'.

questions.question: The emphasis on “Ubuntu” in the G20 2025 Declaration primarily reflects which of the following ideas?
options: Promoting cultural pluralism and respecting local traditions globally
Interconnectedness and shared humanity in multilateral cooperation
Encouraging economic self-reliance among developing countries
Strengthening decentralisation of global governance institutions
questions.explanation: Ubuntu ('I am because we are') expresses interconnectedness and shared humanity, the idea behind South Africa's G20 message.

questions.question: Which of the following countries is not a member of the G20?
questions.explanation: The UAE is often a guest country but not a G20 member. Argentina, Indonesia and Saudi Arabia are members.

questions.question: During 2025 G20 Presidency, which of the following correctly represents the Troika members?
questions.explanation: The troika is the previous, current and next presidencies. In 2025 that was Brazil (2024), South Africa (2025) and the United States (2026).

questions.question: Which of the following is the latest entity to join the G20 as a permanent member?
questions.explanation: The African Union became a permanent member at the New Delhi summit in September 2023. The EU was already a member.

questions.question: Which of the following correctly pairs a G20 initiative with its primary objective?
options: Open Satellite Data Partnership — Global internet governance
Critical Minerals Circularity Initiative — Recycling and innovation in mineral supply chains
Global Healthcare Response Team — Universal health insurance coverage
Countering Drug Terror Nexus — Financial inclusion in conflict zones
questions.explanation: India proposed a G20 Critical Minerals Circularity Initiative for recycling, urban mining and innovation in mineral supply chains. The other pairings mismatch their objectives.

sources.title: PIB: PM's remarks at G20 Johannesburg Summit (Nov 2025)

questions.question: Which team did India defeat in the final to win the 2025 Women’s World Cup?
questions.explanation: India beat South Africa by 52 runs in the final (Navi Mumbai, 2 Nov 2025) to win their first Women's ODI World Cup.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct regarding the start of Cricket World Cups?
options: Men’s World Cup started before the Women’s World Cup
Women’s World Cup started before the Men’s World Cup
Both started in the same year
Women’s World Cup started in 1980, Men’s in 1975
questions.explanation: The first Women's World Cup was held in England in 1973, two years before the first men's World Cup (1975).

questions.question: Which country has won the most ICC Women’s Cricket World Cup titles?
questions.explanation: Australia has won the Women's World Cup a record seven times.

questions.question: Who took the sensational catch to seal India’s victory in the 2025 final?
questions.explanation: Captain Harmanpreet Kaur took the final catch, dismissing Nadine de Klerk off Deepti Sharma's bowling.

sources.title: Wikipedia: 2025 Women's Cricket World Cup final

questions.question: What was the previous name of the biggest stadium in the world, the Narendra Modi Stadium?
questions.explanation: The Narendra Modi Stadium (Motera, Ahmedabad) was earlier called Sardar Patel Stadium.

questions.question: Which specific existing trade route does India aim to bypass through the implementation of IMEC?
questions.explanation: IMEC's rail and sea route through the Gulf, Israel and the Mediterranean is meant to offer an alternative to the Suez Canal route.

questions.question: Which of the following concerns is most frequently associated with China’s Belt and Road Initiative (BRI)?
options: Excessive focus on digital connectivity over physical infrastructure
Creation of debt vulnerabilities due to opaque financing
Absence of strategic objectives beyond trade facilitation
questions.explanation: The BRI is most often criticised for 'debt-trap' risks from opaque lending (e.g. Hambantota).

questions.question: The passage mentions “Minilateralism.” In International Relations, what does this term refer to?
options: A cooperation approach where a small, like-minded group of countries works together to solve a specific issue
A cooperation approach where two countries create a formal bilateral pact to manage a shared issue
A cooperation approach where all or most countries participate through a large multilateral framework to set global rules
A foreign-policy approach where small countries limits external engagement and avoids commitments to other states
questions.explanation: Minilateralism means a small group of like-minded states cooperating on a specific issue (e.g. the Quad or I2U2).

questions.question: The acronym 'IMEC' mentioned in the above passage stands for:
questions.explanation: IMEC is the India–Middle East–Europe Economic Corridor, announced at the 2023 G20 in New Delhi.

questions.question: India, Iran, and Afghanistan signed a tripartite agreement to develop which terminal at Chabahar Port?
questions.explanation: The 2016 India–Iran–Afghanistan trilateral agreement concerns the Shahid Beheshti terminal at Chabahar.

questions.question: The passage mentions the 'Five Eyes' intelligence alliance. Which of the following countries is NOT a member of the Five Eyes?
questions.explanation: The Five Eyes are the US, UK, Canada, Australia and New Zealand. France is not a member.

questions.question: The statement refers to the "Vienna Convention on Diplomatic Relations." In which year was this critical international treaty adopted?
questions.explanation: The Vienna Convention on Diplomatic Relations was adopted in 1961.

sources.title: Wikipedia: Vienna Convention on Diplomatic Relations

questions.question: The capital city of Canada, where the Indian High Commission is located, is:
questions.explanation: Ottawa is Canada's capital.

questions.question: The passage mentions 'OCI' cardholders. Which of the following rights is NOT granted to an Overseas Citizen of India (OCI)?
options: Multiple entry, multi-purpose life-long visa for visiting India
Right to vote in Indian General Elections
Exemption from reporting to police authorities for any length of stay
Parity with NRIs in financial, economic, and educational fields
questions.explanation: OCI cardholders cannot vote in Indian elections. They get a lifelong multiple-entry visa, exemption from police reporting and parity with NRIs in certain matters.

questions.question: The border between the United States and Canada is the longest international border in the world. It is largely defined by which parallel of latitude?
questions.explanation: West of the Great Lakes, the US–Canada border largely follows the 49th parallel.

questions.question: Which incident in India–Canada relations involved a Japanese steamship carrying Indian immigrants being denied entry into Vancouver in 1914?
questions.explanation: The Komagata Maru, a Japanese steamship, was refused entry at Vancouver in 1914.

questions.question: From a strategic and administrative perspective, Pahalgam falls under which broader region?
questions.explanation: Pahalgam is in Anantnag district, in the Kashmir Valley.

questions.question: Which among the following countries is not a member of BIMSTEC?
questions.explanation: BIMSTEC's members are Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Myanmar, Nepal, Sri Lanka and Thailand. Pakistan is not a member.

questions.question: In diplomatic terminology, a “Demarche” refers to:
options: A formal request to reduce tariffs through trade negotiations
A formal diplomatic representation or protest conveyed to another government
A covert intelligence operation carried out without official acknowledgement
A formal treaty or agreement for sharing river waters between countries
questions.explanation: A démarche is a formal diplomatic representation or protest made to another government.

questions.question: Which of the following rivers flows from India into Pakistan?
questions.explanation: The Ravi rises in Himachal Pradesh and flows into Pakistan. The Ganga, Yamuna and Godavari stay in India.

questions.question: The term “Non-Aligned Movement (NAM)” primarily refers to:
options: A collective security arrangement formed during the Cold War era
A multilateral economic grouping promoting South–South cooperation
A coalition of states avoiding formal alignment with major power blocs
A diplomatic mechanism operating under the United Nations framework
questions.explanation: NAM is a grouping of states that chose not to align formally with either Cold War power bloc.
